explanation: The mucosa of stomach has gastric glands. Gastric glands have three major types of cells namely - (i) mucous neck cells which secrete mucus; (ii) peptic or chief cells which secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen; an (iii) parietal or oxyntic cells which secrete HCl and intrinsic factor (factor essential for absorption of vitamin B₁₂). (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 262; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food
option_b: Peptic or chief cells,Secrete the proenzyme pepsinogen
option_c: Parietal or oxyntic cells,Secrete HCl and intrinsic factor

question: The food mixes thoroughly with the acidic gastric juice of the stomach by the churning movements of its muscular wall and is called the ____.
explanation: The stomach stores the food for 4-5 hours. The food mixes thoroughly with the acidic gastric juice of the stomach by the churning movements of its muscular wall and is called the chyme. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 262; Paragraph No. 3)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food

question: The proenzyme pepsinogen,on exposure to _______ gets converted into the active enzyme pepsin.
explanation: The proenzyme pepsinogen, on exposure to hydrochloric acid, gets converted into the active enzyme pepsin, the proteolytic enzyme of the stomach. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 262; Paragraph No. 3)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food

question: Which is incorrect about pepsin?
answer: Pepsin is activated on exposure of pepsinogen to Nitric acid
explanation:
The proenzyme pepsinogen, on exposure to hydrochloric acid, gets converted into the active enzyme pepsin, the proteolytic enzyme of the stomach. Pepsin converts proteins
into proteoses and peptones (peptides). The mucus and bicarbonates present in gastric juice play an important role in lubrication and protection of the mucosal epithelium from excoriation by highly concentrated hydrochloric acid. HCl provides the acidic pH (pH 1.8) optimal for pepsins. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 262; Paragraph No. 3)

question: Various movements of which layer of alimentary canal help in a thorough mixing up of the food with various secretions in the intestine

question: _______juice contains a variety of enzymes like disaccharidases (e.g., maltase), dipeptidases, lipases, nucleosidases
explanation: Intestinal juice contains a variety of enzymes like disaccharidases (e.g., maltase), dipeptidases, lipases, nucleosidases, etc. The mucus along with the bicarbonates from the pancreas protects the intestinal mucosa from acid as well as provides an alkaline medium (pH 7.8) for enzymatic activities. question:
Functions of large intestine

(i)Absorption of some water, minerals and certain drugs 

(ii) Secretion of mucus which helps in adhering the waste (undigested) particles together and lubricating it for an easy passage 

(iii)Secretion of enzymes amylase 

(iv)Secretion of enzyme pepsin
explanation:
No significant digestive activity occurs in the large intestine. The
functions of the large intestine are:
(i) absorption of some water, minerals and certain drugs;
(ii) secretion of mucus which helps in adhering the waste (undigested)
particles together and lubricate it for easy passage.
The undigested, unabsorbed substances called faeces enter the caecum
of the large intestine through the ileocecal valve, which prevents the backflow of
the faecal matter. It is temporarily stored in the rectum till defecation. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 264; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food

question:
The activities of the gastrointestinal tract are under the control of? 
(i)Neural control 
(ii)Hormonal control 
(iii)Respiration 
(iv)Vascular
explanation: The activities of the gastrointestinal tract are under neural and hormonal control for proper coordination of different parts. The sight, smell and/or the presence of food in the oral cavity can stimulate the secretion of saliva. Gastric and intestinal secretions are also, similarly, stimulated by neural signals. The muscular activities of different parts of the alimentary canal can also be moderated by neural mechanisms, both local and through CNS. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 264; Paragraph No. 3)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food

(ii)Intestinal mucosa

question: Saliva acts as an antibacterial agent due to the presence of
explanation: Saliva is composed of a variety of electrolytes, Lysozyme which is an antibacterial agent and includes sodium, potassiumum, calcium, magnesium, bicarbonate, and phosphates. Also found in saliva are immunoglobulins, proteins, enzymes, mucins, and nitrogenous products, such as urea and ammonia. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 262; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food

question: Peristalsis is
explanation: Peristalsis is a series of wavelike muscle contractions that moves food to different processing stations in the digestive tract. The process of peristalsis begins in the oesophagus when a bolus of food is swallowed. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 261; Paragraph No. 3)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food

question: The peristalsis helps in movement of bolus in the oesophagus. The process is______
explanation: Peristalsis is an involuntary process. But swallowing is a voluntary process. Mucus in saliva helps in lubricating and adhering the masticated food particles into a bolus. The bolus is then conveyed into the pharynx and then into the oesophagus by swallowing or deglutition. The bolus further passes down through the oesophagus by successive waves of muscular contractions called peristalsis. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 262; Paragraph No. 4)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food

question: Bilirubin and biliverdin are
explanation: The two most important bile pigments are bilirubin, which is orange or yellow, and its oxidized form biliverdin, which is green. Mixed with the intestinal contents, they give a brown colour to the faeces. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 262; Paragraph No. 4)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food

question: Match the following

question:
Choose the statement that are not correct 

(i) The process of digestion is accomplished by mechanical and chemical processes. 

(ii)The buccal cavity performs two major functions, mastication of food and facilitation of swallowing. 

(iii)The teeth with the help of HCl masticate and mix up the food thoroughly. 

(iv) Mucus in saliva helps in lubricating and adhering the masticated food particles into a bolus.
explanation: The process of digestion is accomplished by mechanical and chemical processes. The buccal cavity performs two major functions, mastication of food and facilitation of swallowing. (iii)The gastro-oesophageal sphincter controls the passage of food into the stomach.

question:

(iii) Lysozyme present in saliva acts as an antibacterial agent that prevents infections.

question:
Choose the correct statement 

(i)The final steps in digestion occurs far away from the mucosal epithelial cells of the intestine.

(ii)The breakdown of biomacromolecules mentioned above occurs in the region before the jejunum of the small intestine.

(iii)The simple substances thus formed are absorbed in the jejunum and ileum regions of the small intestine.

(iv) The undigested and unabsorbed substances are stored in the large intestine and never excreted.
explanation:
The final steps in digestion occur very close to the mucosal epithelial cells of the intestine.
Dipeptides gets converted in to Amino acids through action of Dipeptidases. 
Maltose gets converted in to two molecules of Glucose through action of Maltase
Lactose gets converted in to Glucose + Galactose through action of Lactase
Sucrose gets converted in to Glucose+ Fructose through action of Sucrase                                     
Di and Monoglycerides gets converted in to Fatty acids + Glycerol through action of  Lipases. 
The breakdown of biomacromolecules mentioned above occurs in the duodenum (region preceding the jejunum)region of the small intestine. The simple substances thus formed are absorbed in the jejunum and ileum regions of the small intestine. The undigested and unabsorbed substances are passed on to the large intestine. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 263; Paragraph No. 5,6)
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Digestion  and  Absorption >> Digestion of food

question:
Choose the correct statement

(i)Absorption is the process by which the end products of digestion pass through the intestinal mucosa into the blood or lymph. 

(ii)Transport of water depends upon the osmotic gradient. 

(iii)Small amounts of disaccharides like glucose, amino acids and some electrolytes like chloride ions are generally absorbed by simple diffusion. 

(iv)Active transport occurs against the concentration gradient
explanation: Absorption is the process by which the end products of digestion pass through the intestinal mucosa into the blood or lymph. It is carried out by passive, active or facilitated transport mechanisms. Small amounts of monosaccharides like glucose, and amino acids and some electrolytes like chloride ions are generally absorbed by simple diffusion. The passage of these substances into the blood depends upon the concentration gradients. However, some substances like glucose and amino acids are absorbed with the help of carrier proteins. This mechanism is called facilitated transport. The transport of water depends upon the osmotic gradient. Active transport occurs against the concentration gradient and hence requires energy. Various nutrients like amino acids, monosaccharides like glucose, and electrolytes like Na+ are absorbed into the blood by this mechanism. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 264; Paragraph No. 4)

question: Which of the following terms describes human dentition?[NEET 2018]

Reason : Lipases can break large fat droplets into smaller ones.
 [2011]
answer: Both the Assertion and Reason are incorrect
explanation: It is not lipases but the bile salts which are responsible for the emulsification of fats. Bile salts are steroids secreted by the liver in the bile. In the intestinal lumen, they reduce the surface tension of fat droplets, causing their breakdown into many smaller ones. A stable fine emulsion of fat is thereby formed. question: Find the incorrect statements about contaminants like nitrates and phosphates?
answer: They cause enrichment of aquatic plantys and in turn improve aquatic life
explanation: The prime contaminants are nitrates and phosphates, which act as plant nutrients. They overstimulate the growth of algae, causing unsightly scum and unpleasant odours, and robbing the water of dissolved O₂ vital to other aquatic life. At the same time, other pollutants flowing into a lake may poison whole populations of fish, whose decomposing remains further deplete the water’s dissolved O₂ content. In such fashion, a lake can literally choke to death.

question: A lake which is rich in organic waste may result in (NEET 2016)
answer: Mortality of fish due to lack of oxygen

(NEET 2015)

question:
Eutrophication of water bodies leading to killing of fishes is mainly due to non-availability of 
(NEET 2015)
explanation: Eutrophication is the excessive growth of algae, plants and animals in water bodies due to the nutrient enrichment particularly with nitrogen and phosphate. Nutrients present in sewage, agricultural wastes and fertilisers cause dense growth of plants and plaktonic algae. The excessive growth of plaktonic algae that cause colouration of water is called algal bloom, which is toxic to animals and humans. Eutrophic water bodies also support excessive growth of floating plants. Algal blooms and floating plants cut off light from submerged plants, resulting in their death. There is drastic decrease in O₂ replenishment inside water. Non availability of O₂ results in death of aquatic plants and animals such as fish, which further adds to organic loading of water. Decomposition is replaced by putrefraction which is anaerobic, leading to absence of O₂ in water and death of aquatic animals.

question: Select the correct option regarding Domestic Waste and industrial effluents
answer: A few toxic substances, often present in industrial waste waters, can undergo Biomagnification in the aquatic food chain
explanation:
Sewage from our homes as well as from hospitals are likely to contain many undesirable pathogenic microorganisms, and its disposal into a water without proper treatment may cause outbreak of serious diseases, such as, dysentery, typhoid, jaundice, cholera, etc. Unlike domestic sewage, waste water from industries like petroleum, paper manufacturing, metal extraction and processing, chemical manufacturing, etc., often contain toxic substances, notably, heavy metals (defined as elements with density > 5 g/cm3 such as mercury, cadmium, copper, lead, etc.) and a variety of organic compounds.
A few toxic substances, often present in industrial waste waters, can undergo biological magnification (Biomagnification) in the aquatic food chain. Biomagnification refers to increase in concentration of the toxicant at successive trophic levels. This happens because a toxic substance accumulated by an organism cannot be metabolised or excreted, and is thus passed on to the next higher trophic level. This phenomenon is wellknown for mercury and DDT. NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 16, Page 276

question: Select the correct option regarding Domestic Waste and industrial effluents
answer: In accelerated eutrophication, the natural aging of a lake may be accelerated by pollutants from man’s activities like effluents from the industries and homes.
explanation: Eutrophication is the natural aging of a lake by nutrient enrichment of its water. In a young lake the water is cold and clear, supporting little life. With time, streams draining into the lake introduce nutrients such as nitrogen and phosphorus, which encourage the growth of aquatic organisms. As the lake’s fertility increases, plant and animal life burgeons, and organic remains begin to be deposited on the lake bottom. Over the centuries, as silt and organic debris pile up, the lake grows shallower and warmer, with warm-water organisms supplanting those that thrive in a cold environment. Marsh plants take root in the shallows and begin to fill in the original lake basin. Eventually, the lake gives way to large masses of floating plants (bog), finally converting into land. Depending on climate, size of the lake and other factors, the natural aging of a lake may span thousands of years. However, pollutants from man’s activities like effluents from the industries and homes can radically accelerate the aging process. This phenomenon has been called Cultural or Accelerated Eutrophication. During the past century, lakes in many parts of the earth have been severely eutrophied by sewage and agricultural and industrial wastes. The prime contaminants are nitrates and phosphates, which act as plant nutrients. They overstimulate the growth of algae, causing unsightly scum and unpleasant odours, and robbing the water of dissolved O₂ vital to other aquatic life. At the same time, other pollutants flowing into a lake may poison whole populations of fish, whose decomposing remains further deplete the water’s dissolved O₂ content. In such fashion, a lake can literally choke to death. Heated (thermal) wastewaters flowing out of electricity-generating units, e.g., thermal power plants, constitute another important category of pollutants. Thermal waste water eliminates or reduces the number of organisms sensitive to high temperature, and may enhance the growth of plants and fish in extremely cold areas but, only after causing damage to the indigenous flora and fauna. NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 16, Page 276 and 277

question: Which of the following is correct regarding integrated waste management
answer: The cleaning occurs in two stages incliuding  the conventional sedimentation, filtering and chlorine treatments first and six connected marshes over 60 hectares of marshland with biological agents that assimilate the heavy pollutants
explanation:
Wastewater including sewage can be treated in an integrated manner, by utilising a mix of artificial and natural processes. An example of such an initiative is the town of Arcata, situated along the Northern coast of California. Collaborating with biologists from the Humboldt
State University, the townspeople created an integrated waste water treatment process within a natural system. The cleaning occurs in two stages – (a) the conventional sedimentation, filtering and chlorine treatments are given. After this stage, lots of dangerous pollutants like dissolved heavy metals still remain. To combat this, an innovative approach was taken and (b) the biologists developed a series of six connected marshes over 60 hectares of marshland. Appropriate plants, algae, fungi and bacteria were seeded into this area, which neutralise, absorb and assimilate the pollutants. Hence, as the water flows through the marshes, it gets purified naturally.The marshes also constitute a sanctuary, with a high level of biodiversity in the form of fishes, animals and birds that now reside there.
A citizens group called Friends of the Arcata Marsh (FOAM) are responsible for the upkeep and safeguarding of this wonderful project.NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 16, Page 276 and 277

Recycling is the only solution for the treatment of e-waste, provided it is carried out in an environment friendly manner.

Radiation, that is given off by nuclear waste is extremely damaging to organisms, because it causes mutations at a very high rate. The degradation of natural resources can occur, not just by the action of pollutants but also by improper resource utilisation practices.
Soil erosion and desertification: The development of the fertile top-soil takes centuries. explanation:
The Bishnoi community is known for its peaceful co-existence with nature. The effort to cut down trees by the kings was thwarted by the Bishnois. A Bishnoi woman Amrita Devi showed exemplary courage by hugging a tree and daring king’s men to cut her first before cutting the tree. The tree mattered much more to her than her own life. question: Which of the following is correct regarding People's Participation in Prevention of deforestation
answer: In 1974, local women showed enormous bravery in protecting trees from the axe of contractors by hugging them as a part of the Chipko Movement
explanation:
The Government of India has recently instituted the Amrita Devi Bishnoi Wildlife Protection Award for individuals or communities from rural areas that have shown extraordinary courage and dedication in protecting wildlife(fauna).
You may have heard of the Chipko Movement of Garhwal Himalayas. In 1974, local women showed enormous bravery in protecting trees from the axe of contractors by hugging them. People all over the world have acclaimed the Chipko movement. Realising the significance of participation by local communities, the Government of India in 1980s has introduced the concept of Joint Forest Management (JFM) so as to work closely with the local communities for protecting and managing forests. In return for their services to the forest, the communities get benefit of various forest products (e.g., fruits, gum, rubber, medicine, etc.), and thus the forest can be conserved in a sustainable manner. 
Reference:NCERT Class 12 Biology, Chapter 16, Page 285

Hepatitis-B, Genital herpes and HIV infections are uncurable STIs. Except for hepatitis-B, genital herpes and HIV infections,other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated

question:
Which of the following statements are correct ? 
 (A) Reproductive health refers to total well-being in 
all aspects of reproduction. 
 (B) Amniocentesis is legally banned for sex 
determination in India. 
 (C) "Saheli" – a new oral contraceptive for females 
was developed in collaboration with ICMR (New Delhi). 
 (D) Amniocentesis is used to determine genetic 
disorders and survivability of foetus. 
 Choose the most appropriate answer from the 
options given below :
explanation:
Statement 1 is correct. Reproductive health refers to the total well-being and optimal functioning of all aspects related to reproduction, including physical, emotional, social, and behavioral aspects.

Statement 2 is incorrect. Amniocentesis, a prenatal diagnostic procedure, is not legally banned for sex determination in India. However, it is regulated and allowed only for certain specific medical indications and not for sex determination purposes.

Statement 3 is incorrect. "Saheli" is not a new oral contraceptive developed in collaboration with ICMR (Indian Council of Medical Research) in New Delhi. It is an oral contraceptive pill developed by Hindustan Latex Limited, a public sector undertaking in India.

Statement 4 is correct. Amniocentesis is a prenatal diagnostic procedure used to determine genetic disorders and certain chromosomal abnormalities in the fetus. It involves the sampling of amniotic fluid surrounding the fetus for analysis. It can also provide information about the survivability of the fetus in certain cases.
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Previous Year Questions 2

question:
Given below are two statements :  Statement I :-
 Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is another 
specialised procedure of in-vivo fertilisation. 
Statement II :-
 Infertility cases due to inability of the male partner to inseminate female can be corrected by artificial insemination (AI). 
 In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below: [ NEET 2023(Phase 2)]
answer: (2) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
explanation:
Statement I is incorrect, but statement II is true.

Statement I: Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is another specialized procedure of in-vivo fertilization. This statement is incorrect. Intra Cytoplasmic Sperm Injection (ICSI) is not a procedure of in-vivo fertilization. It is an assisted reproductive technology (ART) technique used in cases of severe male infertility. During ICSI, a single sperm is directly injected into an egg to achieve fertilization in vitro (outside the body).

Statement II: Infertility cases due to inability of the male partner to inseminate female can be corrected by artificial insemination (AI). This statement is true. Artificial insemination (AI) is a technique used to treat infertility, specifically in cases where the male partner is unable to inseminate the female partner naturally. It involves the introduction of sperm into the reproductive tract of the female through artificial means, such as by placing prepared sperm into the cervix, uterus, or fallopian tubes. AI can be performed using the partner's sperm (artificial insemination by husband, AIH) or donor sperm (artificial insemination by donor, AID).

Therefore, the correct answer is that statement I is incorrect, but statement II is true.
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Previous Year Questions 2
option_a: (2) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
option_b:
(1) Statement I is correct but statement II is 
false
option_c: (3) Both Statement I and Statement II are true
option_d: (4) Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

question:
Consider the statements regarding reproductive health. Choose the correct option.

 1. The term simply refers to healthy reproductive organs with normal functions.

 2. It also includes the emotional and social aspects of reproduction.

 3. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), reproductive health means total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, i.e., physical, emotional, psychological, and social.

 4. Behavioral well-being is also an important aspect of reproductive health.
explanation: The term simply refers to healthy reproductive organs with normal functions. However, it has a broader perspective and includes the emotional and social aspects of reproduction also. According to the World Health Organisation (WHO), reproductive health means total well-being in all aspects of reproduction, i.e., physical, emotional, behavioural and social. So, it is behavioural, not psychological.  (NCERT Biology class12: Page no: 57, Paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the statements regarding reproductive health. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. India was amongst the first countries in the world to initiate action plans and programmes at a National level to attain total reproductive health. 

 2. A society with people having physically and functionally normal reproductive organs and normal emotional and behavioural interactions among them in all sex-related aspects might be called reproductively healthy.

 3. The programmes called ‘Family planning’ was initiated in 1961. 

 4. India wants to attain total reproductive health as a national goal just to eradicate STDs.
explanation: India was amongst the first countries in the world to initiate action plans and programmes at a national level to attain total reproductive health as a social goal. It is not a national goal but a social goal. These programmes called ‘family planning’ were initiated in 1951 and not 1961. (NCERT biology class12: Page no: 57, Paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the statements regarding the reproductive health programme. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. Programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas are currently in operation under the popular name ‘Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes’.

 2. RCH programme includes creating awareness among people about various reproduction-related aspects and providing facilities and support for building up a reproductively healthy society. 

 3. Spreading information about contraception is an important task of the RCH programme. 
 
4. Family planning programmes are replaced by RCH programmes.
explanation: These programmes called ‘family planning’ were initiated in 1951 and were periodically assessed over the past decades. Improved programmes covering wider reproduction-related areas are currently in operation under the popular name ‘Reproductive and Child Health Care (RCH) programmes’. Creating awareness among people about various reproduction-related aspects and providing facilities and support for building up a reproductively healthy society are the major tasks under these programmes. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12: page no 58, Paragraph no 1)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the statements regarding the reproductive health programme. Choose the correct option. 

 1. RCH stands for Reproductive and Community health care. 

 2. In the RCH programme with the help of audio-visual and print-media governmental and non-governmental agencies have taken various steps to create awareness among the people about reproduction-related aspects.

 3. Parents, other close relatives, teachers and friends, also have a major role in the dissemination of the information related to reproductive health.

 4. Introduction of sex education in schools should be encouraged to provide the right information to the young.
explanation: RCH stands for Reproductive and child health care. Through RCH programmes, with the help of audio-visual and print-media governmental and non-governmental agencies have taken various steps to create awareness among the people about reproduction-related aspects. Parents, other close relatives, teachers and friends, also have a major role in the dissemination of the above information. The introduction of sex education in schools should also be encouraged to provide the right information to the young to discourage children from believing in myths and having misconceptions about sex-related aspects. (NCERT biology class 12; Page no 58, Paragraph no 2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the statements regarding spreading information related to reproductive health. Choose the correct option.

 1. Proper information about reproductive organs, adolescence and related changes, safe and hygienic sexual practices, sexually transmitted diseases (STD), AIDS, etc., would help people, especially those in the adolescent age group to lead a reproductively healthy life.

 2. Educating people, especially fertile couples and those in the marriageable age group, about available birth control options, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care of the mother and child, the importance of breastfeeding, equal opportunities for the male and the female child, etc., would address the importance of bringing up socially conscious healthy families of the desired size.

 3. Introduction of sex education in schools should not be encouraged as it provides a lot more information than needed. 

 4. Awareness of problems due to uncontrolled population growth, social evils like sex abuse and sex-related crimes, etc., need to be created to enable people to think and take up necessary steps to prevent them and thereby build up a socially responsible and healthy society.
explanation: The introduction of sex education in schools should also be encouraged to provide the right information to the young to discourage children from believing in myths and having misconceptions about sex-related aspects. Proper information about reproductive organs, adolescence and related changes, safe and hygienic sexual practices, sexually transmitted diseases (STD), AIDS, etc., would help people, especially those in the adolescent age group to lead a reproductively healthy life. Educating people, especially fertile couples and those in the marriageable age group, about available birth control options, care of pregnant mothers, post-natal care of the mother and child, the importance of breastfeeding, equal opportunities for the male and the female child, etc., would address the importance of bringing up socially conscious healthy families of the desired size. Awareness of problems due to uncontrolled population growth, social evils like sex abuse and sex-related crimes, etc., need to be created to enable people to think and take up necessary steps to prevent them and thereby build up a socially responsible and healthy society. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 58,  paragraph  no 2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the statements regarding the implementation of RCH programmes. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. Implementation of better techniques and new strategies from time to time are also required to provide more efficient care and assistance to people.

2. Proper implementation is essential to provide medical assistance and care to people with reproduction-related problems like pregnancy, delivery, STDs, abortions, contraception, menstrual problems, infertility,

3. Successful implementation of various action plans to attain reproductive health requires strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support.

4. Statutory ban on amniocentesis shows a negative impact and must be amended.
explanation: Successful implementation of various action plans to attain reproductive health requires strong infrastructural facilities, professional expertise and material support. These are essential to provide medical assistance and care to people with reproduction-related problems like pregnancy, delivery, STDs, abortions, contraception, menstrual problems, infertility, etc. Implementation of better techniques and new strategies from time to time are also required to provide more efficient care and assistance to people. Statutory ban on amniocentesis for sex-determination to legally check the increasing menace of female foeticides, massive child immunisation, etc., are some programmes that merit mention in this connection of successful implementation. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 58,  paragraph  no 3)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the statements regarding indicators of a Reproductive health-wise healthy society. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. Increased number of medically assisted deliveries and better post-natal care leading to decreased maternal and infant mortality rates.

 2. Better awareness about sex-related matters.

 3. Decreased medical facilities for all sex-related problems.

 4. Decreased number of couples with small families.
explanation: Better awareness about sex-related matters, increased number of medically assisted deliveries and better post-natal care lead to decreased maternal and infant mortality rates, increased number of couples with small families, better detection and cure of STDs and overall increased medical facilities for all sex-related problems, etc. all indicate improved reproductive health of the society. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 59,  paragraph  no 1)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the statements regarding population growth. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. Increased health facilities along with better living conditions had an explosive impact on the growth of the population.

2. World population was around 2 billion (2000 million) in 1900 and about 6 billion by 2000 and 7.2 billion in 2011.

3. Indian population which was approximately 35.0 million at the time of our independence reached close to the billion mark by 2005 and crossed 1.2 billion in May 2011.
 
4. A rapid decline in birth rate, maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR) as well as an increase in several people of reproducible age are probable reasons for tremendous population growth.
explanation: Increased health facilities along with better living conditions had an explosive impact on the growth of the population. The world population which was around 2 billion (2000 million) in 1900 rocketed to about 6 billion by 2000 and 7.2 billion in 2011. A similar trend was observed in India too. Our population which was approximately 350 million at the time of our independence reached close to the billion mark by 2000 not 2005 and crossed 1.2 billion in May 2011. A rapid decline in death rate, (not in birth rate), maternal mortality rate (MMR) and infant mortality rate (IMR) as well as an increase in the number of people of reproducible age are probable reasons for the population explosion. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 59,  paragraph  no 2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the statements regarding population control. Choose the correct option.

1. The most important step to overcome this problem is to motivate smaller families by using various contraceptive methods.

2. Statutory raising of marriageable age of the female to 18 years and that of males to 21 years is of no use.  

3. Incentives given to couples with big families can also help in population control. 

4. Many couples, mostly the young, urban, working ones have even adopted a ‘one child norm.
explanation: The most important step to overcome this problem of population growth is to motivate smaller families by using various contraceptive methods. You might have seen advertisements in the media as well as posters/bills, etc., showing a happy couple with two children with the slogan Hum Do Hamare Do (we two, our two). Many couples, mostly the young, urban, working ones have even adopted a ‘one child norm. Statutory raising of marriageable age of the female to 18 years and that of males to 21 years, and incentives given to couples with small families (Not big) are two of the other measures taken to tackle this problem. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 59,  paragraph  no 3)

question:
Consider the statements regarding contraceptive methods. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperm meeting.

 2. In barrier methods, ovum and sperms are prevented from physically meeting with the help of barriers.

 3. Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs). These devices are inserted by doctors or expert nurses into the uterus through Fallopian tubes.

 4. Oral contraceptives are used in the form of tablets and hence are popularly called pills.
explanation: Natural methods work on the principle of avoiding chances of ovum and sperm meeting. In barrier methods, ovum and sperms are prevented from physically meeting with the help of barriers. Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs). These devices are inserted by doctors or expert nurses in the uterus through Vagina (not the fallopian tube). Oral contraceptives are used in the form of tablets and hence are popularly called pills. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 60-61, section 4.2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the statements regarding natural methods of contraception. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. Periodic abstinence is one such method in which the couples avoid or abstain from coitus from day 5 to 14. 

 2. Lactational dysmenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition.

 3. Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is another method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation.

 4. Absence of menstruation after parturition is an effective method for only up to 12 months.
explanation: Periodic abstinence is one such method in which the couples avoid or abstain from coitus from day 10 to 17 of the menstrual cycle when ovulation could be expected. As chances of fertilisation are very high during this period, it is called the fertile period. Therefore, by abstaining from coitus during this period, conception could be prevented. Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is another method in which the male partner withdraws his penis from the vagina just before ejaculation to avoid insemination. The lactational amenorrhea (absence of menstruation) method is based on the fact that ovulation and therefore the cycle does not occur during the period of intense lactation following parturition. Therefore, as long as the mother breastfeeds the child fully, the chances of conception are almost nil. However, this method has been reported to be effective only up to a maximum period of six months following parturition. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 60,  paragraph  no 1)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the statements regarding barrier methods of contraception. Choose the CORRECT option. 

 1. Barrier methods are available for only males (condoms). 

 2. ‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of condoms for males.

 3. Use of condoms has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting UTIs and AIDS.

 4. In barrier methods, ovum and sperms are prevented from physically meeting with the help of barriers.
explanation: In barrier methods, ovum and sperms are prevented from physically meeting with the help of barriers. Such methods are available for both males and females. ‘Nirodh’ is a popular brand of condoms for males. The use of condoms has increased in recent years due to its additional benefit of protecting the user from contracting STIs and AIDS. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 60,  paragraph  no 2)

question:
Consider the statements regarding types of barrier methods. Choose the CORRECT option.

1. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are also barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus.

2. Condoms are barriers made of spandex sheath that is used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract.

3. Spermicidal creams, jellies, and foams are usually used along with other methods to increase their contraceptive efficiency. 

4. Cervical caps are not reusable.
explanation: Condoms are barriers made of thin rubber/ latex sheath that is used to cover the penis in the male or vagina and cervix in the female, just before coitus so that the ejaculated semen would not enter into the female reproductive tract. Diaphragms, cervical caps and vaults are also barriers made of rubber that are inserted into the female reproductive tract to cover the cervix during coitus. They prevent conception by blocking the entry of sperms through the cervix. They are reusable. Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used along with these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 60,  paragraph  no 2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the statements regarding IUDs. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. The Intra Uterine Devices are presently available as the non-medicated IUDs (e.g., Lippes loop), copper-releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 275) and the hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20).

2. IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus and the Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms.

3. The hormone-releasing IUDs, make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms.

4. IUDs are inserted by doctors or expert nurses in the uterus through the cervix.
explanation: A popular method of contraception is the use of Intra Uterine Devices (IUDs). These devices are inserted by doctors or expert nurses into the uterus through the vagina (Cervix is the opening of the uterus. So, anything going into the uterus has to pass through the cervix. The path is the vagina the cervix then the uterus.). These Intra Uterine Devices are presently available as the non-medicated IUDs (e.g., Lippes loop), copper-releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) and the hormone-releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20). IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperms within the uterus and the Cu ions released suppress sperm motility and the fertilising capacity of sperms. The hormone-releasing IUDs, in addition, make the uterus unsuitable for implantation and the cervix hostile to the sperms. IUDs are ideal contraceptives for females who want to delay pregnancy and/or space children. It is one of the most widely accepted methods of contraception in India. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 60, paragraph  no 3)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the statements regarding oral contraceptives. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. They inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent/retard entry of sperms.

2. Pills have to be taken daily for 28 days starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle.

3. Saheli–the new oral contraceptive for females contains a non-steroidal preparation. It is a ‘once-a-month pill
 
4. Oral administration of small doses of either progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations is another contraceptive method used by females.
explanation: Oral administration of small doses of either progestogens or progestogen–estrogen combinations is another contraceptive method used by females. They are used in the form of tablets and hence are popularly called pills. Pills have to be taken daily for 21 days starting preferably within the first five days of the menstrual cycle. After a gap of 7 days (during which menstruation occurs) it has to be repeated in the same pattern till the female desires to prevent conception. They inhibit ovulation and implantation as well as alter the quality of cervical mucus to prevent/retard entry of sperms. Pills are very effective with lesser side effects and are well accepted by females. Saheli–the new oral contraceptive for females contains a non-steroidal preparation. It is a ‘once-a-week pill. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 61, paragraph  no 2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the statements regarding MTP. Choose the correct option. 

1. Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term is called medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) or induced abortion.

2. MTPs are considered relatively safe during the second trimester, i.e., up to 24 weeks of pregnancy.

3. MTP is legal when the continuation of the pregnancy would involve a risk to the life of the pregnant woman or of grave injury to physical or mental health.

4. MTP should not be performed when there is a substantial risk that if the child were born, would suffer from such physical or mental abnormalities as to be seriously handicapped.
explanation: Intentional or voluntary termination of pregnancy before full term is called medical termination of pregnancy (MTP) or induced abortion. The government of India legalised MTP in 1971 with some strict conditions to avoid its misuse. MTPs should be performed when the continuation of the pregnancy would involve a risk to the life of the pregnant woman or of grave injury to physical or mental health or when there is a substantial risk that the child born, would suffer from such physical or mental abnormalities as to be seriously handicapped. MTPs are considered relatively safe during the first trimester, i.e., up to 12 weeks of pregnancy. Second-trimester abortions are much riskier. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 62, section 4.2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the statements regarding STIs. Choose the CORRECT option. 
 
1. Gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis-B, and AIDS are STIs

 2. Infections or diseases which are transmitted through sexual intercourse are collectively called sexually transmitted infections

 3. Some of these infections like hepatitis–B and HIV can also be transmitted by sharing injection needles, surgical instruments, sharing clothes etc., with infected persons, transfusion of blood, or from an infected mother to the foetus too.

 4. Except for Gonorrhoea, Syphilis, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely incurable.
explanation: Infections or diseases which are transmitted through sexual intercourse are collectively called sexually transmitted infections (STI) or venereal diseases (VD) or reproductive tract infections (RTI). Gonorrhoea, syphilis, genital herpes, chlamydiasis, genital warts, trichomoniasis, hepatitis B and of course, the most discussed infection in recent years, HIV leading to AIDS are some of the common STIs. Some of these infections like hepatitis–B and HIV can also be transmitted by sharing injection needles, surgical instruments, etc., with infected persons, transfusion of blood, or from an infected mother to the foetus too. Except for hepatitis B, genital herpes and HIV infections, other diseases are completely curable if detected early and treated properly. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 63,  paragraph  no 2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the statements regarding STIs. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. Early symptoms of most of the STIs are minor and include itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, blisters, swellings, etc.
 
2. Complications of STI include prolapse intervertebral disc (PID), abortions, still births, ectopic pregnancies, infertility or even cancer of the reproductive tract.
 
3. To avoid STIs avoid sex with unknown partners/multiple partners.

4. In case of doubt, one should go to a qualified doctor for early detection and get complete treatment if diagnosed with infection.
explanation: Early symptoms of most STIs are minor and include itching, fluid discharge, slight pain, swellings, etc (No blisters). Complications of STI include pelvic inflammatory diseases (PID), abortions, stillbirths, ectopic pregnancies, infertility or even cancer of the reproductive tract. To avoid STIs avoid sex with unknown partners/multiple partners. In case of doubt, one should go to a qualified doctor for early detection and get complete treatment if diagnosed with the infection. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 63, paragraph no 3)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the statements regarding Infertility. Choose the CORRECT option. 

1. Infertility means the inability to produce children despite unprotected sexual cohabitation. 

2. The reasons for infertility could be many–physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological or even psychological.

3. Specialised health care units (infertility clinics, etc.) could help in the diagnosis and corrective treatment of some of these disorders and enable these couples to have children.

4. The couples could be assisted to have children through certain special techniques commonly known as assisted reproductive technologies (ART).
explanation: Infertility means the inability to produce children inspite unprotected sexual cohabitation. The reasons for infertility could be many–physical, congenital, diseases, drugs, immunological or even psychological. Specialised health care units (infertility clinics, etc.) could help in the diagnosis and corrective treatment of some of these disorders and enable these couples to have children. The couples could be assisted to have children through certain special techniques commonly known as assisted reproductive technologies (ART). question:
Consider the statements regarding In vitro fertilisation. Choose the correct option. 
 
1. In vitro fertilisation (IVF–fertilisation outside the body in almost similar conditions as that in the body) followed by embryo transfer (ET) is one of such ART methods.

2. In this method, popularly known as the test tube baby programme, ova from the wife/donor (female) and sperms from the husband/donor (male) are collected and are induced to form zygotes under simulated conditions in the laboratory.

3. The zygote or early embryos (with more than 8 blastomeres) could then be transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT–zygote intrafallopian transfer) and embryos with less than 8 blastomeres, into the uterus (IUT – Intra uterine transfer),

4. Embryos formed by in-vivo fertilisation (fusion of gametes within the female) also could be used for such transfer to assist those females who cannot conceive.
explanation: In vitro fertilisation (IVF–fertilisation outside the body in almost similar conditions as that in the body) followed by embryo transfer (ET) is one such method. In this method, popularly known as the test tube baby programme, ova from the wife/donor (female) and sperms from the husband/donor (male) are collected and are induced to form zygotes under simulated conditions in the laboratory. The zygote or early embryos (with up to 8 blastomeres) could then be transferred into the fallopian tube (ZIFT–zygote intrafallopian transfer) and embryos with more than 8 blastomeres, into the uterus (IUT – Intra uterine transfer), to complete its further development. Embryos formed by in-vivo fertilisation (fusion of gametes within the female) also could be used for such transfer to assist those females who cannot conceive. (Reference   NCERT biology class 12; page no 64,  paragraph  no 2)
topic_name: Reproduction >> Reproductive Health >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the statements regarding artificial fertility methods. Choose the correct option. 

1. Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube (GIFT – gamete intrafallopian transfer) of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation

2. Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is another specialised procedure to form an embryo in the laboratory in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum.

3. Infertility cases either due to the inability of the female partner to inseminate the male or due to very low sperm counts in the ejaculates, could be corrected by Intra uterine semination technique.

4. In this technique, the semen collected either from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced either into the vagina or into the uterus of the female through natural insemination.
explanation: Transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube (GIFT – gamete intrafallopian transfer) of another female who cannot produce one, but can provide a suitable environment for fertilisation and further development is another method attempted. Intra cytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) is another specialised procedure to form an embryo in the laboratory in which a sperm is directly injected into the ovum. Infertility cases either due to the inability of the male partner to inseminate the female or due to very low sperm counts in the ejaculates could be corrected by the artificial insemination (AI) technique. In this technique, the semen collected either from the husband or a healthy donor is artificially introduced either into the vagina or into the uterus (IUI – intra-uterine insemination) of the female.

question:
Choose the correct statement with regards to external fertilisation.

i) A large number of gametes are produced to ensure the survival of offspring, by increasing the chances of syngamy

ii) A major disadvantage is that the offsprings are vulnerable to predators threatening their survival up to adulthood.

iii) External fertilisation occurs in bony fishes and frogs where a large number of offspring are produced.

iv) Organisms exhibiting external fertilisation show great synchrony between the sexes and release a large number of gametes into the surrounding medium in order to enhance the chances of syngamy.
explanation: Organisms exhibiting external fertilisation show great synchrony between the sexes and release a large number of gametes into the surrounding medium (water) in order to enhance the chances of syngamy. This happens in the bony fishes and frogs where a large number of offspring are produced. A major disadvantage is that the offspring are extremely vulnerable to predators threatening their survival up to adulthood.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12: page no:14, paragraph no:4)

question: Which one of the following generates new genetic combinations leading to variation? (2016)
explanation: Sexual reproduction involves formation and fusion of male and female gametes. Random fusion of these male and female gametes lead to the genetic variability in the offspring which although resemble their parents but also exhibit new traits of their own.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12: page no:8, paragraph no:5)

question: The PGRs can be broadly divided into ?
explanation: The PGRs can be broadly divided into two groups based on their functions in a living plant body. One group of PGRs are involved in growth promoting activities, such as cell division, cell enlargement, pattern formation, tropic growth, flowering, fruiting and seed formation. These are also called plant growth promoters, e.g., auxins, gibberellins and cytokinins. The PGRs of the other group play an important role in plant responses to wounds and stresses of biotic and abiotic origin. They are also involved in various growth inhibiting activities such as dormancy and abscission.
topic_name: Plant Physiology >> Plant Growth and Development >> Plant Growth Regulators Characteristics

question: With regards to photoperiodism, Choose the incorrect option

explanation: Photoperiodic induction : The photoperiod-regulated process that occurs in the leaves resulting in the transmission of floral stimulus to shoot apex is collectively as photoperiodic induction. Number of photoperiodic induction varies from plants to plants. i.e., duration of light and dark period. some plants require the exposure to light for a period exceeding a well defined critical duration, while others must be exposed to light for a period less than this critical duration before the flowering is initiated in them. The former group of plants are called long day plants while the latter ones are termed short day plants. The critical duration is different for different plants. There are many plants, however, where there is no such correlation between exposure to light duration and induction of flowering response; such plants are called day-neutral plants
topic_name: Plant Physiology >> Plant Growth and Development >> Photoperiodism
option_a: Day neutral plants require increased exposure to sunlight for flowering than Long day plants
option_b: It has been hypothesised that there is a hormonal substance(s) that is responsible for flowering that migrates from leaves to shoot apices for inducing flowering only when the plants are exposed to the necessary inductive photoperiod.
option_c: In response to perception of light/dark duration by the leaves, shoot apices modify themselves into flowering apices.
option_d: Some plants require the exposure to light for a period exceeding a well defined critical duration(called Long day plants), while others must be exposed to light for a period less than this critical duration before initiating flowering.

question:
Dr. F. Went noted that if coleoptile tips were removed and placed on agar for one hour, the agar would produce a bending when placed on one side of freshly-cut coleoptile stumps. Of what significance is this experiment?
[2014]
answer: It demonstrated polar movement of auxins
explanation:
Auxin was isolated by F.W. Went from tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings,Dr. F. Went noted that if coleoptile tips were removed and placed on agar for one hour, the agar would produce a bending when placed on one side of freshly-cut coleoptile stumps. It made possible the isolation and exact identification of auxin .Darwin and his son observed that the coleoptiles of canary grass responded to unilateral illumination by growing towards the light source. This is called phototropism. They performed series of experiments which concluded that the tip of coleoptile was the site of transmittable influence that caused the bending of the entire coleoptile. F.W. Went isolated auxin from the tips of coleoptiles of oat seedlings and concluded that phototropism of oat seedlings occur. They also concluded that phototropism in the tips of coleoptiles is due to the polar movement of auxin in the stem.
So, the correct answer is 'it demonstrated polar movements of auxins'
topic_name: Plant Physiology >> Plant Growth and Development >> Previous Year Questions 1

question:
Through their effects on plant growth regulators, what do the temperature and light control in the plants?
[Mains 2012]

Similarly, there are plants for which flowering is either quantitatively or qualitatively dependent on exposure to low temperature. This phenomenon is termed as vernalisation. It prevents precocious reproductive development late in the growing season and enables the plant to have sufficient time to reach maturity. Thus, many plants require a warm-cold-warm sequence to complete their annual cycle

question: How does pruning help in making the hedge dense?

question:

explanation: It is now known that not only the duration of light period but that the duration of dark period is also of equal importance. question:
Which of the following animals are ureotelic in nature?
 
i.Mammals        
ii.Marine fishes        
iii.Aquatic amphibians   
iv.Bony fishes
explanation: The process of excreting ammonia is Ammonotelism. Many bony fishes, aquatic amphibians and aquatic insects are ammonotelic in nature. Ammonia, as it is readily soluble, is generally excreted by diffusion across body surfaces or through gill surfaces (in fish) as ammonium ions. Kidneys do not play any significant role in its removal. Terrestrial adaptation necessitated the production of lesser toxic nitrogenous wastes like urea and uric acid for conservation of water. Mammals, many terrestrial amphibians and marine fishes mainly excrete urea and are called ureotelic animals. Ammonia produced by metabolism is converted into urea in the liver of these animals and released into the blood which is filtered and excreted out by the kidneys. Some amount of urea may be retained in the kidney matrix of some of these animals to maintain a desired osmolarity. Reptiles, birds, land snails and insects excrete nitrogenous wastes as uric acid in the form of pellet or paste with a minimum loss of water and are called uricotelic animals. iii) nerves
explanation: Hilum acts as entrance for ureter, blood vessels and nerves. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which structure is located inner to the hilum
explanation: Inner to the hilum is a broad funnel shaped space called the renal pelvis. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Renal pelvis has projections to its interior called ______.
explanation: Renal pelvis has projections to its interior called calyces. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: What is true about the kidney capsule(Outer / inner layer)
answer: The outer layer of kidney is a tough capsule
explanation: The outer layer of kidney is a tough capsule.Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System
option_a: The outer layer of kidney is a tough capsule

question:
The zones located inside the kidney are called? 
i. Outer cortex       
ii.  Middle lamella        
iii. Inner medulla        
iv. Outer lamella
explanation: Inside the kidney there are two zones an outer cortex and an inner medulla.. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Medulla is divided into a few conical masses called medullary _______
explanation: The medulla is divided into a few conical masses called medullary pyramids projecting into the calyces. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The gross structure of the kidney cortex extends as renal columns into the medulla through which structure
explanation: Cortex further extends in medullary pyramids. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The extension of cortex in medullary pyramids forms columns of _______
explanation: Cortex forms columns of bertini by extending into medullary pyramids. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The complex tubular structures of kidney are called
explanation: Each kidney has nearly one million complex tubular structures called nephrons. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following is the functional unit of kidney
explanation: Nephrons are the functional unit of kidney as the perform the waste filtration treatment. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following are the parts of nephron?
explanation: Each nephron has two parts that include the glomerulus and the renal tubule. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Glomerulus is a tuft of _______
explanation: Glomerulus is formed of of capillaries. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following capillary is present in glomerulus
explanation: Gomerulus contains afferent arteriole which is a fine branch of renal artery. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following capillary takes blood from glomerulus
explanation: Blood from the glomerulus is carried away by an efferent arteriole as indicated by its name "e" stands for exit of blood. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The double walled structure that encloses glomerulus is called
explanation: A double walled cup-like structure called Bowman’s capsule encloses the glomerulus. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 207
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: ______ starts with Bowman's capsule which covers the glomerulus.
explanation: Renal tubule starts with Bowman's capsule which covers the glomerulus. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Glomerulus coupled with bowman's capsule is called
explanation: Glomerulus along with Bowman’s capsule, is called the malpighian body or renal corpuscle. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The renal tubule continues further to form a highly coiled network called
explanation: The renal tubule continues further to form a highly coiled network called proximal convoluted tubule (PCT) Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: After bowman's capsule the next part of the renal tubule , that is a coiled network is called
explanation: The Bowman capsule leads to the proximal tubules, that ends up in the Loop of Henle and then into the distal tubule, and finally into the collecting duct Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following are the two limbs of henle's loop
explanation: Henle's loop consists of two limbs called ascending and descending limbs. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The coiled tubular region of the ascending limb is called
explanation: The ascending limb continues as another highly coiled tubular region called distal convoluted tubule (DCT). Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The DCTs of nephrons open into tubes called
explanation: The DCTs of many nephrons open into a straight tube called collecting duct. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The collecting ducts open into _______ through medullary pyramids in the calyces.
explanation: Colecting ducts converge and open into the renal pelvis through medullary pyramids in the calyces. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following structures of nephron  located in cortical region of kidney?
explanation: The Malpighian or renal corpuscle, PCT and DCT of the nephron are situated in the cortical region of the kidney. Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following structures are located in renal medulla
explanation: The loop of Henle dips into the renal medulla
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following are the characteristics of cortical nephron
explanation: In majority of nephrons, the loop of Henle is too short and extends only very little into the medulla and are called cortical nephrons, these are highly prevalent and present nephrons of kidney. Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System
option_c: Greater extension of loop in medulla

question: The nephrons with longer henle's loop are called
explanation: In some of the nephrons, the loop of Henle is very long and runs deep into the medulla. These nephrons are called juxta medullary nephrons. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The capillary network formed by efferent arterioles of glomerulus is called
explanation: The efferent arteriole emerging from the glomerulus forms a fine capillary network called the peritubular capillaries. Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following statements is/are true about vasa recta?
explanation: A minute vessel of the peritubular capillaries runs parallel to the Henle’s loop forming a ‘U’ shaped vasa recta. Vasa recta is absent or highly reduced in cortical nephrons. Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Peritubular capillaries are located around
explanation: Peritubular capillaries are located around the renal tubule. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292

question: The renal corpuscle is also called...
explanation: The renal corpuscle is also called Malpighian body. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

iv. It is network of minute vessels
explanation: A minute vessel of this network runs parallel to the Henle’s loop forming a ‘U’ shaped vasa recta. Vasa recta is absent or highly reduced in cortical nephrons. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: The first step in urine formation is the filtration of blood, which is carried out by the glomerulus and is called...
explanation: The first step in urine formation is the filtration of blood, which is carried out by the glomerulus and is called Gloemrular filtrate. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 293
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question:
Glomerular filtrate contains all of the following except? 
i. Glucose 
ii. Water 
iii. Urea 
iv. Plasma proteins
explanation: Blood is filtered so finely through these membranes, that almost all the constituents of the plasma except the proteins pass onto the lumen of the Bowman’s capsule. Therefore, it is considered as a process of ultra filtration. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 293
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question:
Which of the following is/are correct regarding podocytes?

explanation: Renal calculi: Stone or insoluble mass of crystallised salts (oxalates, etc.) formed within the kidney. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 299

question: The portion of Nephron extending towards Medullary region?

topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Afferent arteriole is formed by the branching of which artery?
explanation: Glomerulus is a tuft of capillaries formed by the afferent arteriole – a fine branch of renal artery.Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System
option_a: It is direct branch of aorta

question: Blood is carried away from the Glomerulus by?
explanation: Blood from the glomerulus is carried away by an efferent arteriole. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 292
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following is Mismatched?
explanation: Protonephridia or flame cells are the excretory structures in Platyhelminthes (Flatworms, e.g., Planaria), rotifers, some annelids and the cephalochordate – Amphioxus. Protonephridia are primarily concerned with ionic and fluid volume regulation, i.e., osmoregulation. Nephridia are the tubular excretory structures of earthworms and other annelids. Nephridia help to remove nitrogenous wastes and maintain a fluid and ionic balance. Malpighian tubules are the excretory structures of most of the insects. Reference  : NCERT Page 290
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Green glands are also called....
explanation: Antennal glands or green glands perform the excretory function in crustaceans like prawns. Reference  : NCERT Page 290
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System

question: Which of the following is not a charcteristic of Kidneys?

explanation: Kidneys are reddish brown, bean shaped structures situated between the levels of last thoracic and third lumbar vertebra close to the dorsal inner wall of the abdominal cavity. Reference  :  NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 291
topic_name: Human Physiology >> Excretory Products and their Elimination >> Human Excretory System
