explanation: Statins produced by the yeast Monascus purpureus have been commercialised as blood-cholesterol lowering agents. It acts by competitively inhibiting the enzyme responsible for synthesis of cholesterol. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

question: Which one of the following is a wrong matching of microbe and its industrial product, while the remaining three are correct
explanation: Acid producers are Aspergillus niger (a fungus) of citric acid, Acetobacter aceti (a bacterium) of acetic acid; Clostridium butylicum (a bacterium) of butyric acid and Lactobacillus (a bacterium) of lactic acid. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:183, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

question: Microbes are not used for production of enzymes.
explanation: Microbes are also used for production of enzymes. Some examples are lipases, pectinases, proteases, streptokinases by streptococcus(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:183, paragraph no:3
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Chemicals, Enzymes and other Bioactive Molecules

question: A major component of waste water is human excreta. This municipal waste-water is also called as
explanation: We know that large quantities of waste water are generated everyday in cities and towns. A major component of this waste water is human excreta. This municipal waste-water is also called sewage. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:183, paragraph no:5)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Before disposal, sewage is treated in sewage treatment plants (STPs) to make it less polluting.
explanation: Sewage contains large amounts of organic matter and microbes which are pathogenic. This cannot be discharged into natural water bodies like rivers and streams directly. So, before disposal, hence, sewage is treated in sewage treatment plants (STPs) to make it less polluting.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:183, paragraph no:5)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Treatment of waste water is done by the ________ naturally present in the sewage.
explanation: Treatment of waste water is done by the heterotrophic microbes naturally present in the sewage. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Which part of sewage treatment steps basically involve physical removal of particles – large and small – from the sewage
explanation: Primary treatment steps basically involve physical removal of particles – large and small – from the sewage  (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: In Primary treatment _____ and ______occurs.
explanation: Primary treatment steps basically involve physical removal of particles – large and small – from the sewage through filtration and sedimentation (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Floating debris are removed by _____and grit (soil and small pebbles) are removed by_______(answer respectively)
explanation: In Primary treatment steps basically involve physical removal of particles – large and small – from the sewage through filtration and sedimentation. These are removed in stages; initially, floating debris is removed by sequential filtration. Then the grit (soil and small pebbles) are removed by sedimentation (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: What do all the solids that settle after sedimentation form?
explanation: In Primary solid settlement take place. All solids that settle form the primary sludge (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: In Primary treatment of Sewage supernatant forms the _____
explanation: All solids that settle form the primary sludge, and the supernatant forms the effluent. The effluent from the primary settling tank is taken for secondary treatment. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Biological treatment in Sewage treatment is the other name for
explanation: Second part of sewage treatment includes the microbes playing a major role.Thats why its also called biological treatment. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: The primary effluent is passed into large ______ tanks
explanation: The primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks where it is constantly agitated mechanically and air is pumped into it. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question:
In biological treatment, what happens in the large aeration tanks? 

1)Primary effluent is passed through large aeration tanks

2)Vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into flocs

3)Primary effluent is constantly agitated mechanically

4)Air is pumped into it 

Correct sequence of the events is-
explanation: The primary effluent is passed into large aeration tanks where it is constantly agitated mechanically and air is pumped into it. This allows vigorous growth of useful aerobic microbes into flocs (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh like structure is called as
explanation: Flocs are masses of bacteria associated with fungal filaments to form mesh like structures (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: While growing, microbes consume the major part of the organic matter in the effluent. This results in
answer: Significantly reduces the biochemical O₂ demand
explanation: In the sewage the microbes while growing consume the major part of the organic matter in the effluent. This significantly reduces the BOD (biochemical O₂ demand) of the effluent (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment
option_a: Significantly reduces the biochemical O₂ demand
option_d: Significantly increases the biochemical O₂ demand

question: BOD is
explanation: Biological agent, microbes consume the organic,chemical matter by enzyme action utilising the oxygen. BOD refers to the amount of the O₂ that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one liter of water were oxidised by bacteria  (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: The amount of the O₂ that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one liter of water were oxidised by bacteria is
explanation: BOD refers to the amount of the O₂ that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one liter of water were oxidised by bacteria, it can be referred to as Biological O₂ demand, Biochemical O₂ Demand (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: The sewage water is treated till the BOD is _______.
explanation: The sewage water is treated till the BOD is reduced. The BOD test measures the rate of uptake of O₂ by microorganisms in a sample of water and thus, indirectly, BOD is a measure of the organic matter present in the water (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: BOD refers to the amount of the  CO₂  that would be consumed if all the inorganic matter in one liter of water were oxidised by bacteria.
explanation: BOD refers to the amount of the O₂ that would be consumed if all the organic matter in one liter of water were oxidised by bacteria. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question:
BOD test measures- 
(i)Rate of uptake of O₂ by microorganisms in a sample of water 
(ii)Rate of increase in O₂ levels 
(iii)Measure of the organic matter present in the water.
explanation: The sewage water is treated till the BOD is reduced. The BOD test measures the rate of uptake of O₂ by micro-organisms in a sample of water and thus, indirectly, BOD is a measure of the organic matter present in the water (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: The greater the BOD of waste water,
explanation: The greater the BOD of waste water, more is its polluting potential. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: In which tanks flocs are allowed to sediment?
explanation: Once the BOD of sewage or waste water is reduced significantly, the effluent is then passed into a settling tank where the bacterial ‘flocs’ are allowed to sediment. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Bacterial Flocs settling down with reduction in BOD of sewage is called
explanation: Once the BOD of sewage or waste water is reduced significantly, the effluent is then passed into a settling tank where the bacterial ‘flocs’ are allowed to sediment. This sediment is called activated sludge. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: A small part of the _______ is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum.
explanation: A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called
explanation: Small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum. The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question:
The anaerobic bacteria digest the bacteria and the fungi in the sludge and produced which gas during this digestion? 

(i)Methane
 
(ii)Nitrogen  

(iii) CO₂   

(iv)Hydrogen sulphide
explanation: The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters. Here, other kinds of bacteria, which grow anaerobically, digest the bacteria and the fungi in the sludge. During this digestion, bacteria produce a mixture of gases such as methane, hydrogen sulphide and  CO₂ . (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: The property due to which Biogas is used as an energy fuel
explanation: Bacteria, which grow anaerobically, digest the bacteria and the fungi in the sludge. During this digestion, bacteria produce a mixture of gases such as methane, hydrogen sulphide and  CO₂ . These gases form biogas and can be used as source of energy as it is inflammable (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Which combination of gases form biogas?
explanation: During the digestion, bacteria produce a mixture of gases such as methane, hydrogen sulphide and  CO₂ . These gases form biogas and can be used as source of energy as it is inflammable.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment
option_c: Methane, hydrogen sulphide and carbon monoxide

question:
What has The Ministry of Environment and Forests initiated to save major rivers of our country from pollution? 

(i)Ganga Action Plan  

(ii)Yamuna Action Plan  

(iii)Godavari and Ganga Action plans
explanation: The Ministry of Environment and Forests has initiated Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to save these major rivers of our country from pollution. Under these plans, it is proposed to build a large number of sewage treatment plants so that only treated sewage may be discharged in the rivers. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Under Yamuna and Ganga Action plans, it is proposed to build a large number of sewage treatment plants so that only treated sewage may be discharged in the river
explanation: The Ministry of Environment and Forests has initiated Ganga Action Plan and Yamuna Action Plan to save these major rivers of our country from pollution. topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

explanation: Sewage cannot be discharged into natural water bodies like rivers and streams directly – you can understand why. Before disposal, hence, sewage is treated in sewage treatment plants (STPs) to make it less polluting. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:183, paragraph no:5)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: Sewage treatment is carried out in how many stages-
explanation: Sewage treatment is carried out in two stages: Primary treatment and Secondary treatment or Biological treatment (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question: In sewage treatment what is released into natural water bodies?
explanation: The effluent from the secondary treatment plant is generally released into natural water bodies like rivers and streams(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:5)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question:
Assertion: The method of sewage treatment using microbes is the oldest yet most efficient one in the whole world.

answer: Both Assertion and Reason are correct and the Reason is a correct explanation of the Assertion.

question:
The reasons for the pollution of the natural water bodies are-

(i) Increased urbanisation  

(ii) Efficient sewage plants   

(iii) Decreased industrialisation 

(iv) Insufficient sewage plants
explanation: Increasing urbanisation has resulted in sewage being produced in much larger quantities than ever before. However the number of sewage treatment plants has not increased enough to treat such large quantities. So the untreated sewage is often discharged directly into rivers leading to their pollution and increase in water-borne diseases(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in Sewage Treatment

question:

explanation: The untreated sewage is often discharged directly into rivers leading to their pollution and increase in water-borne diseases. question: Which among the following is Incorrect about biogas?
answer: It is obtained primarily from plants
explanation: Biogas is a mixture of gases (containing predominantly methane) produced by the microbial activity and which may be used as fuel (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:4)

option_a: It is a mixture of gases and used as fuel

question: The type of the gas produced by microbes depends upon the microbes and the organic substrates they utilise.
explanation: The microbes produce different types of gaseous end-products during growth and metabolism. The type of the gas produced depends upon the microbes and the organic substrates they utilise (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question:
CO₂  as the main gas is produced in which of the following process? 

(i)Fermentation of dough  

(ii)Cheese making  

(iii)Production of beverages 

(iv)Biogas
explanation: In relation to fermentation of dough, cheese making and production of beverages, the main gas produced was CO₂ . (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question:
Bacteria which grow anaerobically on cellulosic material, produce- 
(i)Large amount of methane  
(ii) CO₂   
(iii)O₂  
(iv)Nitrogen
explanation: Certain bacteria, which grow anaerobically on cellulosic material, produce large amount of methane along with CO₂  and H₂ . These bacteria are collectively called methanogens (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question: _______ bacteria are commonly found in the anaerobic sludge during sewage treatment
explanation: Methanogens, one such common bacterium is Methanobacterium. These bacteria are commonly found in the anaerobic sludge during sewage treatment (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question: _______ bacteria are also present in the rumen (a part of stomach) of cattle.
explanation: Methanogens are also present in the rumen (a part of stomach) of cattle. A lot of cellulosic material present in the food of cattle is also present in the rumen (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question:
Methanobacterium is a common example of- 

(i)Bacteria present in rumen of cattle  

(ii)Bacteria which use methane as main energy source  

(iii)Bacteria present in the anaerobic sludge during sewage treatment  

(iv)Methanogens
explanation: Methanogens, one such common bacterium is Methanobacterium. These bacteria are commonly found in the anaerobic sludge during sewage treatment. They are also present in the rumen (a part of stomach) of cattle. A lot of cellulosic material present in the food of cattle is also present in the rumen (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question: In rumen, Methanobacterium help in the breakdown of
explanation: In rumen, these bacteria help in the breakdown of cellulose and play an important role in the nutrition of cattle. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question: Dung can be used for generation of biogas, commonly called
explanation: The excreta (dung) of cattle, commonly called gobar, is rich in these bacteria. Dung can be used for generation of biogas, commonly called gobar gas. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:185, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question: In what places are the Biogas plants most often built?
explanation: Cattle dung is available in large quantities in rural areas where cattle are used for a variety of purposes. So biogas plants are more often built in rural areas (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:186, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question: In rural areas the biogas produced is used for cooking and lighting
explanation: Cattle dung is available in large quantities in rural areas where cattle are used for a variety of purposes. So biogas plants are more often built in rural areas. The biogas thus produced is used for cooking and lighting. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:186, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question:
The technology of biogas production was developed in India mainly due to the efforts of- 
(i)Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)

(iii)The Indian Renewable Energy Development Agency (IREDA)
(iv)WFF(World Fuel Federation)
explanation: The technology of biogas production was developed in India mainly due to the efforts of Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI) and Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC) (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:186, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question: What is the approximate length(in feet) of a biogas plant?
explanation: The biogas plant consists of a concrete tank (10-15 feet deep) in which bio-wastes are collected and a slurry of dung is fed.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:186, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question:
What is the right sequence of biogas production?  
(a) Dung slurry inside biogas plant  
(b) Microbial action   
(c) Floating cover   
(d) Remains as biofertilizer  
(e) Through a outlet  
(f) Pipe supply to houses  
(g)Gas produced
explanation: The biogas plant consists of a concrete tank (10-15 feet deep) in which bio-wastes are collected and a slurry of dung is fed. A floating cover is placed over the slurry, which keeps on rising as the gas is produced in the tank due to the microbial activity. The biogas plant has an outlet, which is connected to a pipe to supply biogas to nearby houses. The spent slurry is removed through another outlet and may be used as fertiliser. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:186, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes in production of biogas

question: _______refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests.
explanation: Biocontrol refers to the use of biological methods for controlling plant diseases and pests. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:186, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes as biocontrol agents

explanation: Contrary to the ‘conventional’ farming practices which often use chemical methods to kill both useful and harmful life forms indiscriminately, organic farming is a holistic approach that seeks to develop an understanding of the webs of interaction between the myriad of organisms that constitute the field fauna and flora. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:186, paragraph no:3)

question:
Aphids and mosquitoes can be gotten rid by- 
(i)Beetle with red and black markings – the Ladybird  
(ii)Dragonflies 
(iii)Eagles
explanation: The very familiar beetle with red and black markings – the Ladybird, and Dragonflies are useful to get rid of aphids and mosquitoes, respectively (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:187, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes as biocontrol agents

question: An example of microbial biocontrol agents that can be introduced in order to control butterfly caterpillars is
explanation: An example of microbial biocontrol agents that can be introduced in order to control butterfly caterpillars is the bacteria Bacillus thuringiensis (often written as Bt). (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:187, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes as biocontrol agents

question:
True about bacteria Bacillus thuringiensis- 
(i)These are available in sachets as dried spores which are mixed with water  
(ii)Sprayed onto vulnerable plants such as brassicas and fruit trees, where these are eaten by the insect larvae.  
(iii)The bacterial disease will kill the caterpillars, but leave other insects unharmed  
(iv)These are harmful if ingested by humans or grazing animals
explanation: The bacteria Bacillus thuringiensis (often written as Bt) are available in sachets as dried spores which are mixed with water and sprayed onto vulnerable plants such as brassicas and fruit trees, where these are eaten by the insect larvae. In the gut of the larvae, the toxin is released and the larvae get killed. The bacterial disease will kill the caterpillars, but leave other insects unharmed. They don't harm humans or animals as they cannot be activated in their bodies.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:187, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Microbes as biocontrol agents

question: Because of the development of methods of genetic engineering in the last decade or so, the scientists have introduced B. thuringiensis toxin genes into plants.
explanation: The development of methods of genetic engineering in the last decade or so, resulted in the scientists introducing B. thuringiensis toxin genes into plants. Such plants are resistant to attack by insect pests. Bt-cotton is one such example, which is being cultivated in some states of our country. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:187, paragraph no:2)

question: What gases are produced in anaerobic sludge digesters? [AIPMT 2014]
explanation: The type of gases produced by microbial activity depend upon the microbes and the organic substrates they utilise. Certain bacteria, called methanogens, grow anaerobically on cellulosic material and produce large amount of methane along with  CO₂ . These bacteria are commonly found in the anaerobic sludge during sewage treatment. The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters. Here, other kinds of bacteria, which grow anaerobically, digest the bacteria and the fungi in the sludge. During this digestion, bacteria produce a mixture of gases such as methane, hydrogen sulphide and  CO₂ . (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Previous Year Questions

question: The domestic sewage in large cities [AIPMT 2012]
answer: Has very high amount of suspended solids and dissolved salts.
explanation: Sewage water can be purified by passing it through sewage treatment plants with the action of heterotrophic microorganisms. There are 2 stages of this treatment – primary and secondary. Primary treatment removes floating and suspended solids from sewage through two processes of filtration and sedimentation. First floating matter is removed through sequential filtration. The filtrate is kept in large open settling tanks where grit settles down. The sediment is called primary sludge while the supernatant is called effluent. The primary sludge traps a lot of microbes and debris. In secondary treatment, the primary effluent is taken to aeration tanks. A large number of aerobic heterotrophic microbes grow in the aeration tank. They form flocs. Flocs are masses of bacteria held together by slime and fungal filaments to form mesh like structures. The microbes digest a lot of organic matter, converting it into microbial biomass and releasing a lot of minerals. As the BOD of the waste matter is reduced to 10-15% of raw sewage, it is passed into settling tank. The sediment of settling tank is called activated sludge. The remaining is passed into a large tank called anaerobic sludge digester. It is designed for continuous operation. The aerobic microbes present in the sludge get killed. Anaerobic microbes digest the organic mass as well as aerobic microbes of the sludge. They are of two types, non-methanogenic and methanogenic. Methanogenic bacteria produce a mixture of gases containing methane, H2S and CO₂ . (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Previous Year Questions
option_a: Has a high BOD as it contains both aerobic and anaerobic bacteria.
option_b: Is processed by aerobic and then anaerobic bacteria in the secondary treatment in Sewage Treatment Plants (STPs).
option_c: When treated in STPs does not really require the aeration step as the sewage contains adequate oxygen.
option_d: Has very high amount of suspended solids and dissolved salts.

question:
Select the correct statements regarding dissolved 
Oxygen and Biochemical Oxygen Demand. 
 (A) BOD is inversely related to dissolved oxygen. 
 (B) Low dissolved oxygen and high BOD lead to 
loss of aquatic life. 
 (C) High BOD leads to high dissolved oxygen. 
 (D) Both BOD and dissolved oxygen are indicator of 
health of a water body. 
 (E) Both BOD and dissolved oxygen are affected by 
amount of organic matter in the water body. 
 Choose the most appropriate answer from the 
options given below : [ NEET 2023]
explanation:
The correct statements regarding dissolved oxygen (DO) and biochemical oxygen demand (BOD) are as follows:

(A) BOD is inversely related to dissolved oxygen: BOD is a measure of the amount of oxygen consumed by microorganisms while decomposing organic matter in water. As BOD increases, the amount of dissolved oxygen decreases.

(B) Low dissolved oxygen and high BOD lead to the loss of aquatic life: Aquatic organisms require dissolved oxygen for respiration. When dissolved oxygen levels decrease due to high BOD, it can lead to oxygen depletion in the water, causing stress or death to aquatic organisms.

(D) Both BOD and dissolved oxygen are indicators of the health of a water body: BOD and dissolved oxygen levels provide valuable information about the quality and health of a water body. High BOD and low dissolved oxygen levels indicate pollution and poor water quality.

(E) Both BOD and dissolved oxygen are affected by the amount of organic matter in the water body: BOD measures the oxygen demand of organic matter, and the decomposition of organic matter consumes oxygen, reducing dissolved oxygen levels in the water.
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Microbes in Human Welfare >> Previous Year Questions

question: Which one of the following statement regarding BOD is true? [AIIMS 2017]
answer: The greater the BOD of waste water, more is its polluting potential.
explanation: BOD is the method of determining the amount of O₂ required by microorganisms to decompose the waste present in the water supply. It is a measure of organic matter present in the water. If the quantity of organic wastes in the water supply is high then the number of decomposing bacteria present in the water will also be high. As a result, BOD value will increase. The BOD test measures the rate of uptake of O₂ by microorganisms in a sample of water and thus, indirectly, BOD is a measure of the organic matter present in the water. The greater the BOD of waste water, more is its polluting potential. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:184, paragraph no:3)

explanation:
Treatment of waste water is done by the heterotrophic microbes naturally present in the sewage

question:
Consider the following statements regarding Sewage Treatment, choose the correct statements

1) The sedimented bacterial flocs are also known as activated sludge

2) The bacteria and fungi in anaerobic sludge digester are digested

3) Biogas is not inflammable

4) The activated sludge pumped back into aeration tank is served as inoculum
explanation:
Once the BOD of sewage or waste water is reduced significantly, the effluent is then passed into a settling tank where the bacterial ‘flocs’ are allowed to sediment. This sediment is called activated sludge
The remaining major part of the sludge is pumped into large tanks called anaerobic sludge digesters. Here, other kinds of bacteria, which grow anaerobically, digest the bacteria and the fungi in the sludge
Biogas can be used as source of energy as it is inflammable
A small part of the activated sludge is pumped back into the aeration tank to serve as the inoculum
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 12, Chapter 10, pg 184, para 4)

question: Energy currency of the cell is
explanation:
During oxidation within a cell, all the energy contained in respiratory substrates is not released free into the cell, or in a single step. It is released in a series of slow stepwise reactions controlled by enzymes, and it is trapped as chemical energy in the form of ATP. Hence, it is important to understand that the energy released by oxidation in respiration is not (or rather cannot be) used directly but is used to synthesise ATP, which is broken down whenever (and wherever) energy needs to be utilised. Hence, ATP acts as the energy currency of the cell

explanation:
The ratio of the volume of CO₂ evolved to the volume of O₂ consumed in respiration is called the respiratory quotient (RQ) or respiratory ratio. When carbohydrates are used as substrate and are completely oxidised, the RQ will be 1, because equal amounts of CO₂ and O₂ are evolved and consumed,
When fats are used in respiration, the RQ is less than 1. When proteins are respiratory substrates the ratio would be about 0.9.  (Reference  : NCERT, page 236, paragraph 1,2  and  3).

question: Match List  I with List II    (a) ETS complex-I (b) ETS complex-II (c) ETS complex III (d) ETS complex IV     List II (i) cytochrome bc1 (ii) Cytochrome a, a3 and two copper centers (iii) NADH dehydrogenase (iv) Ubiquinone and FADH2 dehydrogenase. explanation:
Electrons from NADH produced in the mitochondrial matrix during citric acid cycle are oxidised by an NADH dehydrogenase (complex I), and electrons are then transferred to ubiquinone located within the inner membrane. Ubiquinone also receives reducing equivalents via FADH2 (complex II) that is generated during oxidation of succinate in the citric acid cycle. The reduced ubiquinone (ubiquinol) is then oxidised with the transfer of electrons to cytochrome c via cytochrome bc1 complex (complex III). Cytochrome c is a small protein attached to the outer surface of the inner membrane and acts as a mobile carrier for transfer of electrons between complex III and IV. question: Heat loss or heat gain is a function of __________

This is the main reason why very small animals are rarely found in polar regions.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12: page no:224, paragraph no:3)

question:
Pick the correct statements : 

A.During the course of evolution, the costs and benefits of maintaining a constant internal environment are taken into consideration. 

B.Some species have evolved the ability to regulate, but only over a limited range of environmental conditions, beyond which they simply conform. 

C.If the stressful external conditions are localised or remain only for a short duration, the organism has two other alternatives for survival. 

D.During the course of evolution, only the benefits of maintaining a variable internal environment are taken into consideration.
explanation: During the course of evolution, the costs and benefits of maintaining a constant internal environment are taken into consideration. question: Altitude sickness is related to?
explanation: Tourists visiting high altitude areas such as Rohtang Pass or Mansarovar, experience altitude sickness. Its symptoms include nausea, fatigue and heart palpitations. The body compensates low O₂ availability by increasing red blood cell production, decreasing the binding affinity of haemoglobin and by increasing breathing rate.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12: page no:226, paragraph no:2)

question:
The measurement in number is not appropriate in which cases?
 
 i) If there are 200 carrot grass (Parthenium hysterophorus) plants but only a single huge banyan tree with a large canopy.
 
 ii) Siberian cranes at Bharatpur wetlands in any year
explanation:
The size, in nature, could be as low as <10 (Siberian cranes at Bharatpur wetlands in any year)

Total number is generally the most appropriate measure of population density, it is in some cases either meaningless or difficult to determine. In an area, if there are 200 carrot grass (Parthenium hysterophorus) plants but only a single huge banyan tree with a large canopy, stating that the population density of banyan is low relative to that of carrot grass amounts to underestimating the enormous role of the Banyan in that community. 

In such cases, the % cover or biomass is a more meaningful measure of the population size. Total number is again not an easily adoptable measure if the population is huge and counting is impossible or very time-consuming. question:

 ii) Barnacles growing on the back of a whale.
 
 iii) The cattle egret and grazing cattle in close association.
 
 iv) Lice on human
explanation: Commensalism is the interaction in which one species benefits and the other is neither harmed nor benefited. An orchid growing as an epiphyte on a mango branch, and barnacles growing on the back of a whale benefit while neither the mango tree nor the whale derives any apparent benefit. The cattle egret and grazing cattle in close association, a sight you are most likely to catch if you live in farmed rural areas, is a classic example of commensalism.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12: page no:236, paragraph no:4)

question: In many species of fig trees, there is a tight one-to-one relationship with the pollinator species of wasp. Given statement is true or false?
explanation: In many species of fig trees, there is a tight one-to-one relationship with the pollinator species of wasp. It means that a given fig species can be pollinated only by its ‘partner’ wasp species and no other species. The female wasp uses the fruit not only as an oviposition (egg-laying) site but uses the developing seeds within the fruit for nourishing its larvae. The wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for suitable egg-laying sites. In return for the favour of pollination the fig offers the wasp some of its developing seeds, as food for the developing wasp larvae. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12: page no:237, paragraph no:3)

question: Which of the following is not an attribute of a population? [NEET 2020]
explanation:
A population has certain attributes whereas, an individual organism does not. An individual may have births and deaths, but a population has birth rates and death rates. In a population these rates refer to per capita births and deaths. The rates, hence, expressed are change in numbers (increase or decrease) with respect to members of the population. Here is an example. If in a pond there were 20 lotus plants last year and through reproduction 8 new plants are added, taking the current population to 28, we calculate the birth rate as 8/20 = 0.4 offspring per lotus per year. If 4 individuals in a laboratory population of 40 fruitflies died during a specified time interval, say a week, the death rate in the population during that period is 4/40 = 0.1 individuals per fruitfly per week.
Another attribute characteristic of a population is sex ratio. An individual is either a male or a female but a population has a sex ratio (e.g., 60 % of the population are females and 40 % males).(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12: page no:227, paragraph no:2,3)

question:
Consider these statements regarding Exponential Growth and choose the correct option. 
 
 1. Any species growing exponentially under unlimited resource conditions can reach enormous population densities in a short time. 
 
 2. Darwin observed Exponential growth while developing his theory of natural selection. 
 
 3. Exponential graph results in a J-shaped curve. 
 
 4. Geometrical Growth is shown by dN/dt = rN.
explanation: Any species growing exponentially under unlimited resource conditions can reach enormous population densities in a short time. When resources in the habitat are unlimited, each species has the ability to realise fully its innate potential to grow in number, as Darwin observed while developing his theory of natural selection. If in a population of size N, the birth rates (not total number but per capita births) are represented as b and death rates (again, per capita death rates) as d, then the increase or decrease in N during a unit time period t (dN/dt) will be dN/dt = (b – d) × N Let (b–d) = r, then dN/dt = rN. The above equation describes the exponential or geometric growth pattern of a population and results in a J-shaped curve. When we plot N in relation to time. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 12, Page No. 230, Para 1)

question:
Consider these statements regarding Intrinsic rate and choose the correct option. 
 
 1. r is known as intrinsic rate of natural increase 
 
 2. It is also known as Biotic potential. 
 
 3. It is a very important parameter chosen for assessing impacts of only biotic factors on population growth. 
 
 4. For the Norway rat the r is 0.15, and for the flour beetle it is 0.012. 
 
 5. In 1981, the r value for the human population in India was 0.0205.
explanation: r is intrinsic rate of natural increase, also called Biotic potential. It is a very important parameter chosen for assessing impacts of any biotic or abiotic factor on population growth. For the Norway rat the r is 0.015, and for the flour beetle it is 0.12. In 1981, the r value for human population in India was 0.0205. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 12, Page No. 230, Para 2)

question:
Consider these statements regarding Logistic Growth and choose the correct option. 
 
 1. No Population of any species in nature has at its disposal unlimited resources to permit exponential growth. 
 
 2. Only the ‘fittest’ individual will survive and reproduce. 
 
 3. In nature, a given habitat has enough resources to support a maximum possible number, beyond which no further growth is possible. It is called carrying capacity (K) for that species in that habitat. 
 
 4. The geometrical growth model is considered a more realistic one.
explanation: No population of any species in nature has at its disposal unlimited resources to permit exponential growth. This leads to competition between individuals for limited resources. Eventually, the ‘fittest’ individual will survive and reproduce. In nature, a given habitat has enough resources to support a maximum possible number, beyond which no further growth is possible. Let us call this limit as nature’s carrying capacity (K) for that species in that habitat. Since resources for growth for most animal populations are finite and become limiting sooner or later, the logistic growth model is considered a more realistic one. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 12, Page No. 231, Para 2)

question:
Consider these statements regarding Logistic Growth and choose the correct option. 
 
 1. A population growing in a habitat with limited resources show initially a lag phase. 
 
 2. Lag phase is reached when the population density reaches the carrying capacity. 
 
 3. A plot of N in relation to time (t) results in a sigmoid curve. 
 
 4. This population growth is called Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth.
explanation: A population growing in a habitat with limited resources show initially a lag phase, followed by phases of acceleration and deceleration and finally an asymptote, when the population density reaches the carrying capacity. A plot of N in relation to time (t) results in a sigmoid curve. This type of population growth is called Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 12, Page No. 231, Para 2)

question:
Consider these statements regarding population interaction and choose the correct option. 
 
 1. In commensalism the one species is harmed whereas the other is unaffected. 
 
 2. The interaction where one species is benefitted and the other is neither benefitted nor harmed is called amensalism. 
 
 3. Both the species benefit in mutualism. 
 
 4. In both parasitism and predation only one species benefits.
explanation: Both the species benefit in mutualism. In both parasitism and predation only one species benefits (parasite and predator, respectively) and the interaction is detrimental to the other species (host and prey, respectively). The interaction where one species is benefitted and the other is neither benefitted nor harmed is called commensalism. In amensalism on the other hand one species is harmed whereas the other is unaffected. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 12, Page No. 233, Para 1)

question:
Consider these statements regarding mutualism by fig and wasp and choose the correct option. 

1. In many species of fig trees, there is a tight one-to-one relationship with the pollinator species of wasp. 

2. A given fig species can be pollinated only by its ‘partner’ wasp species and no other species. 

3. The wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for suitable egg-laying sites. 

4. Fig offers the wasp some of its developing seeds, as food for the developing wasp larvae.
explanation: In many species of fig trees, there is a tight one-to-one relationship with the pollinator species of wasp. It means that a given fig species can be pollinated only by it ‘partner’ wasp species and no other species. The female wasp uses the fruit not only as an oviposition (egg-laying) site but uses the developing seeds within the fruit for nourishing its larvae. The wasp pollinates the fig inflorescence while searching for suitable egg-laying sites. In return for the favour of pollination the fig offers the wasp some of its developing seeds, as food for the developing wasp larvae. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 12, Page No. 237, Last Para)

explanation: The Mediterranean orchid Ophrys employs ‘sexual deceit’ to get pollination done by a species of bee. One petal of its flower bears an uncanny resemblance to the female of the bee in size, colour and markings. The male bee is attracted to what it perceives as a female, ‘pseudocopulates’ with the flower, and during that process is dusted with pollen from the flower. question:
Consider the following statements:

a. Consciousness is the defining property of living organisms.

b. Cellular organisation of the body is the defining feature of life forms.

c. Properties of tissues are present in the individual constituent cells.

d. Properties of cellular organelles are present in the molecular constituents of the organelle.

e. All living organisms are linked to one another by the sharing of common genetic material but to varying degrees.

Among these the false statements are
explanation:
All organisms, from the prokaryotes to the most complex eukaryotes can sense and respond to environmental cues. Photoperiod affects reproduction in seasonal breeders, both plants and animals. All organisms handle chemicals entering their bodies. All organisms, therefore, are ‘aware’ of their surroundings. A human being is the only organism who is aware of himself, i.e., has self-consciousness. Consciousness, therefore, becomes the defining property of living organisms. The cellular organisation of the body is the defining feature of life forms. Properties of tissues are not present in the constituent cells but arise as a result of interactions among the constituent cells. Similarly, the properties of cellular organelles are not present in the molecular constituents of the organelle but arise as a result of interactions among the molecular components comprising the organelle. Biology is the story of life on earth. Biology is the story of the evolution of living organisms on earth. All living organisms – present, past and future, are linked to one another by the sharing of the common genetic material, but to varying degrees.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 5; Paragraph No. 4)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> The Living World >> Definition Of Living

question:
Consider the following statements:

i. Growth is a defining property of all living organisms.

ii. Reproduction is a defining all-inclusive characteristic of all living organisms.

iii. Metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms without exception.

iv. Cellular organisation of the body is a defining feature of all life forms.

v. Consciousness is a defining property of all living organisms.                                                                                                                                                           

Choose the correct option regarding the above statements:
answer: Only i and ii are false.
explanation:
i. All living organisms grow, but growth is not a “defining” property of all living organisms because non-living organisms grow too. Non-living objects also grow if we take an increase in body mass as a criterion for growth. Mountains, boulders and sand mounds do grow. However, this kind of growth exhibited by non-living objects is by the accumulation of material on the surface. In living organisms, growth is from the inside. Growth, therefore, cannot be taken as a defining property of living organisms.

ii. There are many organisms which do not reproduce (mules, sterile worker bees, infertile human couples, etc). Hence, reproduction also cannot be an all-inclusive “defining” characteristic of living organisms. Of course, no non-living object is capable of reproducing or replicating by itself.

iii. All plants, animals, fungi and microbes exhibit metabolism. The total of all the chemical reactions occurring in our body is metabolism. No non-living object exhibits metabolism. Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems. An isolated metabolic reaction(s) outside the body of an organism, performed in a test tube is neither living nor non-living. Hence, while metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms without exception, isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are not living things but surely living reactions.

iv. Cellular organisation of the body is the defining feature of life forms.

v. All organisms, from the prokaryotes to the most complex eukaryotes can sense and respond to environmental cues. Consciousness, therefore, becomes the defining property of living organisms.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology class 11, pages 3-5)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> The Living World >> Definition Of Living
option_b: Only i and ii are false.
option_c: Only iv and v are true.

explanation:
Here you must recognise that taxa can indicate categories at very different levels. ‘Plants’ – also form a taxa. ‘Wheat’ is also a taxa. Similarly, ‘animals’, ‘mammals’, ‘dogs’ are all taxa – but you know that a dog is a mammal and mammals are animals. Therefore, ‘animals’, ‘mammals’ and ‘dogs’ represent taxa at different levels. question: Select the correctly written scientific name of Mango which was first described by Carolus Linnaeus [2019]
explanation:
The scientific name of mango is written as Mangifera indica. Let us see how it is a binomial name. In this name Mangifera represents the genus while indica, is a particular species, or a specific epithet. Other universal rules of nomenclature are as follows:

1. Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics. They are Latinised or derived from Latin irrespective of their origin.

2. The first word in a biological name represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet.

3. Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined, or printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin.

4. The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter. It can be illustrated with the example of Mangifera indica.

Name of the author appears after the specific epithet, i.e., at the end of the biological name and is written in an abbreviated form, e.g., Mangifera indica Linn. It indicates that this species was first described by Linnaeus.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 7 ; Paragraph No. 1 and 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> The Living World >> Previous Year Questions

2. In living organisms, growth is from inside.

4. Growth can be taken as a defining property of living organisms.
explanation:
In majority of higher animals and plants, growth and reproduction are mutually exclusive events. One must remember that increase in body mass is considered as growth. Non-living objects also grow if we take increase in body mass as a criterion for growth. Mountains, boulders and sand mounds do grow. However, this kind of growth exhibited by non-living objects is by accumulation of material on the surface. In living organisms, growth is from inside. Growth, therefore, cannot be taken as a defining property of living organisms. 
(Reference   NCERT biology class 11; Chapter 1; Page no 4; Paragraph no; 1)

4. The fungi, the filamentous algae, the protozoa of mosses, all cannot multiply by fragmentation.
explanation:
There are many organisms which do not reproduce (mules, sterile worker bees, infertile human couples, etc). When it comes to unicellular organisms like bacteria, unicellular algae or Amoeba, reproduction is synonymous with growth, i.e., increase in number of cells. volvox is a multicellular algae. The fungi, the filamentous algae, the protonema of mosses, all easily multiply by fragmentation. reproduction also cannot be an all-inclusive defining characteristic of living organisms.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding metabolism. Choose the correct option.
 
1. The sum total of all the chemical reactions occurring in our body is metabolism.

2. Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems.

3. Metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms with some exceptions.

4. Cellular organisation of the body is not the defining feature of life forms.
explanation:
The sum total of all the chemical reactions occurring in our body is metabolism. No non-living object exhibits metabolism. Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free systems. An isolated metabolic reaction(s) outside the body of an organism, performed in a test tube is neither living nor non-living. Hence, while metabolism is a defining feature of all living organisms without exception, isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are not living things but surely living reactions. Hence, cellular organisation of the body is the defining feature of life forms.
 (Reference   NCERT biology class 11; Chapter 1; Page no 5; Paragraph no 1)

3. The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter.

4. Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italized script.
explanation:
Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics. They are Latinised or derived from Latin irrespective of their origin. The first word in a biological name represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet. Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined, or printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin. The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter. It can be illustrated with the example of Mangifera indica.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding classification. Choose the correct option. 

1. Classification is the process by which anything is grouped into convenient categories based on some easy experimented characters.

2. The scientific term for these categories is taxa.

3. The ‘animals’, ‘mammals’ and ‘dogs’ represent taxa at different levels.

4. All living organisms can be classified into different taxa. This process of classification is taxonomy.
explanation:
Classification is the process by which anything is grouped into convenient categories based on some easily observable characters. The scientific term for these categories is taxa. The ‘animals’, ‘mammals’ and ‘dogs’ represent taxa at different levels. All living organisms can be classified into different taxa. This process of classification is taxonomy. 
(Reference   NCERT biology class 11; Chapter 1; Page no 7; Paragraph no 3 and 4)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> The Living World >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding taxonomy. Choose the CORRECT option. 

1. Study of different kinds of organisms and their diversities, also the relationships among them is referred to as systematics. 

2. Characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature these processes are not required for taxonomy.

3. External and internal structure, along with the structure of cell, development process and ecological evolution of organisms aren't essential to form the basis of modern taxonomic studies.

4. The word systematics is derived from the Latin word ‘systema’ which means systematic arrangement of organisms.
explanation:
External and internal structure, along with the structure of cell, development process and ecological information of organisms are essential and form the basis of modern taxonomic studies. Hence, characterisation, identification, classification and nomenclature are the processes that are basic to taxonomy. Human beings were, since long, not only interested in knowing more about different kinds of organisms and their diversities, but also the relationships among them. This branch of study was referred to as systematics. The word systematics is derived from the Latin word ‘systema’ which means systematic arrangement of organisms. 
(Reference   NCERT biology class 11; Chapter 1; Page no 8; Paragraph no 1,2 and 4)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> The Living World >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding taxonomy. Choose the correct option. 

1. Classification is not a single step process but involves hierarchy of steps in which each step represents a rank or category.

2. Each category, referred to as a unit of classification, in fact, represents a rank and is commonly termed as taxanim.

3. All categories together constitute the taxonomic hierarchy.

4. Category is a part of overall taxonomic arrangement, it is called the taxonomic assemblage.
explanation:
Classification is not a single step process but involves hierarchy of steps in which each step represents a rank or category. Since the category is a part of overall taxonomic arrangement, it is called the taxonomic category and all categories together constitute the taxonomic hierarchy. Each category, referred to as a unit of classification, in fact, represents a rank and is commonly termed as taxon. 
(Reference   NCERT biology class 11; Chapter 1; Page no 8; Paragraph no 4)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> The Living World >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:

2. Order is the assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters.

3. Genus Panthera, comprising lion, tiger, leopard is put along with genus, Felis (cats) in the family canidae.

4. Classes comprising animals like fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds along with mammals constitute the next higher category called Phylum.
explanation:
Genus Panthera, comprising lion, tiger, leopard is put along with genus, Felis (cats) in the family Felidae. Taxonomic studies consider a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities as a species. Order being a higher category, is the assemblage of families which exhibit a few similar characters. Classes comprising animals like fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds along with mammals constitute the next higher category called Phylum.

question:

explanation:

question:
Consider the following statements regarding  taxonomic categories.  Choose the correct option.

2. The Kingdom Plantae, on the other hand, is distinct, and comprises all plants from various divisions.

3. Class includes related orders.

4. Each genus may have one or more than one specific epithets representing different organisms, but having morphological similarities.
explanation:

explanation:

question:
Consider the following statements regarding common characteristics in taxa. Choose the CORRECT option.
 
1. As we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics goes on decreasing

2. Lower the taxa, more are the characteristics that the members within the taxon share.

3. Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining the relationship to other taxa at the same level.

4.Higher the category ,more easy it becomes to determine the relation between the other taxa at the same level.
explanation:
As we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics goes on decreasing. Lower the taxa, more are the characteristics that the members within the taxon share. Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining the relationship to other taxa at the same level. Hence, the problem of classification becomes more complex.

question: The interphase is also called the resting phase.
explanation: The interphase, though called the resting phase, is the time during which the cell is preparing for division by undergoing both cell growth and DNA replication in an orderly manner.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:163, paragraph no:3).

question: The cells that do not divide further exit G1 phase to enter an inactive stage called________

question:
Assertion: DNA synthesis occurs in G1 and G2 periods of cell cycle.

 Reason: During G1 and G2 phase, the DNA content become double.
answer: Both Assertion and Reason are false
explanation: The synthesis of DNA occurs only in a restricted portion of the interphase during S period, which is preceded and followed by two "gap" periods of interphase (G1 and G2) in which there is no DNA synthesis. G1 is the period between the end of mitosis(.and the start of DNA synthesis. S is the period of DNA synthesis and G2 is the interval between the end of DNA synthesis and the start of mitosis. During G1, a cell contains two times (4C) the amount of DNA present in the original diploid cell (2C). Following mitosis, the daughter cell again enter is the G1 period and have a DNA content equivalent to 2(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:163, paragraph no:4).
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Interphase

question: In the M-phase, the only component of the cell involved is the nucleus.
explanation: M-phase is the most dramatic period of the cell cycle, involving a major reorganisation of virtually all components of the cell. There are 4 divisions for karyogenesis- prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telphase followed by cytokinesis where cytoplasm and other cell organelles also divide. So cell division by mitosis involves all the components of the cell. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:164, paragraph no:3)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Prophase and Metaphase

question: Mitosis is called equational divison because
answer: Same number of chromosomes between parent and progeny cells.
explanation: Plant cells however, are enclosed by a relatively inextensible cell wall, thererfore they undergo cytokinesis by a different mechanism. In plant cells, wall formation starts in the centre of the cell and grows outward to meet the existing lateral walls. The formation of the new cell wall begins with the formation of a simple precursor, called the cell-plate that represents the middle lamella between the walls of two adjacent cells. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:166, paragraph no:3)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Prophase and Metaphase

option_b: Different number of chromosomes between parent and progeny cells.
option_c: Different number of chromatids between parent and progeny cells.

3. It restores nucleocytoplasmic ratio
4. It helps in cell repair
explanation: Mitosis usually results in the production of diploid daughter cells with identical genetic complements. The growth of multicellular organisms is due to mitosis. Cell growth results in disturbing the ratio between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. It, therefore, becomes essential for the cell to divide to restore the nucleo-cytoplasmic ratio. A very significant contribution of mitosis is cell repair. The cells of the upper layer of the epidermis, cells of the lining of the gut, and blood cells are constantly replaced.  (Reference  : NCERT biology class 11: Page no: 167, Paragraph no 1)

The phenomenon is called synapsis and it occurs during the end of zygotene stage, and may also appear at the start of pachytene but disappear towards the mid phase of pachytene,  DNA replication occurs during S phase or synthetic phase which is the second phase of interphase. During zygotene, homologous chromosomes begin to align along their entire length by a process called synapsis that is necessarily precise. Each pair of chromosomes is held together by a ribbon-like protein and forms the synaptonemal complex. Then, during pachytene, the pairs of chromosomes become condensed and coiled.

question: Which of the following options gives the correct sequence of events during mitosis ?[NEET 2017]
answer: Condensation-Nuclear membrane disassemblyﬁ-Arrangement at equatorﬁ-Centromere division-Segregation-Telophase
explanation: Mitosis is divided into four phase prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase. During prophase the indistinct and interwined DNA molecules condenses to form elongated chromosomes. The nuclear membrane disintegrates during prometaphase. During metaphase, the chromosomes align themselves at the equatorial plate. During anaphase, centromere of each chromosome divides into two so that each chromosome come to have its own centromere. Chromatids move towards opposite poles along the path of their chromosome fibres. Finally during telophase, two chromosome groups reorganise to form two nuclei. Nuclear envelope reappears, Golgi complex and endoplasmic reticulum are reformed, etc. Crossing over occurs during meiosis
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: During cell growth, DNA synthesis takes place on
explanation: In S ­phase (synthetic phase) of cell cycle, the chromosomes replicate. For this their DNA molecules function as templates and form carbon copies. The DNA content doubles i.e., 1C to 2C for haploid cells and 2C to 4C for diploid cells. As a result duplicate sets of genes are formed. However, there is no increase in the chromosome number; if the cell had diploid or 2n number of chromosomes at G1, even after S phase the number of chromosomes remains the same, i.e., 2n. In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:163, paragraph no:4-5)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: When cell has stalled DNA replication fork, which checkpoint should be predominantly activated?[NEET 2016]
explanation: If cell has stalled DNA replication fork, it implies that it has crossed G1 or G1 cyclin cell cycle check point and has entered S­phase of cell cycle, where it is preparing for chromosome replication. Afterwards it will enter G2 phase and will soon approach second check point called mitotic cyclin (CM) which lies between G 2 and M­phase). In animal cells, during the S phase, DNA replication begins in the nucleus, and the centriole duplicates in the cytoplasm. During the G2 phase, proteins are synthesised in preparation for mitosis while cell growth continues. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:163, paragraph no:5)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 1

Metaphase I: The bivalent chromosomes align on the equatorial plate (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:168, paragraph no:2)..

question: Identify the meiotic stage in which the homologous chromosomes separate while the sister chromatids remain associated at their centromeres.[AIPMT 2012]

Thus, the homologous chromosomes of each pair, rather than the chromatids of a chromosome, are separated. As a result, half of the chromosomes, which appear in early prophase, go to each pole. Thus the paternal and maternal chromosomes of each homologous pair segregate during anaphase I independently of the other chromosomes. question: If you are provided with root­tips of onion in your class and are asked to count the chromosomes, which of the following stages can you most conveniently look into?[AIPMT 2004]
explanation: Metaphase is the best time to count and study the number and morphology of chromosomes. The distinctly visible chromosome arrange themselves at the equatorial or metaphasic plate. The centromeres lie at the equatorial plate while the limbs are placed variously according to their size and spiral arrangement. At prophase the chromosomes appear thin and filamentous, forming a network. So they are not very clearly visible. At telophase the chromosomes uncoil and lengthen and therefore are not clearly seen. Anaphase also shows chromosomes distinctly and they can be counted. But during anaphase chromatids seperate and start moving towards opposite pole. So for counting metaphase is the best stage(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:165, paragraph no:2)..

question: Which one of the following precedes reformation of the nuclear envelope during M phase of the cell cycle?[AIPMT 2004]
answer: Decondensation from chromosomes, and reassembly of the nuclear lamina
explanation: M phase or mitotic phase is the actual division phase and formation of contractile ring and formation of phragmoplast precedes reformation of nuclear envelope. Contractile ring is belt­like bundle of actin and myosin that appears during cell division immediately below the plasma membrane. Contraction of this ring leads to the separation of the two daughter cells. Phragmoplast is the region of plant cell cytoplasm that becomes evident in the latter stages of mitosis. It forms from the residual microtubules of the polar mitotic spindle and appears to function in transporting materials to the new cell plate forming between the daughter cells. Once the cell plate is complete, the phragmoplast is divided and gradually disappears, the cell plate finally becoming transformed into the middle lamella lying between the new cell walls.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:166, paragraph no:1)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Spindle fibre unite with which structure of chromosomes?[AIPMT 2000]
explanation: Spindle is microtubular apparatus that appears in many eukaryotic cells at the beginning of nuclear division and is responsible for the ordered separation of the chromosomes, chromosomes being attached to the spindle fibres by their centromeres. Two types of spindle fibres can be distinguished as the interpolar fibre, which stretches continuously from pole to pole of the spindle; the kinetochore fibre, which stretches from the pole to the centromere (kinetochore) of an individual chromosome. The mechanism by which the chromosomes move and the spindle fibres contract remains unclear. Cells of animals and lower plants possess centrioles, which act as organizer regions for spindle microtubule formation, but centrioles are absent from the cells of higher plants(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:165, paragraph no:2)..

question: In which stage of cell cycle, DNA replication occurs?[AIPMT 2000]
explanation: During S phase or synthetic phase the replication of DNA takes place. For replication of DNA histone proteins are required so they are also synthesized during this phase. It takes about 30%­ 50% of the total cell cycle. Prophase and telophase are stages involved in mitosis or meiosis. During G2 phase division of centrioles, mitochondria and chloroplasts occurs.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:163, paragraph no:4)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Microtubule is involved in the[AIPMT 1998]
explanation: Microtubules are unbranched hollow submicroscopic tubules of protein tubulin which develop on specific nucleating regions and can undergo quick growth or dissolution at their ends by assembly or disassembly of monomers. Microtubules form spindle during cell division. Centrioles help in cell division by forming spindle poles or microtubules. In animal cells, microfilament collect in the middle region of the cell below the cell membrane. They induce the cell membrane to invaginate. In plant cells, cell plate is formed to separate the two daughter cells. Some of the spindle fibres called interzonal microtubules are deposited around phragmoplast. Vesicles from Golgi apparatus are deposited and coalesce on the phragmoplast to form a cell plate.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:164, paragraph no:5)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: How many mitotic divisions are needed for a single cell to make 128 cells?[AIPMT 1997]
explanation: Mitosis is an equational division where after division each cell produces two daughter cells. So, the number of mitotic divisions can be calculated by 2^n. where, n is the number of division of cell. 2^n = 128 2^n = 2^7 n = 7 therefore after 7 divisions one cell will give 128 cells in case of mitosis. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:164, paragraph no:4)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: During cell division in apical meristem, the nuclear membrane appears in[AIPMT 1997]
explanation: This is the stage which shows the following key events: Chromosomes cluster at opposite spindle poles and their identity is lost as discrete elements; Nuclear envelope develops around the chromosome clusters at each pole forming two daughter nuclei; Nucleolus, golgi complex and ER reform.In apical meristems mitotic divisions occur at a rapid rate. In late telophase of mitosis, a nuclear membrane appears on the outside from either pieces of nuclear envelope or endoplasmic reticulum. The telophase may last as long as the prophase. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:166, paragraph no:2)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: When paternal and maternal chromosomes change their materials with each other in cell division this event is called[AIPMT 1996]
explanation: Crossing over is responsible for inducing variability. It involves an exchange of equal segments of non­sister chromatids belonging to two different but homologous chromosomes. Crossing over takes place at four stranded stage. Only two of the four chromatids take part in crossing over. The other two are called non crossovers. Zygotene is characterized by pairing of homologous chromosomes which is called synapsis. The first meiotic division which is completed at first telophase may be followed by cytokinesis giving rise to a dyad(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:168, paragraph no:2)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Which typical stage is known for DNA replication?[AIPMT 1996]
explanation: Interphase is the stage between two successive cell divisions. During interphase, chromosomes are decondensed and are distributed throughout the nucleus. It is the largest period in the cell cycle and is divided into three phases ­ G 1 , S and G 2 . During G 1 phase the cell grows and synthesis of tRNA, mRNA, ribosomes, enzymes and proteins necessary for DNA synthesis occurs. During S phase replication of DNA takes place. The nucleotides get assembled and DNA molecules are synthesized. During G 2 phase organelles like centrioles are doubled and mitochondria, chloroplasts etc. divide(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:163, paragraph no:4)..
topic_name: Cell Structure and Functions >> Cell Cycle and Division >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Which of the following represents the best stage to view the shape, size and number of chromosomes?[AIPMT 1994]

The centromeres lie at the equatorial plate while the limbs are placed variously according to their size and spiral arrangement. At prophase the chromosomes appear thin and filamentous, forming a network. So they are not very clearly visible. At telophase the chromosomes uncoil and lengthen and therefore are not clearly seen. Anaphase also shows chromosomes distinctly and they can be counted. But during anaphase chromatids seperate and start moving towards opposite pole. So for counting metaphase is the best stage(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:165,  paragraph no:2)..

question: Which statement best explains the evolutionary advantage of meiosis?[AIPMT 1994]
answer: Genetic recombinations are possible from generation to generation
explanation: Meiosis involves exchange of genes between homologous chromosomes. So the gametes produced are genetically different from each other. Offsprings produced by the fusion of gametes therefore also show recombinations or genetic variations. These variations in the offsprings make organisms more adaptable to the environment and these have a definite role in evolution.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:170, paragraph no:2)..

question: Meiosis II performs[AIPMT 1993]
