question: DNA fingerprinting refer to (2014)
answer: Molecular analysis of profiles of DNA samples
explanation: DNA fingerprinting is a technique of determining nucleotide sequences of certain areas of DNA which are unique to each individual. The difference of about 0.1% or 3 × 106 base pairs (out of 3 × 109 bp) provides individuality to each human being. Human genome possesses numerous small noncoding but inheritable sequences of bases which are repeated many times. These sequences occur near telomere, centromeres, Y chromosome and heterochromatic area. The area with same sequence of bases repeated several times is called repetitive DNA. It is separated as satellite from the bulk DNA during density gradient centrifugation and hence called satellite DNA where, repetition of bases is in tandem. Satellite DNAs show polymorphism (the occurrence of mutations in a population at high frequency), which is the basis of genetic mapping of human genome as well as DNA fingerprinting. While mutations in genes produce alleles with different expressions, mutations in non-coding repetitive DNA have no immediate impact. These mutations which have piled up with time form the basis of polymorphism.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:122, paragraph no:3)

question: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in DNA sequence, called as (NEET 2021)
explanation: DNA fingerprinting is a technique of determining nucleotide sequences of certain areas of DNA which are unique to each individual. The difference of about 0.1% or 3 × 106 base pairs (out of 3 × 109 bp) provides individuality to each human being. Human genome possesses numerous small noncoding but inheritable sequences of bases which are repeated many times. These sequences occur near telomere, centromeres, Y chromosome and heterochromatic area. The area with same sequence of bases repeated several times is called repetitive DNA. It is separated as satellite from the bulk DNA during density gradient centrifugation and hence called satellite DNA where, repetition of bases is in tandem. Satellite DNAs show polymorphism (the occurrence of mutations in a population at high frequency), which is the basis of genetic mapping of human genome as well as DNA fingerprinting. While mutations in genes produce alleles with different expressions, mutations in non-coding repetitive DNA have no immediate impact. These mutations which have piled up with time form the basis of polymorphism.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:122, paragraph no:3)

question: If Adenine makes 30% of the DNA molecule, what will be the percentage of Thymine, Guanine and Cytosine in it?  (NEET 2021)
explanation: According to Chargaff ’s rule, the amount of adenine is always equal to that of thymine and the amount of guanine is always equal to that of cytosine, i.e., A = T and G = C. Also, the purines and pyrimidines are always in equal amounts, i.e., A + G = T + C. Now, given dsDNA has 17% cytosine and hence guanine will be also 17%. So, A + T must be 66%, therefore, percentage of adenine or thymine would be 66/2 = 33%.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 12; page no:97, paragraph no:3)

question:
The salient features of genetic code are : 
 (A) The code is palindromic 
 (B) UGA act as initiator codon 
 (C) The code is unambiguous and specific 
 (D) The code is nearly universal 
 Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below : [ NEET 2023(Phase 2)]
explanation:
The salient features of the genetic code are: (C) The code is unambiguous and specific: Each codon in the genetic code corresponds to a specific amino acid or a termination signal. There is no ambiguity in the translation of codons to their corresponding amino acids. (D) The code is nearly universal: The genetic code is nearly universal, meaning that the same codons code for the same amino acids across different organisms. There are a few exceptions and variations, but the overall genetic code is highly conserved.

Option (A) is incorrect because the genetic code is not palindromic. Palindromic sequences read the same forward and backward, which is not the case for the genetic code.

Option (B) is incorrect because UGA is not an initiator codon. UGA is a termination codon, signaling the end of protein synthesis.

Therefore, the correct answer is option 4, which includes features (C) and (D) as the salient features of the genetic code.
topic_name: Genetics and Evolution >> Molecular Basis of Inheritance >> Previous Year Questions 4

options given below : [ NEET 2023(Phase 2)]
explanation: The unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material came from the experiments of Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase (1952). question: All of the following are examples of physical barriers against infections except-
explanation: Innate immunity consist of four types of barriers. These are — (i) physical barriers : skin on our body is the main barrier which prevents entry of the microorganisms. Mucus coating of the epithelium lining the respiratory, gastrointestinal and urogenital tracts also help in trapping microbes entering our body. (Ii) physiological barriers : acid in the stomach, saliva in the mouth, tears from eyes–all prevent microbial growth. (Iii) cellular barriers : certain types of leukocytes (WBC) of our body like polymorphonuclear leukocytes (PMNL-neutrophils) and monocytes and natural killer (type of lymphocytes) in the blood as well as macrophages in tissues can phagocytose and destroy microbes. (Iv) cytokine barriers : virus-infected cells secrete proteins called interferons which protect non-infected cells from further viral infection.
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Human Health and Disease >> Innate Immunity
option_b: Mucus coating of epithelial lining of organs

question: Which of the following is correct regarding AIDS causative agent HIV?[2016]

The envelope consists of a lipid bilayer derived from host cell membrane and projecting knob like glycoprotein spikes. It contains two protein coats. HIV is a retrovirus that attacks helper T cells. Without an adequate supply of helper cells, the immune system cannot signal B cells to produce antibodies to kill infected cells, thus body becomes susceptible to infections. This immune deficiency is described by the name acquired immune deficiency syndrome or AIDS.

question: If you suspect major deficiency of antibodies in a person,to which of the following would you look for confirmatory evidence?[2015]
explanation: Serum globulins are proteins that include gamma globulins (antibodies) and a variety of enzymes and carrier/ transport proteins. There are four major groups that can be identified : alpha­1 globulins, alpha­2 globulins, beta globulins and gamma globulins. Once the abnormal group has been identified, further studies can determine the specific protein excess or deficit. Since the gamma fraction usually makes up the largest portion of the globulins, therefore antibody deficiency is mainly related with the low level of serum globulins.

It is a microscopic endoparasite of man. It is commonly found in the upper part of the large intestine (colon) and is very often lodged in the liver, lungs, brain and testes. In its life cycle, it occurs in three distinct forms (i) trophozoite or magna form, (ii) precystic or minuta form, and (iii) cystic form. Trophozoite is the most active, motile and feeding form which is pathogenic to man. It lives in the mucosa and submucous layers of the colon and feeds on these layers and erythrocytes.

question: HIV that causes AIDS, first starts destroying[2015]
explanation: The AIDS retrovirus, called human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), mounts a direct attack on cd4 + t helper cells because it recognizes the cd4 coreceptors associated with these cells. HIV’s attack on cd4 + t cells cripples the immune system in at least three ways. First, HIV infected cells die only after releasing replicated viruses that infect other cd4 + t cells, until the entire population of cd4 + t cell is destroyed. Second, HIV causes infected cd4 + t cells, to secrete a soluble suppressing factor that blocks other t cells from responding to the HIV antigen. Finally, HIV may block transcription of mhc genes, hindering the recognition and destruction of infected cd4 + t cells, and thus protecting those cells from any remaining vestiges of the immune system. The combined effect of these responses to HIV infection is to wipe out the human immune defense.
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Human Health and Disease >> Previous Year Questions

question: Identify the site where wuchereria bancrofti is normally found in human body.[2013]
answer: Lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs
explanation: Wuchereria bancrofti is a dreaded human parasite. It is a digenetic parasite completing its life cycle in two hosts, the final host is man harbouring the adult worm. The disease passes through four stages in human beings: in the first stage, the patient has increased eosinophils, enlarged lymph nodes. Second or carrier stage is symptomless.Third stage is characterised by filarial fever, inflammation of lymph nodes (lymphadenitis) and lymph vessels (lymphangiectasis) and reversible lymphoedema (excess fluid in tissues due to obstruction of lymph vessels) in various body parts. The fourth or final stage is manifested by lymphoedema accompanied by thickening of subcutaneous tissues and skin so that there is permanent swelling mostly of feet, legs, thighs, scrotal sacs, breast etc. It is called elephantiasis.
topic_name: Biology In Human Welfare >> Human Health and Disease >> Previous Year Questions

option_d: Lymphatic vessels of the lower limbs

ii)The recombinants will grow in a ampicillin containing medium but not on that containing tetracycline.

iii)Non-recombinants will not grow in the medium containing both the antibiotics.

iv) Non- recombinants will grow on the medium containing both the antibiotics
explanation: For example, you can ligate a foreign DNA at the BamH I site of tetracycline resistance gene in the vector pBR322. The recombinant plasmids will lose tetracycline resistance due to insertion of foreign DNA but can still be selected out from non-recombinant ones by plating the transformants on tetracycline containing medium. The transformants growing on ampicillin containing medium are then transferred on a medium containing tetracycline. The recombinants will grow in ampicillin containing medium but not on that containing tetracycline. But, non- recombinants will grow on the medium containing both the antibiotics. In this case, one antibiotic resistance gene helps in selecting the transformants, whereas the other antibiotic resistance gene gets ‘inactivated due to insertion’ of alien DNA, and helps in selection of recombinants

In this, a recombinant DNA is inserted within the coding sequence of an enzyme, β-galactosidase. This results into inactivation of the gene for synthesis of this enzyme, which is referred to as insertional inactivation.

explanation:
The cuts made by restriction endonucleases can be only sealed DNA ligases bit however, they have asked a question with regard to restriction endonucleases, so it is not in regard to endonucleases.
Restriction enzymes are part of a larger category of enzymes known as nucleases. Exonucleases and endonucleases are the two types.
Endonucleases make cuts at specified places within the DNA, whereas exonucleases remove nucleotides off the ends.
The length of a DNA sequence is 'inspected' by each restriction endonuclease. It will connect to the DNA and cut each of the two strands of the double helix at precise spots in their sugar phosphate backbones after it has found its specific recognition sequence.
Each restriction endonuclease recognises nucleotide sequences in DNA that are palindromic.
In genetic engineering, restriction endonucleases are employed to create'recombinant' DNA molecules, which are made up of DNA from different sources/genomes.
topic_name: Biotechnology and Its Applications >> Biotechnology : Principles And Processes >> Previous Year Questions 1

(iii) Some plasmids naturally provide genetic advantage to the host cell, e.g. antibiotic resistance

(iv) Plasmids can be found exclusively in prokaryotic cells

Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?
explanation: Plasmids are naturally occuring, circular extra chromosomal DNA present in bacteria and some eukaryotes (yeast). They are capable of self replicating and cloning themselves independently of the chromosomal DNA as they have their own origin of replication. Plasmids can provide genetic advantages, e.g. by conferring antibiotic resistance, and other survival skills to the host cell. Artificial plasmids are used in molecular cloning and expression experiments, wherein a gene of interest is inserted into a plasmid along with other genes for selection (selectable markers) for the specific purpose of its expression in a host cell. In that case, plasmids are also known as vectors for cloning.

question:
Assertion: Two different DNA molecules cleaved by the same restriction enzyme can be joined together by ligase

Reason: Restriction endonucleases hydrolyze the phosphodiester bond within the polynucleotide chain
answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Restriction endonucleases are a class of enzymes that can cleave within the DNA at specific sites. Every restriction endonuclease has a specific recognition site, which is mostly palindromic in nature. Within the recognition site, the restriction endonuclease hydrolyzes* the phosphodiester bond in both the strands. Thus, even if the two DNA molecules are different, a specific restriction enzyme would cut at the same recognition site in both the DNA molecules and create DNA fragments with the same sticky ends. These sticky ends can form a double helix by complementary base pairing and are joined together by DNA ligase. (*Hydrolyzation is the process by which a water molecule is added to break a bond)

question:
Assertion: DNA fragments obtained after restriction digestion can be separated using gel electrophoresis.

Reason: The size of the DNA fragments determines their location and movements in the agarose gel upon electrophoresis.
answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: Upon restriction digestion, DNA is cut into fragments of many sizes. Upon the application of electric field, the negative charge on the DNA fragments allows them to move towards the positive electrode (anode) in a matrix commonly constituted by agarose gel. The agarose gel consists of pores of uniform size. And since the charge on every DNA fragment is roughly the same, the speed at which they migrate in the gel is determined by their size–the larger the fragment, the slower it will move through the pores. Hence, DNA fragments of different sizes are located in different positions in the gel matrix.

question:
Consider the following statements in the context of genetic engineering:

(i) Restriction endonucleases always create sticky ends after cleaving the DNA

(ii) Hydrogen bonds are formed when DNA fragments join after restriction digestion

(iii) Ligases, like endonucleases, identify palindromic sequences and join the DNA fragments together

(iv) Recombinant DNA can be formed by mixing DNA molecules with restriction endonucleases and DNA ligase

Which of the above statements is/are CORRECT?
explanation: Restriction endonucleases recognize palindromic sequences in a DNA molecule. The process in which a restriction enzyme binds to a DNA recognition site and cleaves it into fragments is referred to as restriction digestion. Many restriction enzymes cut away from the center of their recognition sites; this leads to the creation of staggering ends knowns as 'sticky ends'. However, there are many restriction endonucleases that cleave at the center of the recognition site and create blunt ends. For example, EcoRI creates sticky ends but SmaI produces blunt ends. The nitrogenous bases in the polynucleotide chain of DNA are bound together by hydrogen bonds (A and T are bound by 2 hydrogen bonds and G and C are bound by 3 hydrogen bonds). Thus, during rejoining of DNA fragments, the bases at the sticky ends rejoin via hydrogen bond formation. Unlike endonucleases, ligases rejoin the phosphdiester bonds in broken DNA fragments regardless of the sequence of bases. It is possible to create recombinant DNA by mixing different kinds of DNA with restriction enzymes and DNA ligase.
topic_name: Biotechnology and Its Applications >> Biotechnology: Principles And Processes >> Multiple statement question and Assertion Reason

question:
Two DNA samples- A and B- from two different bacterial cells. Sample A was cleaved with only EcoRI and sample B was cleaved only with HindIII. The DNA fragments obtained from the digestion were mixed together with DNA ligase. The following statements are the possible consequences of this experiment:

(i) Recombinant DNA with fragments from sample A and B would be obtained after ligase action

(ii) No recombinant DNA would be obtained because the endonucleases used for A and B are different

(iii) Recombinant DNA with fragments from sample A and B would be obtained along with the original A and B samples after ligase action

(iv) No recombinant DNA would be obtained because ligase cannot join fragments with different sticky ends.

Which of the above statements present the CORRECT consequence(s) of the experiment?
explanation: In order to yield recombinant DNA, the source DNA and the vector/host DNA must be cut by the same restriction endonuclease. This allows the creation of the same kind of staggered or sticky ends at the end, which enables joining of the fragments by complementary base pairing. Ligase rejoins the phosphodiester bond in the fragmented DNA to yield 'unbroken' recombinant DNA. Ligase enables the formation of the phosphodiester bonds regardless of the sequence of bases.Even though restriction endonucleases are specific, ligases are not specific.
topic_name: Biotechnology and Its Applications >> Biotechnology: Principles And Processes >> Multiple statement question and Assertion Reason

question:
Consider the following statements: 

(i) Gel electrophoresis can separate DNA fragments on the basis of their charge only, each fragment of DNA even if they have equal length have different charge.

(ii) Gel electrophoresis can separate DNA fragments on the basis of their mass only

(iii) Gel electrophoresis allows the visualization of DNA with naked eye

(iv) In genetic engineering, gel electrophoresis is performed before the formation of recombinant DNA

Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?
explanation: Gel electrophoresis is a technique that is utilized to separate DNA molecules of different sizes. It utilizes a gel made up of agarose onto which the DNA mixture is loaded and an electric field is applied to it. Since DNA molecules are negatively charged, they move towards the positive electrode (anode) under external electric field. The agarose gel has a particular pore size, that allows DNA molecules of certain size to move more freely than others. Since all DNA molecules have essentially the same charge, they get resolved in the gel on the basis of their size (and hence, mass)- the smaller DNA molecules move faster than the larger ones. DNA fragments resolved in such a manner are not visible by naked eye. For visualization, a dye known as ethidium bromide is added in the gel which gives orange colour to DNA when viewed under UV light. question: Which of the following statement is incorrect?
answer: Mitochondrion, a power house of cell has ds DNA, RNA, ribosomes and enzyme. so it can survive outside the cell
explanation: Mitochondria (sing.: mitochondrion), unless specifically stained, are not easily visible under the microscope. The number of mitochondria per cell is variable depending on the physiological activity of the cells. In terms of shape and size also, considerable degree of variability is observed. Typically it is sausage shaped or cylindrical having a diameter of 0.2-1.0μm (average 0.5μm) and length 1.0-4.1μm. Each mitochondrion is a double membrane-bound structure with the outer membrane and the inner membrane dividing its lumen distinctly into two aqueous compartments, i.e., the outer compartment and the inner compartment. The inner compartment is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called the matrix. The outer membrane forms the continuous limiting boundary of the organelle. The inner membrane forms a number of infoldings called the cristae (sing.: crista) towards the matrix. The cristae increase the surface area. The two membranes have their own specific enzymes associated with the mitochondrial function. Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell. The matrix also possesses single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and the components required for the synthesis of proteins. The mitochondria divide by fission.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:134, paragraph no:6).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >>  Cell Organelles

The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients: Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), e.g., potato; elaioplasts store oils and fats whereas the aleuroplasts store proteins. question: Which of the following is correct about the outer and inner membrane of chloroplast?
answer: More permeable and less permeable respectively
explanation: Like mitochondria, the chloroplasts are also double membrane bound. Of the two, the inner chloroplast membrane is relatively less permeable. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:136, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >>  Cell Organelles

question: Grana of the chloroplast are interconnected by -
explanation: Like mitochondria, the chloroplasts are also double membrane bound. Of the two, the inner chloroplast membrane is relatively less permeable. The space limited by the inner membrane of the chloroplast is called the stroma. A number of organised flattened membranous sacs called the thylakoids, are present in the stroma. Thylakoids are arranged in stacks like the piles of coins called grana (singular: granum) or the intergranal thylakoids. In addition, there are flat membranous tubules called the stroma lamellae connecting the thylakoids of the different grana. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:136, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >>  Cell Organelles

question: Which of the following is not membraneless?
explanation:
All are membraneless. Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953). They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:136, paragraph no:2)
The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm as it is not a membrane bound structure. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:138, paragraph no:3)
Electron microscopy has revealed that the nuclear envelope, which consists of two parallel membranes with a space between (10 to 50 nm) called the perinuclear space, forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:138, paragraph no:2) diagram (e0814)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >>  Cell Organelles

question: The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of
explanation: The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:136, paragraph no:1)

question: "These are lens-shaped, oval, spherical, discoid or even ribbon-like organelles having variable length (5-10μm) and width (2-4μm)" is a statement about which of the following?
explanation: Majority of the chloroplasts of the green plants are found in the mesophyll cells of the leaves. These are lens-shaped, oval, spherical, discoid or even ribbon like organelles having variable length (5-10μm) and width (2-4μm). Their number varies from 1 per cell of the Chlamydomonas, a green alga to 20-40 per cell in the mesophyll. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:1)

question: The central tubules in the axoneme of cilia and flagella are connected by bridges and is also enclosed by a central sheath, which is connected to one of the tubules of each peripheral doublets by a  _____________. Fill in the blank.
explanation: The central tubules in the axoneme of cilia and flagella are connected by bridges and is also enclosed by a central sheath, which is connected to one of the tubules of each peripheral doublets by a radial spoke. Thus, there are nine radial spokes. The peripheral doublets are also interconnected by linkers. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:137, paragraph no:2)

question: An organelle with an internal cross section showing characteristic "9 + 2" morphology is the -

The axoneme usually has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules. Such an arrangement of axonemal microtubules is referred to as the 9+2 array.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:137, paragraph no:2) diagram (e0815)

question: Choose the correct statement about cilia and flagella.
answer: They are hair-like outgrowths of the cell membrane
explanation: Cilia (sing.: cilium) and flagella (sing.: flagellum) are hair-like outgrowths of the cell membrane. Cilia are small structures which work like oars, causing the movement of either the cell or the surrounding fluid. Flagella are comparatively longer and responsible for cell movement. The prokaryotic bacteria also possess flagella but these are structurally different from that of the eukaryotic flagella.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:137, paragraph no:1)

question:

i) An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures.
ii) Consisting of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm

question: Which one is correct about the nuclear membranes (nms)
answer: Both nms are parallel to each other and fused to form nuclear pores at a number of places
explanation: Electron microscopy has revealed that the nuclear envelope, which consists of two parallel membranes with a space between (10 to 50 nm) called the perinuclear space, forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm.The outer membrane usually remains continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum and also bears ribosomes on it. At a number of places the nuclear envelope is interrupted by minute pores, which are formed by the fusion of its two membranes. These nuclear pores are the passages through which movement of RNA and protein molecules takes place in both directions between the nucleus and the cytoplasm. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:38, paragraph no:2)

question: Structure which provides the shape to chromosomes is called -
explanation: Every chromosome (visible only in dividing cells) essentially has a primary constriction or the centromere on the sides of which disc shaped structures called kinetochores are present . Centromere holds two chromatids of a chromosome. Based on the position of the centromere, the chromosomes can be classified into four types. The metacentric chromosome has middle centromere forming two equal arms of the chromosome. The sub metacentric chromosome has centromere slightly away from the middle of the chromosome resulting into one shorter arm and one longer arm. In case of acrocentric chromosome the centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm, whereas the telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:139, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Nucleus

question: Which of the following is the smallest cell?
explanation: Cells differ greatly in size, shape and activities. For example, Mycoplasmas, the smallest cells, are only 0.3 μm in length while bacteria could be 3 to 5 μm. The largest isolated single cell is the egg of an ostrich. Among multicellular organisms, human red blood cells are about 7.0 μm in diameter. Nerve cells are some of the longest cells. Cells also vary greatly in their shape. They may be disc-like, polygonal, columnar, cuboid, thread like, or even irregular. The shape of the cell may vary with the function they perform. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:126, paragraph no:6)

question: Which of the following cell organelles is responsible for extracting energy from carbohydrates to form atp? [NEET 2017]
explanation: Mitochondria are miniature biochemical factories where food stuffs or respiratory substrates are completely oxidised to  CO₂  and water. The energy liberated in the process is initially stored in the form of reduced coenzymes and reduced prosthetic groups. The latter soon undergo oxidation and form energy rich ATP. ATP comes out of mitochondria and helps perform various energy requiring processes of the cell like muscle contraction, nerve impulse conduction, biosynthesis, membrane transport, cell division, movement, etc. Because of the formation of ATP, the mitochondria are called power houses of the cell. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:135, paragraph no:1).

explanation: Pili and fimbriae are bacterial appendages which are not involved in locomotion. Actually, pili are long fewer and thicker tubular outgrowths which develop in response to F + or fertility factor in Gram negative bacteria. Being long they are helpful in attaching to recipient cell and forming conjugation tube. Fimbriae are small bristlelike fibres sprouting from cell surface in large number. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:129, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Bacterial cell wall is made up of peptidoglycan.
option_b: Pili and fimbriae are mainly involved in motility of bacterial cells.

question: A cell organelle containing hydrolytic enzymes is [NEET 2016]
explanation: Lysosomes are small vesicles which are bounded by a single membrane and contain hydrolytic enzymes in the form of minute crystalline or semicrystalline granules of  protein. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:134, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question:
Mitochondria and chloroplast are 

i)Semiautonomous organelles
ii)Formed by division of preexisting organelles and they contain DNA but lack protein synthesising machinery.

Which one of the following options is correct? 
[NEET 2016]
answer: i is true but ii is false.
explanation: Both mitochondria and chloroplast are semiautonomous organelles. They have their own DNA which produces its own, mRNA, tRNA and rRNA. These organelles also possess their own ribosomes and hence are able to synthesise some of their proteins.

option_a: i is true but ii is false.
option_b: Both i and ii are false.

question: Microtubules are the constituents of [NEET 2016]
explanation: Microtubules are unbranched hollow submicroscopic tubules of protein tubulin which develop on specific nucleating regions. It can undergo quick growth or dissolution at their ends by assembly or disassembly of monomers. They are present in the cytoplasm as well as in specialised structures like centrioles, basal bodies, cilia or flagella, sensory hair, equatorial ring of thrombocytes, spindle apparatus, chromosome fibres, nerve processes, sperm tails, axostyle of parasitic flagellates, fibre system of Stentor, cytopharyngeal basket of Nassula, etc. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following cell organelles is enclosed by a single membrane? [NEET 2016]
explanation: Lysosomes are small vesicles bounded by a single membrane and contain hydrolytic enzymes. Nucleus, mitochondria and chloroplasts are double membrane bound cells organelles. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:134, paragraph no:2).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following structures is not found in a prokaryotic cell? [AIPMT 2015]
explanation: A prokaryotic cell is characterised by absence of an organised nucleus and membrane bound cell organelles. DNA is naked i.e., without a nuclear envelope and lies variously coiled in the cytoplasm. It is commonly called nucleoid or genophore. Mesosomes, plasma membrane and ribosomes are found(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:128, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Cellular organelles with membranes are [AIPMT 2015]
explanation: Endoplasmic reticulum, nuclei, lysosomes, Golgi apparatus and mitochondria are membrane bound cell organelles whereas ribosomes are naked ribonucleoprotein protoplasmic particles. Chromosomes are the hereditary particles present in the nucleus(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:129, paragraph no:5).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following are not membrane bound? [AIPMT 2015]
explanation: Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953). They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and are not surrounded by any membrane. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:2).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Dna is not present in [2015 cancelled]
explanation: Ribosome is a small spherical body within a living cell that is the site of protein synthesis. Ribosomes consist of two subunits, one large and one small, each of which comprises some RNA (called ribosomal RNA) and protein. They do not have any DNA(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:129, paragraph no:4).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Nuclear envelope is a derivative of (2015 cancelled)
explanation: Recent developments have shown that nuclear membrane is derived from rough endoplasmic reticulum. During cell division, nuclear membrane is disintegrated. The nuclear envelope transmembrane proteins are absorbed in the RER. Once the division is completed, RER reassembles the nuclear envelope. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:133, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The structures that are formed by stacking of organised flattened membranous sacs in the chloroplasts are [2015 cancelled]
explanation: A chloroplast is a vesicle, bound by an envelope of two unit membranes and filled with a fluid matrix called stroma. The lamellae, after separation from the inner membrane, usually take the form of closed, flattened, ovoid sacs, the thylakoids, which lie closely packed in piles, the grana. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

It forms a link between the cell and nuclear membranes. It is the site of important metabolic reactions, including phospholipid and fatty acid synthesis. question: The chromosomes in which centromere is situated close to one end are [2015 cancelled]
explanation: Centromere is a part of a chromosome that attaches to the spindle during cell division. A chromosome with the centromere close to one end is acrocentric. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:139, paragraph no:2).

question: The solid linear cytoskeletal elements having a diameter of 6 nm and made up of a single type of monomer are known as [AIPMT 2014]
explanation: Micrfilaments are solid microscopic linear cytoskeleton elements with an external diameter of 6 nm(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The osmotic expansion of a cell kept in water is chiefly regulated by [AIPMT 2014]
explanation: Vacuoles are non cytoplasmic areas present inside cytoplasm and separated from latter by tonoplast. They are believed to be formed by expansion and pinching off from ER. There occurs a large central vacuole and many small vacuoles in plant cells. They play a major role in osmotic expansion of cell. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:134, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The golgi complex plays a major role [NEET 2013]
answer: In post translational modification of proteins and glycosylation of lipids
explanation: Post translational modification (PTM) is a step in protein biosynthesis. Proteins are created on ribosomes translating mRNA into polypeptide chains. These polypeptide chains undergo PTM, such as folding, cutting and other processes, before becoming the mature protein product. Proteins synthesized by the rough endoplasmic reticulum and lipids synthesized by smooth endoplasmic reticulum reach the cisternae of the Golgi apparatus. Here, they combine with carbohydrates to form glycoproteins and glycolipids. This process is called glycosylation. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:134, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_b: In post translational modification of proteins and glycosylation of lipids
option_c: In trapping the light and transforming it into chemical energy

It forms a link between the cell and nuclear membranes. It is the site of important metabolic reactions, including phospholipid and fatty acid synthesis. question: The term ‘glycocalyx’ is used for [Karnataka neet 2013]
answer: A layer surrounding the cell wall of bacteria
explanation: Glycocalyx is a sticky, gelatinous material that collects outside the cell wall of bacteria to form an additional surface layer. When this layer is firmly attached to the surface of the cell, it is called a capsule. If it is loosely distributed around the cell, the glycocalyx is called a slime layer. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:128, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: A layer present between cell wall and membrane of bacteria
option_c: Bacterial cell glycoengineered to possess nglycosylated proteins
option_d: A layer surrounding the cell wall of bacteria

question: Which of the following types of plastid does not contain stored food material? [Karnataka neet 2013]
explanation: Chromoplasts are yellow or reddish in colour because of the presence of carotenoid pigments. They do not contain stored food material. Chromoplasts are formed either from leucoplasts or chloroplasts. Chromoplasts provide colour to many flowers for attracting pollinating insects. They provide bright red or orange colour to fruits for attracting animals for dispersal.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:135, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following best illustrates “feedback” in development? [Karnataka neet 2013]
answer: As tissue x develops, it secretes something that induces tissue y to develop.
explanation: As tissue X develops it secretes something that induces tissue Y to develop indicating positive feedback mechanism.

question: Which one of the following does not differ in e.coli and chlamydomonas? [AIPMT 2012]
explanation: E.coli (bacteria) is a prokaryote while Chlamydomonas (algae) is a eukaryote. Ribosomes of both groups differ being  70s and 80s

question: Which one of the following cellular parts is correctly described? [AIPMT Mains 2012]
answer: Thylakoids flattened membranous sacs forming the grana of chloroplasts
explanation: Thylakoid are the flattened saclike membranous structures that are stacked on top of one another to form the grana of plant chloroplast. Chlorophyll and other photosynthetic pigments are situated in the thylakoid membranes, which are the site for the lightdependent reactions of photosynthesis. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following structures is an organelle within an organelle? [AIPMT Mains 2012]
explanation: Ribosomes occur in all living cells except mammalian erythrocytes or red blood corpuscles. Depending upon the place of their occurrence, ribosomes are of two types–cytoplasmic ribosomes and organelle ribosomes. The cytoplasmic ribosomes (cytoribosomes) may remain free in the cytoplasmic matrix or attached to the cytosolic surface of endoplasmic reticulum with the help of special ribophorin or SRP protein. The organelle ribosomes are found in plastids (plastiribosomes) and mitochondria (mitoribosomes) Cytoplasmic ribosome are of eighty S type in eukaryotic cell whereas organelle ribosomes are of seventyS type. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:2).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Peptide synthesis inside a cell takes place in [AIPMT 2011]
explanation: Peptide synthesis inside a cell takes place in ribosome. Ribosomes are found in all cells and are involved in protein synthesis. The major constituents of ribosomes are RNA and proteins present in approximately equal amounts.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:2).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Important site for formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids is [AIPMT 2011]
explanation: Eukaryotic cells contain a unique cluster of membrane vesicles known as Golgi apparatus. It principally performs the function of packaging materials. The newly synthesized proteins are handed over to the Golgi apparatus which is catalysed by the addition of carbohydrates, lipid or sulphates moieties to the proteins. Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:134, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following is not considered as a part of the endomembrane system? [AIPMTMains 2011]
explanation: While each of the membranous organelles is distinct in terms of its structure and function, many of these are considered together as an endomembrane system because their functions are coordinated. The endomembrane system include endoplasmic reticulum (ER), Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Since the functions of the mitochondria, chloroplast and peroxisomes are not coordinated with the above components, these are not considered as part of the endomembrane system(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:133, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The plasma membrane consists mainly of [AIPMT 2010]
answer: Proteins embedded in a phospholipid bilayer
explanation: Plasma membrane consists of lipids, proteins, carbohydrates and water. Lipid molecules possess both hydrophobic and hydrophilic ends and are thus arranged in the form of lipid bilayer. Most common lipid of the bilayer is phospholipid. Protein molecules occur at places both inside (intrinsic proteins) and on the outer side (extrinsic proteins) of the phospholipid bilayer.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:131, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Phospholipids embedded in a protein bilayer
option_b: Proteins embedded in a phospholipid bilayer
option_c: Proteins embedded in a polymer of glucose molecules
option_d: Proteins embedded in a carbohydrate bilayer

question: The main area of various types of activities of a cell is [AIPMT 2010]
explanation: Cytoplasm is granular, crystallocolloidal complex that forms the living protoplasm of a cell excluding its nucleus. It consists of proteins, nucleic acids, fats, carbohydrates, vitamins, minerals, waste metabolites, and all the organelles. It is the main area for various types of activities of a cell like respiration, nutrition, storage, etc.
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following has its own dna? [AIPMT 2010]
explanation: Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell. The matrix also possesses single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and the components required for the synthesis of proteins. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:135, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following structures between two adjacent cells is an effective transport pathway? [AIPMT 2010]
explanation: Plasmodesmata are fine cytoplasmic strands that connect the protoplasts of adjacent plant cells by passing through their cell walls. Plasmodesmata are cylindrical in shape(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:132, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures present in the cytoplasm which helps in the maintenance of cell shape is called
explanation: An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures consisting of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton. The cytoskeleton in a cell are involved in many functions such as mechanical support, motility, maintenance of the shape of the cell. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Middle lamella is composed mainly of [AIPMT 2009]
explanation: Middle lamella of cell wall is composed of calcium and magnesium pectate. It joins the adjoining cells together and thus acts as a cementing layer. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:132, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Cytoskeleton is made up of [AIPMT 2009]
explanation: The ability of eukaryotic cells to adopt a variety of shapes and to carry out coordinated and directed movements depends on the cytoskeleton. The main proteins that are present in the cytoskeleton are tubulin (in the microtubules), actin, myosin, tropomyosin and other (in the microfilaments) and keratins, vimentin, desmin,lamin and other (in intermediate filaments)(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:4).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Plasmodesmata are [AIPMT 2009]
explanation: The cell wall and middle lamellae may be traversed by plasmodesmata which connect the cytoplasm of neighbouring cells. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:132, paragraph no:5).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_b: Membranes connecting the nucleus with plasmalemma

question: In germinating seeds fatty acids are degraded exclusively in the [AIPMT 2008]
explanation: Glyoxysomes are small, spherical vesicles enclosed by a single unit membrane. Glyoxysomes are generally found in cells of yeast, Neurospora and in germinating fatty seeds where fat is being converted into carbohydrates, i.e., glyoxylate cycle (gluconeogenesis).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Vacuole in a plant cell [AIPMT 2008]
answer: Is membranebound and contains water and excretory substances
explanation: In a plant cell, vacuole may be defined as a nonliving reservoir, bounded by a differentially or selectively permeable membrane, the tonoplast. It is filled with a highly concentrated solution called vascular sap or cell sap which contains many dissolved solutes such as organic acids, soluble carbohydrates, soluble nitrogenous compounds as nitrates, enzyme, tannins, chlorides, phosphates, amino acids, alkaloids and anthocyanin pigments.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:134, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_b: Lacks membrane and contains water and excretory substances
option_c: Is membranebound and contains storage proteins and lipids
option_d: Is membranebound and contains water and excretory substances

question: The two subunits of ribosome remain united at a critical ion level of [AIPMT 2008]
explanation: Ribosomes are very small organelles having a diameter in nanometers range

question: Keeping in view the ‘fluid mosaic model‘ for the structure of cell membrane, which one of he following statement is correct with respect to the movements of lipids and proteins from one lipid monolayer to the other (described as flipflop movement)? [AIPMT 2008]
answer: While lipids can rarely flipflop, proteins cannot
explanation: According to fluid mosaic model there is rapid internal motion involving flexing within each lipid molecule a rapid lateral diffusion of the lipids is possible and a slow ‘flipflop’ motion, i.e., a transfer of lipid molecules from one side of the bilayer to the other, is also possible. The lipid molecules might also rotate about their axes. The proteins of the membrane are concerned with the enzymatic activity of the membrane, with transport of molecules, and with a receptor function whereas, the lipid bilayer provides the permeability barrier
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: While proteins can flipflop, lipids can not
option_b: Neither lipids, nor proteins can flipflop
option_c: Both lipids and proteins can flipflop
option_d: While lipids can rarely flipflop, proteins cannot

question: Which one of the following is not a constituent of cell membrane? [AIPMT 2007]
explanation: Studies showed that the cell membrane is mainly composed of lipids and proteins. The major lipids are phospholipids that are arranged in a bilayer. Also, the lipids are arranged within the membrane with the polar head towards the outer sides and the hydrophobic tails towards the inner part.This ensures that the nonpolar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment (Figure 8.4). In addition to phospholipids membrane also contains cholesterol. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:131, paragraph no:2).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

answer: Both chloroplasts and mitochondria have an internal compartment, the thylakoid space bounded by the thylakoid membrane.

question: Biological organisation starts with [AIPMT 2007]
explanation: Molecular assemblies are large organised sets of molecular units that make up parts of organelles. For example, one common macromolecular assembly is the microtubule which is important in forming structure in the cell related to maintaining the cell structure or related to cell movement. The cell (plasma) membrane that surrounds many organelles and the cell is a highly organised molecular assembly.
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following statements regarding mitochondrial membrane is not correct ? [AIPMT 2006]
answer: The enzymes of the electron transfer chain are embedded in the outer membrane.
explanation: The outer membrane of mitochondrion is smooth, freely permeable to most small molecules, contains fewer enzymes and is poor in proteins. It has porin proteins which form channels for the passage of molecules through it. It allows uptake of substrates and release of ATP. The inner membrane is semipermeable and regulates the passage of materials into and out of the mitochondrion. It is rich in enzymes and carrier proteins (permeases). It is usually produced into numerous infolds called cristae (singular crista). It bears minute regularly spaced lollipopshaped particles known as oxysomes. The rest of the inner membrane contains the electron carrier molecules of the electron transport chain.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:135, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: The outer membrane resembles a sieve.
option_b: The outer membrane is permeable to all kinds of molecules.
option_c: The enzymes of the electron transfer chain are embedded in the outer membrane.
option_d: The inner membrane is highly convoluted forming a series of infoldings

question: Which of the following statements regarding cilia is not correct ? [AIPMT 2006]
answer: The organized beating of cilia is controlled by fluxes of ca 2+ across the membrane.
explanation: Cilia are fine hair like vibratile, cytoplasmic processes borne by certain cell types. Their movement either propel the organism or move the medium past a fixed cell. The cilia are enclosed by a unit membrane which is an extension of the plasma membrane of the cell. Within the membrane, is a fluid matrix having a supporting axial shaft, or axoneme. The microtubules, single as well as double, are composed of the globular units of the protein tubulin. The arms of A microtubules contain a protein dynein. The latter is ATPase enzyme which catalyzes hydrolysis of ATP to ADP, and transfers the free energy released direct to ciliary work. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:137, paragraph no:1-2).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Cilia contain an outer ring of nine doublet microtubules surrounding two singlet microtubules.
option_b: The organized beating of cilia is controlled by fluxes of ca 2+ across the membrane.
option_d: Microtubules of cilia are composed of tubulin

question: A major breakthrough in the studies of cells came with the development of electron microscope. this is because [AIPMT 2006]
answer: The resolving power of the electron microscope is much higher than that of the light microscope
explanation: Microscopes are used for studying cellular structures. They are used to magnify small objects. In electron microscopes, a high energy beam of electrons is focused through electromagnetic lenses. It can magnify very small details with high resolving power. The increased resolution results from the shorter wavelength of the electron beam.

question: Chlorophyll in chloroplasts is located in [AIPMT 2005]
explanation: Like mitochondria, the chloroplasts are also double membrane bound. Of the two, the inner chloroplast membrane is relatively less permeable. The space limited by the inner membrane of the chloroplast is called the stroma. A number of organised flattened membranous sacs called the thylakoids, are present in the stroma (Figure 8.8). Thylakoids are arranged in stacks like the piles of coins called grana (singular: granum) or the intergranal thylakoids. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:136, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: A student wishes to study the cell structure under a light microscope having 10x eyepiece and 45x objective. he should illuminate the object by which one of the following colours of light so as to get the best possible resolution? [AIPMT 2005]
explanation: Resolution of microscope is inversely proportional to wavelength of light used. Out of four options given, blue light has minimum wavelength and hence maximum resolution.
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: According to widely accepted “fluid mosaic model” cell membranes are semifluid, where lipids and integral proteins can diffuse randomly. in recent years, this model has been modified in several respects. in this regard, which of the following statements is incorrect? [AIPMT 2005]
answer: Proteins can also undergo flipflop movements in the lipid bilayer.
explanation: According to this, the quasi-fluid nature of lipid enables lateral movement of proteins within the overall bilayer. This ability to move within the membrane is measured as its fluidity.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:132, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Questions 1

option_b: Proteins can also undergo flipflop movements in the lipid bilayer.

question: Centromere is required for [AIPMT 2005]
explanation: Centromere is the point at which the two chromatids of a chromosome are held together. During movement of chromosomes, the spindle fibres (on which the chromatids move) are attached to the centromere. Crossing over involves physical exchange of genetic material between nonsister chromatids of homologous chromosomes. Cytoplasmic cleavage is the division of cytoplasm. Transcription is the process in which the genetic information of DNA is transferred to mRNA as the first step in protein synthesis. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:138, paragraph no:1).

question: Chemiosmotic theory of ATP synthesis in the chloroplasts and mitochondria is based on [AIPMT 2005]
explanation: Chemiosmotic coupling hypothesis is the most widely accepted explanation for oxidative phosphorylation in mitochondria and photophosphorylation in thylakoid membranes. Mitchell proposed the idea of chemiosmotic coupling. He suggested that a concentration gradient of protons is established across the mitochondrial membrane because there is an accumulation of hydrogen ions on one side of the mitochondrial membrane. The proton accumulation is necessary for energy transfer to the endergonic ADP phosphorylation process.

question: The main organelle involved in modification and outing of newly synthesized proteins to their destinations is [AIPMT 2005]

question: The telomeres of eukaryotic chromosomes consist of short sequences of [AIPMT 2004]

question: Function of telomeres in nucleus is [AIPMT 2000]

The sub metacentric chromosome has centromere slightly away from the middle of the chromosome resulting into one shorter arm and one longer arm. question: Active and passive transports across cell membrane differ in [AIPMT 1993]
answer: Passive transport is along the concentration gradient while active transport is due to metabolic energy
explanation: Many molecules can move briefly across the membrane without any requirement of energy and this is called the passive transport. Neutral solutes may move across the membrane by the process of simple diffusion along the concentration gradient, i.e., from higher concentration to the lower. Water may also move across this membrane from higher to lower concentration. Movement of water by diffusion is called osmosis. As the polar molecules cannot pass through the nonpolar lipid bilayer, they require a carrier protein of the membrane to facilitate their transport across the membrane. A few ions or molecules are transported across the membrane against their concentration gradient, i.e., from lower to the higher concentration. Such a transport is an energy dependent process, in which ATP is utilised and is called active transport, e.g., Na+/K+ Pump. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:132, paragraph no:3).

question: Three morphological forms of golgi complex are
explanation:
Camillo Golgi (1898) first observed densely stained reticular structures near the nucleus. These were later named Golgi bodies after him. They consist of many flat, disc-shaped sacs or cisternae of 0.5μm to 1.0μm diameter (Figure 8.6). These are stacked parallel to each other. Varied number of cisternae are present in a Golgi complex. The Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with distinct convex cis or the forming face and concave trans or the maturing face. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:133, paragraph no:5).
The cis and the trans faces of the organelle are entirely different, but interconnected. The golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face. This explains, why the golgi apparatus remains in close association with the endoplasmic reticulum. A number of proteins synthesised by ribosomes on the endoplasmic reticulum are modified in the cisternae of the golgi apparatus before they are released from its trans face. Golgi apparatus is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no:134, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Previous Year Aiims Questions
