4. His analysis of the allowed conformations of proteins through the use of the ‘Schleiden plot’ rank among the most outstanding contributions in structural biology.
explanation:
G.N. RAMACHANDRAN, an outstanding figure in the field of protein structure, was the founder of the ‘Madras school’ of conformational analysis of biopolymers. His discovery of the triple helical structure of collagen published in Nature in 1954 and his analysis of the allowed conformations of proteins through the use of the ‘Ramachandran plot’ rank among the most outstanding contributions in structural biology.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:124, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding G.N. RAMACHANDRAN and choose the correct option:

1. While at Cambridge, Ramachandran met Rudolf Virchow and was deeply influenced by his publications on models of the α-helix and β-sheet structures.

2. He received a Ph.D. from Cambridge University in 1949.

3. He discovered the double helical structure of collagen.

4. Ramachandran graduated in 1942 as the top-ranking student in the B.Sc. (Honors) Physics course of the University of Madras.
explanation:
Ramachandran graduated in 1942 as the top-ranking student in the B.Sc. (Honors) Physics course of the University of Madras. He received a Ph.D. from Cambridge University in 1949. While at Cambridge, Ramachandran met Linus Pauling and was deeply influenced by his publications on
models of the α-helix and β-sheet structures that directed his attention to solving the structure of collagen.
His discovery of the triple helical structure of collagen published in Nature in 1954 and his
analysis of the allowed conformations of proteins through the use of the ‘Ramachandran plot’ rank among the most outstanding contributions in structural biology.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:124, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell and choose the correct option:

1. Some organisms may not comprise of cells but still are alive.

2. Some are composed of a single cell and are called unicellular organisms 

3. Organisms composed of many cells, are called multicellular organisms.

4. DNA is the is the basic unit of life
explanation:
‘what is it that makes an organism living, or what is it that an inanimate thing does not have which
a living thing has’? 
The answer to this is the presence of the basic unit of life – the cell in all living organisms. All organisms are composed of cells. Some are composed of a single
cell and are called unicellular organisms while others, like us, composed
of many cells, are called multicellular organisms. Cell is the basic unit of life
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:125, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following Assertion and reason and choose the correct option:

Assertion: All organisms are composed of cells

Reason: Some are composed of a single cell and are called unicellular organisms while others are composedof many cells, are called multicellular organisms.
answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation:
Cell is the basic unit of life. It is the basic unit that performs each and every function in a living organism. hence all organisms are composed of cells.
 Some are composed of a single cell and are called unicellular organisms while others are composedof many cells, are called multicellular organisms.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:125, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions
option_a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_b: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_c: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_d: Both Assertion and Reason are false.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell and choose the correct option:

1. Unicellular organisms are always dependent on other for their baisc function.

2. Unicellular organisms are capable of performing the essential functions of life. 

3. Anything less than a complete structure of a cell does not ensure independent living. 

4. Cell is the fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms.
explanation:
Unicellular organisms are capable of (i) independent existence and
(ii) performing the essential functions of life. Anything less than a complete
structure of a cell does not ensure independent living. Hence, cell is the
fundamental structural and functional unit of all living organisms.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:125, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell and choose the correct option:

1. Robert Brown saw and described a live cell.

2. Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first discovered the nucleus.

3. The invention of the microscope and its improvement leading to the electron microscope revealed all the structural details of the cell.

4. Matthias Schleiden was an European botanist,
explanation:
Anton Von Leeuwenhoek first saw and described a live cell. Robert
Brown later discovered the nucleus. The invention of the microscope and
its improvement leading to the electron microscope revealed all the
structural details of the cell.
In 1838, Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist, examined a large number
of plants and observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of
cells which form the tissues of the plant.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:125, paragraph no: 3, 4)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell theory and choose the correct option:

1. Matthias Schleiden was a German botanist,

2. In 1938, Matthias Schleiden examined a large number of plants and observed cell wall

3. Theodore Schwann was an American Zoologist

4. Theodore Schwann, studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the ‘plasma membrane’.
explanation:
In 1838, Matthias Schleiden, a German botanist, examined a large number
of plants and observed that all plants are composed of different kinds of
cells which form the tissues of the plant. 
(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:125, paragraph no: 4)

At about the same time, Theodore Schwann (1839), a British Zoologist, studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the
‘plasma membrane’.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:126, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding Theodore Schwann and choose the correct option:

1. Schwann was a British Zoologist, studied different types of animal cells and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the ‘plasma membrane’. 

2. He also studied on plant tissues, and concluded that the presence of cell wall is a unique character of the plant cells. 

3. Schwann proposed the hypothesis that the bodies of animals and plants are composed of cells and products of cells.

4. He also first explained that cells are divided and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells.
explanation:
Schwann (1839), a British Zoologist, studied different types of animal cells
and reported that cells had a thin outer layer which is today known as the
‘plasma membrane’. He also concluded, based on his studies on plant
tissues, that the presence of cell wall is a unique character of the plant
cells. On the basis of this, Schwann proposed the hypothesis that the bodies
of animals and plants are composed of cells and products of cells.
Rudolf Virchow (1855) first explained that cells divided and new cells are formed from
pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula).
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:126, paragraph no: 1, 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell theory and choose the correct option:

1. Schleiden and Schwann together formulated the cell theory. 

2. Schleiden and Schwann together explained as to how new cells were formed. 

3. Rudolf Virchow (1855) first explained that cells divided and new cells are formed from pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula). 

4. The modified Cell theory concludes: all living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells only
explanation:
Schleiden and Schwann together formulated the cell theory. This theory
however, did not explain as to how new cells were formed. Rudolf Virchow
(1855) first explained that cells divided and new cells are formed from
pre-existing cells (Omnis cellula-e cellula). He modified the hypothesis of
Schleiden and Schwann to give the cell theory a final shape. Cell theory
as understood today is:
(i) all living organisms are composed of cells and products of cells.
(ii) all cells arise from pre-existing cells.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:126, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell and choose the correct option:

1. The onion cell which is a typical plant cell, has a distinct outermost boundary called cell membrane. 

2. The cells of the human cheek have an outer membrane as the delimiting structure of the cell.

3. Inside each cell is a dense membrane bound structure called ribosome that helps in protien synthesis.

4. The nucleus contains the chromosomes which in turn contain the genetic material, DNA.
explanation:
The onion cell which is a typical plant cell, has a distinct cell wall as its outer boundary and just within it is the cell membrane.  (ribosomes are membraneless structure)The cells of the human cheek have an outer membrane as the delimiting structure of the cell. Inside each cell is a dense membrane bound structure called nucleus. This nucleus contains the chromosomes which in turn contain the genetic material, DNA.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:126, paragraph no: 3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell and choose the correct option:

1. Cells that have membrane bound nuclei are called eukaryotic cells

2. Cells that lack a membrane bound nucleus are prokaryotic cells 

3. Only eukaryotic cells have a semi-fluid matrix called cytoplasm.

4. The cytoplasm is the main arena of cellular activities in both the plant and animal cells.
explanation:
Cells that have membrane bound nuclei are called eukaryotic whereas cells that lack a membrane bound nucleus are prokaryotic. In both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, a semi-fluid matrix
called cytoplasm occupies the volume of the cell. The cytoplasm is the main arena of cellular activities in both the plant and animal cells.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:126, paragraph no: 3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell and choose the correct option:

1. Various chemical reactions occur in the cytoplasm to keep the cell in the ‘living state’.

2. The eukaryotic cells have other membrane bound organelles 

3. Organelles that are membrane bound are endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the golgi complex, lysosomes, ribosomes, mitochondria, microbodies and vacuoles.

4. Some prokaryotic cells have membrane bound organelles like lysosomes and vacuole
explanation:
Various chemical reactions occur in cytoplasm to keep the cell in the ‘living state’.
Besides the nucleus, the eukaryotic cells have other membrane bound distinct structures called organelles like the endoplasmic reticulum (ER), the golgi complex, lysosomes, mitochondria, microbodies and vacuoles.
The prokaryotic cells lack such membrane bound organelles. Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells – both eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:126, paragraph no: 3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell and choose the correct option:

1. Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells –both eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic. 

2. Within the cell, ribosomes are found not only in the cytoplasm but also within the two organelles – chloroplasts (in plants) and mitochondria and on rough ER.

3. Centrosome is present in plant cell only 

4. Centrosomes help in protein and enzyme synthesis that is vital for a cell to perform its functions
explanation:
Ribosomes are non-membrane bound organelles found in all cells –both eukaryotic as well as prokaryotic. Within the cell, ribosomes are found not only in the cytoplasm but also within the two organelles – chloroplasts (in plants) and mitochondria and on rough ER.
Animal cells contain another non-membrane bound organelle called centrosome which helps in cell division.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:126, paragraph no: 4)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell and choose the correct option:

1. Mycoplasmas, the smallest cells, are only 1.3 μm in length. 

2. The largest isolated single cell is the egg of an ostrich.

3. Human red blood cells are about 7.0 μm in diameter. 

4. Nerve cells are some of the longest cells.
explanation:
Mycoplasmas, the smallest cells, are only 0.3 μm in length while bacteria could be 3 to 5 μm. The largest isolated single cell is the egg of an ostrich. Among multicellular organisms, human red blood cells are about 7.0 μm in diameter. Nerve cells are some of the longest cells. Cells also vary greatly in their shape.


(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:127, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. The prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae, mycoplasma and PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms). 

2. They are generally smaller and multiply slower than the eukaryotic cells

3. They may vary greatly in shape and size. 

4. The two basic shapes of bacteria are bacillus (rod like) and  coccus (spherical) only
explanation:
The prokaryotic cells are represented by bacteria, blue-green algae, mycoplasma and PPLO (Pleuro Pneumonia Like Organisms). They are
generally smaller and multiply more rapidly than the eukaryotic cells (Figure 8.2). They may vary greatly in shape and size. The four basic
shapes of bacteria are bacillus (rod like), coccus (spherical), vibrio (comma shaped) and spirillum (spiral).

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:127, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. All the prokaryotic cells including mycoplasma have a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane.

2. The fluid matrix filling the cell is the cytoplasm.

3. There is well-defined nucleus. 

4. The genetic material is basically naked, not enveloped by a nuclear membrane.
explanation:
All prokaryotes have a cell wall surrounding the cell membrane except in mycoplasma. The fluid
matrix filling the cell is the cytoplasm. There is no well-defined nucleus. The genetic material is
basically naked, not enveloped by a nuclear membrane.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:128, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. In the genomic DNA there are two chromosomes

2. In prokaryotes there is presence of circular DNA in genome

3. Many bacteria have small circular DNA outside the genomic DNA called plasmids. 

4. The plasmid DNA confers certain unique phenotypic characters to such bacteria like resistance to antibiotics.
explanation:
The genetic material is basically naked, not enveloped by a nuclearnmembrane. In addition to the genomic DNA (the single chromosome/circular DNA), many bacteria have small circular DNA outside the genomic DNA. These smaller DNA are called plasmids. The plasmid DNA confers certain unique phenotypic characters to such bacteria. One such character is resistance to antibiotics.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:128, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. The plasmid DNA is used to monitor bacterial transformation with foreign DNA. 

2. No organelles, like the ones in eukaryotes, are found in prokaryotic cells except for mesosomes. 

3. Prokaryotes have something unique in the form of inclusions. 

4. Mesosomes are essentially infoldings of cell membrane.
explanation:
The plasmid DNA is used to monitor bacterial transformation with foreign DNA. Nuclear membrane is found in eukaryotes. No organelles, like the ones in eukaryotes, are found in prokaryotic cells except for ribosomes. Prokaryotes have something unique in the form of inclusions. A specialised differentiated form of cell membrane called mesosome is the characteristic of prokaryotes. They are essentially infoldings of cell membrane.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:128, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option:

Assertion: Most prokaryotic cells, particularly the bacterial cells, have a chemically complex cell envelope.

Reason:  The cell envelope consists of a tightly bound three layered structure i.e., the outermost glycocalyx followed by the cell wall and then the plasma membrane.
answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation:
Most prokaryotic cells, particularly the bacterial cells, have a chemically
complex cell envelope. The cell envelope consists of a tightly bound three
layered structure i.e., the outermost glycocalyx followed by the cell wall and
then the plasma membrane.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:128, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions
option_a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_b: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_c: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_d: Both Assertion and Reason are false.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. Most prokaryotic cells, particularly the bacterial cells, have a chemically complex cell envelope.

2. The cell envelope consists of a tightly bound three layered structure i.e., the outermost cell wall followed by the glycocalyx layer and then the plasma membrane.

3. Bacteria can be classified on the basis of the differences in the cell membrane

4. Gram positive and Gram negative bacteria on the basis of gram staining
explanation:
Most prokaryotic cells, particularly the bacterial cells, have a chemically
complex cell envelope. The cell envelope consists of a tightly bound three
layered structure i.e., the outermost glycocalyx followed by the cell wall and
then the plasma membrane. Although each layer of the envelope performs
distinct function, they act together as a single protective unit. Bacteria can
be classified into two groups on the basis of the differences in the cell envelopes
and the manner in which they respond to the staining procedure developed
by Gram viz., those that take up the gram stain are Gram positive and the
others that do not are called Gram negative bacteria.


(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:128, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. Glycocalyx differs in composition and thickness among different bacteria. 

2. It could be a loose sheath called the slime layer in some, while in others it may be thick and tough, called the capsule. 

3. The cell wall determines the shape of the cell and provides a strong structural support to prevent the bacterium from bursting or collapsing.

4. The plasma membrane is different in structure to that of the eukaryotes.
explanation:
Glycocalyx differs in composition and thickness among different
bacteria. It could be a loose sheath called the slime layer in some, while
in others it may be thick and tough, called the capsule. The cell wall
determines the shape of the cell and provides a strong structural support
to prevent the bacterium from bursting or collapsing.
The plasma membrane is selectively permeable in nature and interacts
with the outside world. This membrane is similar structurally to that of
the eukaryotes.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:128, paragraph no: 2, 3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the CORRECT option:

1. The plasma membrane isn't an selectively permeable in nature and interacts with the outside world. 

2. This membrane is similar structurally to that of the eukaryotes.

3. A special membranous structure is the mesosome which is formed by the extensions of the cell wall into the cell. 

4. These extensions of mesosomes are in the form of vesicles only
explanation:
The plasma membrane is selectively permeable in nature and interacts
with the outside world. This membrane is similar structurally to that of
the eukaryotes.
A special membranous structure is the mesosome which is formed
by the extensions of plasma membrane into the cell. These extensions are
in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae. 


(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:128, paragraph no: 3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. Mesosomes helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells.

2. These extensions of mesosmes are in the form of vesicles, tubules and lamellae.

3. In some prokaryotes like mycoplasma, there are other membranous extensions into the cytoplasm called chromatophores which contain pigments.

4. Mesosomes also help in respiration, secretion processes, to increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content.
explanation:
mesosomes helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and distribution to daughter cells.
They also help in respiration, secretion processes, to increase the surface area of the plasma membrane and enzymatic content. In some prokaryotes like cyanobacteria, there are other membranous extensions into the cytoplasm
called chromatophores which contain pigments.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:129, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option:

Assertion: Bacterial cells can be motile.

Reason: If motile, they have thin filamentous extensions from their cell wall called flagella.
answer: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
explanation:
Bacterial cells may be motile or non-motile. If motile, they have thin
filamentous extensions from their cell wall called flagella. Bacteria show a
range in the number and arrangement of flagella.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:129, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions
option_a: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion
option_b: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
option_c: Assertion is true but Reason is false
option_d: Both Assertion and Reason are false.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding motility of bacteria and choose the correct option:

1. All Bacterial cells are motile.

2. Motile bacteria have thin filamentous extensions from their cytoplasm called flagella. 

3. Bacterial flagellum is composed of three parts – filament, hook and basal body. 

4. The hook is the longest portion and extends from the cell surface to the outside.
explanation:
Bacterial cells may be motile or non-motile. If motile, they have thin filamentous extensions from their cell wall called flagella. Bacteria show a range in the number and arrangement of flagella. Bacterial flagellum is composed of three parts – filament, hook and basal body. The filament is the longest portion and extends from the cell surface to the outside.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:129, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding bacteria and choose the correct option:

1. Besides flagella, Pili and Fimbriae are also surface structures of the bacteria that also plays a role in motility. 

2. The pili are elongated tubular structures made of a special protein. 

3. The fimbriae are long filamentous like fibres sprouting out of the cell. 

4. In some bacteria, they are known to help attach the bacteria to rocks in streams and also to the host tissues.
explanation:
Besides flagella, Pili and Fimbriae are also surface structures of the bacteria but do not play a role in motility. The pili are elongated tubular structures made of a special protein. The fimbriae are small bristle like fibres sprouting out of the cell. In some bacteria, they are known to help attach the bacteria to rocks in streams and also to the host tissues.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:129, paragraph no: 3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. In prokaryotes, ribosomes are associated with the plasma membrane of the cell. 

2. They are made of two subunits - 60S and 40S units which when present together form 80S prokaryotic ribosomes. 

3. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis. 

4. Several ribosomes may attach to a single tRNA and form a chain called polyribosomes or polysome.
explanation:
In prokaryotes, ribosomes are associated with the plasma membrane of
the cell. They are about 15 nm by 20 nm in size and are made of two
subunits - 50S and 30S units which when present together form 70S
prokaryotic ribosomes. Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis. Several
ribosomes may attach to a single mRNA and form a chain called
polyribosomes or polysome. 

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:129, paragraph no: 4)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding prokaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.

2. Reserve material in prokaryotic cells are stored in the cytoplasm in the form of inclusion bodies. 

3. inclusion bodies are bounded membrane system.

4. examples of inclusion bodies are: phosphate granules, cyanadian granules and glycogen granules. 

5. Gas vacuoles are found in blue green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria.
explanation:
The ribosomes of a polysome translate the mRNA into proteins.
Inclusion bodies: Reserve material in prokaryotic cells are stored in
the cytoplasm in the form of inclusion bodies.
These are not bound by any membrane system and lie free in the cytoplasm, e.g., phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules and glycogen granules. Gas vacuoles are found in blue green and purple and green photosynthetic bacteria.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:129, paragraph no: 5)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding Eukaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. The eukaryotes include all the protists, plants and animals except fungi.

2. In eukaryotic cells there is an extensive compartmentalisation of cytoplasm through the presence of membrane bound organelles. 

3. Eukaryotic cells possess an organised nucleus with a nuclear envelope.

4. Eukaryotic cells do not have any locomotory structures.
explanation:
The eukaryotes include all the protists, plants, animals and fungi. 
In eukaryotic cells there is an extensive compartmentalisation of cytoplasm through the presence of membrane bound organelles. 
Eukaryotic cells possess an organised nucleus with a nuclear envelope. In addition, eukaryotic cells have a variety of complex locomotory and cytoskeletal structures.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:129, paragraph no: 6)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding Eukaryotic cells and choose the correct option:

1. Their genetic material is organised into chromosomes.

2. All eukaryotic cells are identical.

3. Plant and animal cells are different as the former possess cell walls, plastids and a large central vacuole which are absent in animal cells.

4. On the other hand, plant cells have centrioles which are absent in almost all animal cells
explanation:
Their genetic material is organised into chromosomes.
All eukaryotic cells are not identical. Plant and animal cells are different as the former possess cell walls, plastids and a large central vacuole which are absent in animal cells. 
On the other hand, animal cells have centrioles which are absent in almost all plant cells

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:129, paragraph no: 6)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell membrane and choose the correct option:

1. The detailed structure of the membrane was studied only after the advent of the simple microscope in the 1980s. 

2. Chemical studies in human red blood cells (RBCs), enabled the scientists to deduce the possible structure of chromosomes.

3. studies showed that the cell membrane is mainly composed of lipids and proteins.

4. In cell membrane, major lipids are phospholipids that are arranged in a single layer.
explanation:
The detailed structure of the membrane was studied only after the advent
of the electron microscope in the 1950s. Meanwhile, chemical studies on
the cell membrane, especially in human red blood cells (RBCs), enabled
the scientists to deduce the possible structure of plasma membrane.
These studies showed that the cell membrane is mainly composed of
lipids and proteins. The major lipids are phospholipids that are arranged
in a bilayer.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:131, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the cell membrane and choose the correct option:

1. The lipids are arranged within the membrane with the polar head towards the outer sides and the hydrophobic tails towards the inner part.

2. The nonpolar tail of saturated hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.

3. Phospholipids membrane also contains cholesterol.

4. Biochemical investigations clearly revealed that the cell membranes also possess protein and carbohydrate.
explanation:
In cell membrane, the major lipids are phospholipids that are arranged
in a bilayer. Also, the lipids are arranged within the membrane with the
polar head towards the outer sides and the hydrophobic tails towards
the inner part. This ensures that the nonpolar tail of saturated
hydrocarbons is protected from the aqueous environment.
In addition to phospholipids membrane also contains cholesterol.
Later, biochemical investigation clearly revealed that the cell membranes
also possess protein and carbohydrate.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:131, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Eukaryotic cell membrane and choose the correct option:

1. The ratio of protein and lipid is similar in all cell types. 

2. In human beings, the membrane of the erythrocyte has approximately 40 % protein and 52 % lipids.

3. Depending on the ease of extraction, membrane proteins can be classified as integral and peripheral. 

4. Peripheral proteins lie on the surface of membrane while the integral proteins are partially or totally buried in the membrane.
explanation:

1. Many of these membranous organelles are considered together as an endomembrane system because their functions are coordinated.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding endoplasmic reticulum and choose the correct option:

1. Electron microscopic studies of eukaryotic cells reveal the presence of a network or reticulum of tiny tubular structures scattered in the cytoplasm that is called the endoplasmic reticulum (ER).

2. ER divides the intracellular space into two distinct compartments, i.e., luminal  and intra luminal compartments.

3. The ER often shows ribosomes attached to their outer surface. 

4. The endoplasmic reticulum bearing ribosomes on their surface is called rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER).
explanation:
Electron microscopic studies of eukaryotic cells reveal the presence of a network or reticulum of tiny tubular structures scattered in the cytoplasm that is called the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) (Figure 8.5). Hence, ER divides the intracellular space into two distinct compartments, i.e., luminal (inside ER) and extra luminal (cytoplasm) compartments.
The ER often shows ribosomes attached to their outer surface. The endoplasmic reticulum bearing ribosomes on their surface is called rough
endoplasmic reticulum (RER).


(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:133, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

1. The endoplasmic reticulum bearing ribosomes on their surface is called rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). 

2. In the absence of ribosomes they appear smooth and are called smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER). 

3. RER is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in lipid synthesis and secretion.

4. RER are extensive and continuous with the outer membrane of the lysosomes.
explanation:
The endoplasmic reticulum bearing ribosomes on their surface is called rough endoplasmic reticulum (RER). In the absence of ribosomes they appear smooth and are called smooth endoplasmic reticulum (SER). RER is frequently observed in the cells actively involved in protein synthesis and secretion. They are extensive and continuous with the outer membrane of the nucleus.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:133, paragraph no: 3)

later named Golgi bodies after him. They consist of many flat, disc-shaped sacs or cisternae of

4. Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the trans face of the golgi apparatus
explanation:
The Golgi cisternae are concentrically arranged near the nucleus with distinct convex cis or the forming face and concave trans or the maturing face. The cis and the trans faces of the organelle are entirely different, but interconnected.
The golgi apparatus principally performs the function of packaging materials, to be delivered either to the intra-cellular targets or secreted outside the cell. Materials to be packaged in the form of vesicles from the ER fuse with the cis face of the golgi apparatus and move towards the maturing face.

3. These hydrolytic enzymes are optimally active at the basic pH. 

4. These hydrolytic enzymes are capable of digesting carbohydrates, proteins, lipids and nucleic acids.
explanation:

1. The vacuole is the membrane-bound space found in the cytoplasm.

2. It contains water, sap, excretory product and other materials not useful for the cell. 

3. The vacuole is bound by a single membrane called cytoplast.

4. In plant cells the vacuoles can occupy up to 20 % of the volume of the cell.
explanation:
The vacuole is the membrane-bound space found in the cytoplasm. It contains
water, sap, excretory product and other materials not useful for the cell. The
vacuole is bound by a single membrane called tonoplast. In plant cells the
vacuoles can occupy up to 90 % of the volume of the cell.

2. the concentration is significantly lower in the vacuole than in the cytoplasm.

3. In Amoeba the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion.

4. In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles are formed by engulfing the food particles.
explanation:
In plants, the tonoplast facilitates the transport of a number of ions and other materials against concentration gradients into the vacuole, hence their concentration is significantly higher in the vacuole than in the cytoplasm.
In Amoeba the contractile vacuole is important for osmoregulation and excretion. In many cells, as in protists, food vacuoles are formed by engulfing the food particles.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding mitochondria and choose the correct option:

1. Mitochondria is easily stained, and are easily visible under the microscope.

2.  The number of mitochondria per cell is variable depending on the physiological activity of the cells. 

3. They are similar in terms of shape and size.

4. Typically it is sausage-shaped or cylindrical having a diameter of 0.2-1.0μm (average 0.5μm) and length 1.0-4.1μm.
explanation:
Mitochondria (sing.: mitochondrion), unless specifically stained, are not
easily visible under the microscope. The number of mitochondria per cell
is variable depending on the physiological activity of the cells. In terms of
shape and size also, considerable degree of variability is observed. Typically
it is sausage-shaped or cylindrical having a diameter of 0.2-1.0μm (average
0.5μm) and length 1.0-4.1μm.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding mitochondria and choose the correct option:

1. Each mitochondrion is a double membrane-bound structure with the outer membrane and the inner membrane.

2. The inner compartment is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called the matrix.

3. The outer membrane forms the continuous limiting boundary of the organelle. 

4. The inner membrane forms a number of infoldings called the cisternae towards the matrix.
explanation:
Each mitochondrion is a double membrane-bound structure with the outer membrane and the inner
membrane dividing its lumen distinctly into two aqueous compartments,
i.e., the outer compartment and the inner compartment. The inner
compartment is filled with a dense homogeneous substance called the
matrix. The outer membrane forms the continuous limiting boundary of
the organelle. The inner membrane forms a number of infoldings called
the cristae (sing.: crista) towards the matrix. (cistermae are present in golgi bodies)

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:135, paragraph no: 1)

3. Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration as well as anaerobic respiration.

4. They produce cellular energy in the form of ATP, hence they are called ‘power houses’ of the cell.

The cristae increase the surface area. The two membranes have their own specific enzymes associated with the mitochondrial function. Mitochondria are the sites of aerobic respiration. The matrix also possesses single circular DNA molecule, a few RNA molecules, ribosomes (70S) and the components required for the synthesis of proteins. The mitochondria divide by fission.

1. The chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments which are responsible for trapping light energy essential for photosynthesis. 

2. In the chromoplasts fat soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls and others are present. 

3. The leucoplasts are the red in colour and are present in varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients. 

4. Amyloplasts store oils and fats.
explanation:
The chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and carotenoid pigments which are responsible for trapping light energy essential for photosynthesis. In the chromoplasts fat soluble carotenoid pigments like carotene, xanthophylls and others are present. This gives the part of the plant a yellow, orange or red colour. The leucoplasts are the colourless plastids of varied shapes and sizes with stored nutrients: Amyloplasts store carbohydrates (starch), e.g., potato; elaioplasts store oils and fats whereas the aleuroplasts store proteins.

4. The number of chloroplasts in green alga is 20-40 per cell in the mesophyll.
explanation:
Majority of the chloroplasts of the green plants are found in the mesophyll cells of the leaves. These are lens-shaped, oval, spherical, discoid or even ribbon-like organelles having variable length (5-10μm) and width (2-4μm). Their number varies from 1 per cell of the Chlamydomonas, a
green alga to 20-40 per cell in the mesophyll.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:136, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding plastid and choose the correct option:

1. The chloroplasts are also double membrane bound. 

2. The inner membrane of the chloroplast membrane is relatively more permeable.

3. The space limited by the inner membrane of the chloroplast is called the matrix.

4. Thylakoids are arranged in stacks like the piles of coins called grana
explanation:
Like mitochondria, the chloroplasts are also double membrane bound. Of the two, the inner chloroplast membrane is relatively less permeable. The space limited by the inner membrane of the chloroplast is called the stroma. A number of organised flattened membranous sacs called the thylakoids, are present in the stroma. Thylakoids are arranged in stacks like the piles of coins called
grana (singular: granum) or the intergranal thylakoids.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:136, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding plastid and choose the correct option:

1. There are flat membranous tubules called the stroma lamellae connecting the thylakoids of the different grana.

2. The membrane of the thylakoids enclose a space called a stroma. 

3. The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins. 

4. It also contains small, single-stranded circular DNA molecules and ribosomes.
explanation:
there are flat membranous tubules called the stroma lamellae connecting the thylakoids of the different grana. The membrane of the thylakoids enclose a space called a lumen. The stroma of the chloroplast contains enzymes required for the synthesis of carbohydrates and proteins. It also contains small, double- stranded circular DNA molecules and ribosomes. Chlorophyll pigments are present in the thylakoids. The ribosomes of the chloroplasts are smaller (70S) than the cytoplasmic ribosomes (80S).

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:136, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding ribosomes and choose the correct option:

1. They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins 

2. They are surrounded by a membrane. 

3. The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S while the prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S. 

4. The two subunits of 80S ribosomes are 60S and 30S while that of 70S ribosomes are 50S and 20S.
explanation:
Ribosomes are the granular structures first observed under the electron microscope as dense particles by George Palade (1953). They are composed of ribonucleic acid (RNA) and proteins and
are not surrounded by any membrane. The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S while the
prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S. Each ribosome has two subunits, larger and smaller subunits. The two subunits of 80S ribosomes are 60S and 40S while that of 70S ribosomes are 50S and 30S. Here ‘S’ (Svedberg’s Unit) stands for the sedimentation coefficient; it is indirectly a measure of density and size. Both 70S and 80S ribosomes are composed of two subunits.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:136, paragraph no: 3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the cytoskeleton of a cell and choose the correct option:

1. Cytoskeleton are filamentous proteinaceous structures.

2. It consists of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm which are collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton. 

3. The cytoskeleton in a cell provides mechanical support to a cell

4. It does not have any role in motility but maintains the shape of the cell.
explanation:
An elaborate network of filamentous proteinaceous structures consisting of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is collectively referred to as the cytoskeleton. The cytoskeleton in a cell are involved in many functions such as mechanical
support, motility, maintenance of the shape of the cell.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:136, paragraph no: 4)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cilli and flagella, and choose the correct option:

1. Cilia and flagella are hair-like outgrowths of the endoplasmic reticulum.

2. Cilia are small structures that work like oars, causing the movement of either the cell or the surrounding fluid.

3. Flagella are comparatively longer and responsible for cell movement. 

4. The prokaryotic bacteria also possess flagella that are structurally similar to that of the eukaryotic flagella.
explanation:
Cilia (sing.: cilium) and flagella (sing.: flagellum) are hair-like outgrowths of the cell membrane. Cilia are small structures which work like oars, causing the movement of either the cell or the surrounding fluid. Flagella are comparatively longer and responsible for cell movement. The prokaryotic bacteria also possess flagella but these are structurally different from that of the eukaryotic flagella.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:137, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cilli and flagella, and choose the correct option:

1. A cilium or the flagellum are uncovered, ie. that they are not covered with any membrane or sheath. 

2. Their core called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis. 

3. The axoneme usually has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules. 

4. Both the cilium and flagellum emerge from centriole-like structure called spindle fibre.
explanation:
The electron microscopic study of a cilium or the flagellum show that they are covered with plasma membrane. Their core called the axoneme, possesses a number of microtubules running parallel to the long axis. The axoneme usually has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules. Such an arrangement of axonemal microtubules is referred to as the 9+2 array. Both the cilium and flagellum emerge from centriole-like structure called the basal bodies.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:137, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cilli and flagella, and choose the correct option:

1. The arrangement of axonemal microtubules is referred to as the 9+2 array. 

2. The central tubules are connected by bridges and is also enclosed by a central sheath, which is connected to one of the tubules of each peripheral doublets by a radial spoke. 

3. There are 4 radial spokes. 

4. The peripheral doublets are also interconnected by radial spokes.
explanation:
The axoneme usually has nine doublets of radially arranged peripheral microtubules, and a pair of centrally located microtubules. Such an arrangement of axonemal microtubules is referred to as the 9+2 array. The central tubules are connected by bridges and is also enclosed by a central sheath, which is connected to one of the tubules of each peripheral doublets by a radial spoke. Thus, there are nine radial spokes. The peripheral doublets are also interconnected by linkers. Both the cilium and flagellum emerge from centriole-like structure called the basal bodies.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:137, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding centrosome, and choose the correct option:

1. Centrosome is an organelle usually containing two cylindrical structures called centrioles. 

2. They are surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar materials. 

3. Both the centrioles in a centrosome lie parallel to each other in which each has an organisation like the cartwheel.

4. They are made up of eight evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein.
explanation:
Centrosome is an organelle usually containing two cylindrical structures called centrioles. They are surrounded by amorphous pericentriolar materials. Both the centrioles in a centrosome lie perpendicular to each other in which each has an organisation like the cartwheel. They are made up of nine evenly spaced peripheral fibrils of tubulin protein.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:137, paragraph no: 3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding centrosome and choose the correct option:

1. Each of the peripheral fibril is a doublet.

2. The adjacent triplets are also linked.

3. The central part of the proximal region of the centriole is also proteinaceous and called central tubule.

4. The centrioles form the basal body of cilia or flagella, and spindle fibres that give rise to spindle apparatus during cell division in animal cells.
explanation:
Each of the peripheral fibril is a triplet.The adjacent triplets are also linked.
The central part of the proximal region of the centriole is also proteinaceous and called the hub, which is connected with tubules of the peripheral triplets by radial spokes made of protein. The centrioles form the basal body of cilia or flagella, and spindle fibres that give rise to spindle
apparatus during cell division in animal cells.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:138, paragraph no: 5)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding nucleus and choose the correct option:

1. Nucleus as a cell organelle was first described by Robert Whitteker as early as 1831. 

2. Later the material of the nucleus stained by the basic dyes was given the name chromatin by Flemming.

3. The interphase nucleus is the phase where nucleus of a cell when it is dividing

4. In interphase, the nucleus has highly extended and elaborate nucleoprotein fibres called chromatin, nuclear matrix and one or more spherical bodies called nucleoli
explanation:
Nucleus as a cell organelle was first described by Robert Brown as early
as 1831. Later the material of the nucleus stained by the basic dyes was
given the name chromatin by Flemming.
The interphase nucleus (nucleus of a cell when it is not dividing) has highly
extended and elaborate nucleoprotein fibres called chromatin, nuclear matrix
and one or more spherical bodies called nucleoli

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:138, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding nucleus and choose the correct option:

1. The nuclear envelope consists of two parallel membranes with a space between called the subnuclear space.

2. Nuclear envelop forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm. 

3. The outer membrane usually remains continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum and also bears ribosomes on it.

4.  At a number of places the nuclear envelope do not have any kind of pores.
explanation:
Electron microscopy has revealed that the nuclear envelope, which consists of two parallel membranes with a space between (10 to 50 nm) called the perinuclear space, forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm. The outer membrane usually remains continuous with the endoplasmic reticulum and also bears ribosomes on it. At a number of places the nuclear envelope is interrupted by minute pores, which are formed by the fusion of its two membranes. These nuclear pores are the passages through which movement of RNA and protein molecules takes place in both directions between the nucleus and the cytoplasm.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:138, paragraph no: 3)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding nucleus and choose the correct option:

1. The nuclear matrix or the nucleoplasm contains nucleolus and chromatin. 

2. The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the cytoplasm. 

3. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm as it is a membrane bound structure. 

4. It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
explanation:
The nuclear matrix or the nucleoplasm contains nucleolus and chromatin. The nucleoli are spherical structures present in the nucleoplasm. The content of nucleolus is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm as it is not a membrane bound structure. It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis. Larger and more numerous nucleoli are present in cells actively carrying out protein synthesis.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:138, paragraph no: 5)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding nucleus and choose the correct option:

1. The interphase nucleus has a loose and indistinct network of nucleoprotein fibres called chromatin.

2. Chromatin contains DNA and some basic proteins called histones, some non-histone proteins and also RNA. 

3. A single human cell has approximately two centimeter long thread of DNA.

4. There are forty six (twenty three pairs) chromosomes in human cell.
explanation:
You may recall that the interphase nucleus has a loose
and indistinct network of nucleoprotein fibres called
chromatin. But during different stages of cell division, cells
show structured chromosomes in place of the nucleus.
Chromatin contains DNA and some basic proteins called
histones, some non-histone proteins and also RNA. A
single human cell has approximately two metre long
thread of DNA distributed among its forty six (twenty three
pairs) chromosomes.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:139, paragraph no: 1)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding nucleus and choose the correct option:

1. In a dividing cell, each chromosome has a primary constriction or the centromere on the sides of which disc shaped structures called kinetochores are present. 

2. Centromere holds two chromatids of a chromosome. 

3. Based on the position of the centromere, the chromosomes can be classified into three types

4. In metacentric chromosome, centromere is situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm,
explanation:
Every chromosome (visible only in dividing cells)
essentially has a primary constriction or the centromere
on the sides of which disc shaped structures called
kinetochores are present (Figure 8.12). Centromere holds
two chromatids of a chromosome. Based on the position
of the centromere, the chromosomes can be classified into
four types (Figure 8.13). The metacentric chromosome
has middle centromere forming two equal arms of the
chromosome.

(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:139, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the nucleus and choose the correct option:

1. The metacentric chromosome has middle centromere forming two equal arms of the chromosome. 

2. The sub-metacentric chromosome has centromere situated close to its end forming one extremely short and one very long arm, whereas the telocentric chromosome has a terminal  centromere. 

3. In acrocentric chromosome the centromere is slightly away from the middle of the chromosome resulting into one shorter arm and one longer arm. 

4. Sometimes a few chromosomes have non-staining secondary constrictions at a constant location, that gives the appearance of a small fragment called the telomere.
explanation:
The metacentric chromosome
has middle centromere forming two equal arms of the
chromosome. The sub-metacentric chromosome has
centromere slightly away from the middle of the
chromosome resulting into one shorter arm and one
longer arm. In case of acrocentric chromosome the
centromere is situated close to its end forming one
extremely short and one very long arm, whereas the
telocentric chromosome has a terminal centromere. Sometimes a few chromosomes have non-staining secondary
constrictions at a constant location. This gives the appearance of a small
fragment called the satellite.


(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:139, paragraph no: 2)
topic_name: Cell Structure And Functions >> Cell : The Unit Of Life >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question: Among the following options, Which one describe the mechanism of mineral absorption in an incorrect manner?
answer: The root endodermis because of the layer of suberin has the ability to actively transport ions in a bidirectional manner
explanation:
Unlike water, all minerals cannot be passively absorbed by the roots. Two factors account for this: 
(i) minerals are present in the soil as charged particles (ions) which cannot move across cell membranes
(ii) the concentration of minerals in the soil is usually lower than the concentration of minerals in the root. 
Therefore, most minerals must enter the root by active absorption into the cytoplasm of epidermal cells. This needs energy in the form of ATP. The active uptake of ions is partly responsible for the water potential gradient in roots, and therefore for the uptake of water by osmosis. Some ions also move into the epidermal cells passively. Ions are absorbed from the soil by both passive and active transport. Specific proteins in the membranes of root hair cells actively pump ions from the soil into the cytoplasms of the epidermal cells. Like all cells, the endodermal cells have many transport proteins embedded in their plasma membrane; they let some solutes cross the membrane, but not others. Transport proteins of endodermal cells are control points, where a plant adjusts the quantity and types of solutes that reach the xylem. Note that the root endodermis because of the layer of suberin has the ability to actively transport ions in one direction only.
Reference  :NCERT Class 11th Pg., 189

option_c: Transport proteins of endodermal cells are control points, where a plant adjusts the quantity and types of solutes that reach the xylem.

question:
Given below are two statements : 
 Statement I : 
 The process of translocation through phloem is unidirectional but through xylem, it is bidirectional. 
 Statement II : 
 The most readily mobilized elements are phosphorus, sulphur, nitrogen and potassium. 
 In the light of the above statements, choose the 
most appropriate answer from the options given below : [ NEET 2023(Phase 2)]
answer: (2) Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
explanation:
The correct option is 2: Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

Explanation: Statement I: The process of translocation through phloem is bidirectional, not unidirectional. Phloem transports sugars and other organic compounds both upward (source to sink) and downward (sink to source) in plants.

Statement II: The statement is correct. Phosphorus, sulfur, nitrogen, and potassium are highly mobile elements in plants and are readily transported and remobilized within the plant for various metabolic processes.

Therefore, the correct answer is that Statement I is incorrect, but Statement II is correct.

question:
Identify the correct statements regarding Mass flow hypothesis.
(A) Mass flow is faster than diffusion.
(B) Mass flow is the result of pressure difference between the end points.
(C) Different substances involved in mass flow move at different paces.
(D) Mass flow can result through either a positive or a negative hydrostatic pressure gradient.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below: [ NEET 2023(Phase 2)]
explanation:
Long distance transport of substances within a plant cannot be by diffusion alone as it is a slow process. 
Thus, special long distance transport system (mass flow system) become necessary so as to move substances across long distance and at a much faster rate. Thus statement (A) is correct.
Mass flow is the movement of substances in bulk from one point to another as a result of pressure differences between the two points. Thus, statement (B) is correct.
It is a characteristic of mass flow that substances, whether in solution or in suspension, are swept along at the same pace. Thus, statement (C) is incorrect.
Bulk flow can be achieved either through a positive hydrostatic pressure gradient or a negative hydrostatic pressure gradient. Thus, statement (D) is correct.
Thus, option (2) is correct as it is mentioning all the correct statements
topic_name: Plant Physiology >> Transport in plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Consider the following statements about the root pressure choose the incorrect option.
answer: Root pressure plays a major role in water movement up tall trees.
explanation: Root pressure can, at best, only provide a modest push in the overall process of water transport. They obviously do not play a major role in water movement up tall trees. The greatest contribution of root pressure may be to re-establish the continuous chains of water molecules in the xylem which often break under the enormous tensions created by transpiration. Root pressure does not account for the majority of water transport; most plants meet their need by transpiratory pull. (Reference  : NCERT, page 186, paragraph 4).

question: Consider the following statements about the Pressure Flow or Mass Flow Hypothesis and choose the correct option.
answer: The process of loading at the source produces a hypertonic condition in the phloem.
explanation: The accepted mechanism used for the translocation of sugars from source to sink is called the pressure flow hypothesis. As glucose is prepared at the source (by photosynthesis) it is converted to sucrose (a dissacharide). The sugar is then moved in the form of sucrose into the companion cells and then into the living phloem sieve tube cells by active transport. This process of loading at the source produces a hypertonic condition in the phloem. (Reference  : NCERT, page 191, paragraph 1)
topic_name: Plant Physiology >> Transport in plants >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question: Consider the following statements about the Pressure Flow or Mass Flow Hypothesis and Choose the incorrect option.

explanation: As sugars are removed, the osmotic pressure decreases and water moves out of the phloem. To summarise, the movement of sugars in the phloem begins at the source, where sugars are loaded (actively transported) into a sieve tube. Loading of the phloem sets up a water potential gradient that facilitates the mass movement in the phloem. (Reference  : NCERT, page 191, paragraph 1  and  2).

topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy  of Flowering Plants >> Permanent Tissues

question: The dead, elongated cells having lignified thick cell wall occurring in groups in various parts of the plant, with tapering ends and occur in groups and serve mechanical functions, are ________
explanation: Sclerenchyma consists of long, narrow cells with thick and lignified cell walls having a few or numerous pits. They are usually dead and without protoplasts. On the basis of variation in form, structure, origin and development, sclerenchyma may be either fibres or sclereids(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:86, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy  of Flowering Plants >> Permanent Tissues

question: The dead, elongated cells having lignified thick cell wall occurring in groups, with tapering ends and serving a mechanical function are called –
explanation: Tracheids are elongated or tube like cells with thick and lignified walls and tapering ends. These are dead and are without protoplasm (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11; page no 87,paragraph no 2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy  of Flowering Plants >> Permanent Tissues

question: The protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ. What is this type of primary xylem called?
explanation:
In stems, the protoxylem lies towards the centre (pith) and the metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ. This type
of primary xylem is called endarch.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:87, paragraph no:3)

question: _________transfer water and minerals from roots to leaves and ________transfer food materials from leaves to roots  and  other parts of the plant.
explanation: Xylem functions as a conducting tissue for water and minerals from roots to the stem and leaves. Phloem transports food materials, usually from leaves to other parts of the plant (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:87, paragraph no:3  and  5)

question: ___________are elongated or tube like cells with thick and lignified walls and tapering ends. These are dead and are without protoplasm
explanation: Tracheids are elongated or tube like cells with thick and lignified walls and tapering ends. These are dead and are without protoplasm. The inner layers of the cell walls have thickenings which vary in form. In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water transporting elements(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:87, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Complex Tissues

question: _______ are much elongated, unbranched and have pointed, needle like apices and absent in the primary phloem but are found in the secondary phloem
explanation: Phloem fibres (bast fibres) are made up of sclerenchymatous cells. These are generally absent in the primary phloem but are found in the secondary phloem. These are much elongated, unbranched and have pointed, needle like apices. The cell wall of phloem fibres is quite thick. At maturity, these fibres lose their protoplasm and become dead.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:88, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Complex Tissues

question: Which of the following is the living element of xylem ?

question: Match the following.

explanation: The first formed primary xylem elements are called protoxylem and the later formed primary xylem is called metaxylem. question: Which one is INCORRECT about bulliform or motor cell?
answer: It is large-sized, thin-walled colored, vacuolate cells on the adaxial surface.

When they are flaccid due to water stress, they make the leaves curl inwards to minimise water loss.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:94, paragraph no:2)

question: Which one is correct about the secondary growth?
explanation:
At some places, the cambium forms a narrow band of parenchyma, which passes through the secondary xylem and the
secondary phloem in the radial directions. These are the secondary medullary rays

The youngest secondary phloem is just outside the cambium because it is produced by the cambium towards the outside of the stem.
The youngest secondary xylem is inside the cambium because it is produced by the cambium towards the inside of the stem.

The oldest secondary phloem is just inside the primary phloem because it was produced earlier by the cambium and is gradually pushed towards the center of the stem by the continuous production of new secondary phloem.

The oldest secondary xylem is just above the pith because it was produced earlier by the cambium and is gradually pushed towards the periphery of the stem by the continuous production of new secondary xylem.


(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:94, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Secondary Growth

That is, they have intact end walls unlike vessels. Vessels are long cylindrical tube like structures made of many cells, called vessel members, each with lignified walls and a large central cavity. Vessel members are interconnected through perforation in their common wal
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Lenticels are involved in [Neet 2013]
explanation: Lenticels are lens shaped openings formed in bark due to secondary growth. They permit gaseous exchange in woody trees. They also contribute to transpiration but in minute amounts because the suberised complementary cells present beneath the pore prevent excessive water loss. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:97, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Age of a tree can be estimated by [Neet 2013]
explanation: Two bands of secondary xylem i.e., autumn wood and spring wood are produced in one year. These two bands make an annual ring. The age of plant can be determined by counting the annual rings. It is called dendrochronolgy. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:96, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Interfascicular cambium develops from the cells of [Neet 2013]
explanation: In dicot stems, the cells of cambium present between primary xylem and primary phloem is the intrasfascicular cambium. The cells of medullary rays, adjoining these intrafascicular cambium become meristematic and form the interfascicular cambium. Thus, a continuous ring of cambium is formed. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:95, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Meristematic tissue responsible for increase in girth of tree trunk is (Karnataka neet 2013]
explanation: Lateral meristems are the meristems which are present along the lateral sides of stem and roots. They divide only in radial direction. Intrastelar or vascular cambium ring formed by intrafascicular (also called fascicular) and interfascicular cambium; and cork cambium (phellogen) are examples of this type of meristem. These meristems are responsible for increase in girth of stem and roots. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:85, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Bundle sheath cells (Karnataka neet 2013]
explanation: Bundle sheath cells are rich in the enzyme RuBisCo.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

answer: Guard cells are always surrounded by subsidiary cells.
explanation: The epidermal surface of the leaf exhibits modifications to form stomatal apparatus(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:89, paragraph no:1)
