question: Gymnosperms are also called soft wood spermatophytes because they lack [NEET 2012]
explanation:
Gymnosperms lack xylem fibres so they are called softwood.

Gymnosperms lack vessels in their xylem (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:87, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Water containing cavities in vascular bundles are found in [NEET 2012]
explanation: The monocot stem has a sclerenchymatous hypodermis, a large number of scattered vascular bundles, each surrounded by a sclerenchymatous bundle sheath, and a large, conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed. Peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones. The phloem parenchyma is absent, and water-containing cavities are present within the vascular bundles(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:93, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Closed vascular bundles lack [NEET 2012]
explanation: Vascular bundle consists of complex tissues, the phloem and xylem. In dicots, between xylem and phloem, cambium is present which helps in secondary growth. This type of vascular bundle is called open. While in monocots cambium is absent, so these are called closed vascular bundles.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Companion cells are closely associated with [NEET 2012]
explanation: Companion cell is a type of cell found within the phloem of flowering plants. Each companion cell is usually closely associated with a sieve element. They remain connected with sieve cells by plasmodesmata. They help in loading of phloem sieve cells with sugars through active transport. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:88, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The common bottle cork is a product of [NEET 2012]
explanation: Cork cambium or phellogen is a type of cambium arising within the outer layer of the stems of woody plants, usually as a complete ring surrounding the inner tissues. The cells of the cork cambium divide to produce an outer corky tissue (cork or phellem) and an inner secondary cortex (phelloderm). The common bottle cork produced from Quercus suber is a product of phellogen.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: As compared to a dicot root, a monocot root has (Mains 2012]
explanation:
As compared to the dicot root which have fewer xylem bundles, there are usually more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles in the monocot
root. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:91, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The cork cambium, cork and secondary cortex are collectively called [NEET 2011]
explanation: In hypodermis or outer cortical cells, a layer becomes meristematic which is known as cork cambium or phellogen. This phellogen also cuts off cells both on its outer side and inner side. The cells cut off on outer side are phellem or cork cells and cells cut off on inner side are phelloderm or secondary cortex. Phellem, phellogen and phelloderm collectively constitute periderm. The function of periderm is protective (because at maturity epidermis ruptures and hence the function is performed by periderm).(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:96, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Ground tissue includes [NEET 2011]
answer: All tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles
explanation: Ground tissue can be defined as all the tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles. Ground tissue constitutes the interior of organs except vascular system. It consists of simple tissues such as parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. Parenchymatous cells are usually present in cortex, pericycle, pith and medullary rays, in the primary stems and roots. Ground tissue system of the leaves is called mesophyll. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:89, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_b: All tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles

question: Some vascular bundles are described as open because these (Mains 2011]
answer: Are capable of producing secondary xylem and phloem
explanation: In dicot stem, cambium is present between xylem and phloem, such vascular bundles are called open. In monocot stem, the cambium is absent, such vascular bundles are called closed. Cambium are the meristematic cells which produces secondary xylem and phloem. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:92, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Are surrounded by pericycle but no endodermis
option_b: Are capable of producing secondary xylem and phloem
option_c: Possess conjunctive tissue between xylem and phloem

question: Function of companion cells is (Mains 2011]
answer: Maintaining the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes
explanation: Companion cells move sugar and amino acids into and out of the sieve elements and maintain pressure gradient in the sive tubes. In “source” tissue such as leaf companion cells use transmembrane proteins to take up sugar and amino acids by active transport. Movement of sugars in the phloem begins at the source, where sugars are loaded (actively transported) into a seive tube. Loading sets up a water potential gradient that facilitates movement of sugar. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:88, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Providing energy to sieve elements for active transport
option_c: Maintaining the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes
option_d: Being susceptible to pests and pathogens

question: Heartwood differs from sapwood in [NEET 2010]
explanation: In old trees, the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown due to deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic substances and essential oils in the central or innermost layers of the stem. These substances make it hard, durable and resistant to the attacks of microorganisms and insects. This region comprises dead elements with highly lignified walls and is called heartwood. The heartwood does not conduct water but it gives mechanical support to the stem. The peripheral region of the secondary xylem, is higher in colour and is known as the sapwood. It is involved in the conduction of water and minerals from root to leaf.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:96, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following is not a lateral meristem? [NEET 2010]
explanation: Meristem is classified on the basis of position in plant bodies into lateral meristem, apical meristem and intercalary meristem. Lateral meristem is present on the lateral sides, e.g., vascular cambium (fascicular and interfascicular cambium) and cork cambium (phellogen). (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:85, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The chief water conducting elements of xylem in gymnosperms are [NEET 2010]
explanation: The chief water conducting elements of xylem in gymnosperms are tracheids. These are elongated cells with tapering ends and are dead because of deposition of lignin. These show scalariform, annular, reticulate or bordered pitted thickening. These are the only water conducting xylem elements in both gymnosperm and pteridophytes. Generally vessels are absent in gymnosperm with exceptions like Gnetum, Welwitschia, Ephedra. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:87, paragraph no:2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Transport of food material in higher plants takes place through (Mains 2010]
explanation:
Phloem transports food materials, usually from leaves to other parts of the plant. Phloem in angiosperms is composed
of sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres. (Reference  : NCERT, page 87, paragraph 4).
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: In barley stem vascular bundles are [NEET 2009]
explanation: Barley is a monocotyledonous plant. The vascular bundle of stem is conjoint,collateral,exarch and closed (because cambium is absent). It is also scattered throughout the ground tissue.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Palisade parenchyma is absent in leaves of [NEET 2009]
explanation: Palisade parenchyma is absent in leaves of Sorghum. It is a monocot plant where the parenchyma tissues of the leaves are not differentiated into palisade and spongy.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The annular and spirally thickened conducting elements generally develop in the protoxylem when the root or stem is [NEET 2009]
explanation: The protoxylem differentiates in the parts of the primary body that have not completed their growth and differentiation. In fact in the shoot, the protoxylem matures among actively elongating tissues and is, therefore subjected to stresses. In the root, the protoxylem elements persist longer because here they mature beyond the region of maximum growth. In this differentiation annular and spiral thickening take place.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Anatomically fairly old dicotyledonous root is distinguished from the dicotyledonous stem by [NEET 2009]
explanation: In dicot root the protoxylem is located near the periphery of the vascular cylinder, the metaxylem farther inward. In roots xylem is exarch or centripetal. In dicot stem the protoxylem is located near the centre of vascular bundle and metaxylem is located near the periphery i.e., the xylem is endarch or centrifugal.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Vascular tissues in flowering plants develop from [NEET 2008]
explanation: Dermatogen is the region or histogen of single layer of outermost cells formed from the apical meristem. Dermatogen gives rise to epidermis of stem and other aerial parts. Periblem is the middle histogen which forms the cortex of stem and roots. Plerome is the central histogen which forms stele or part of stem and root inner to endodermis. Part of plerome that forms vascular tissues is called procambium. The pericycle layer converts into a secondary meristem called cork cambium or phellogen which divides to form secondary cortex or phelloderm.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The length of different internodes in a culm of sugarcane is variable because of [NEET 2008]
explanation: Internode is the part of a plant stem, that occurs between two adjacent nodes. Intercalary meristem are internodal in position and is found in the stem of grasses and other monocotyledonous plants. In early stages the internode is wholly or partially meristematic but later on some of its parts become matured more rapidly than the rest so a definite continuous sequence of development is maintained i.e., mature tissue left behind whereas new ones grow which later shows variable length.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Size of leaf lamina at the node below each internode

question: Passage cells are thin walled cells found in [NEET 2007]
answer: Endodermis of roots facilitating rapid transport of water from cortex to pericycle
explanation: Endodermis is a single layered structure which separates cortex from stele. There are both thick walled and thin walled cells in the endodermis. The thin walled cells are known as passage cells or transfusion cells which are opposite the protoxylem groups. These cells help in rapid transport of water from cortex to pericycle.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Phloem elements that serve as entry points for substance for transport to other plant parts
option_b: Testa of seeds to enable emergence of growing embryonic axis during seed germination
option_c: Central region of style through which the pollen tube grows towards the ovary
option_d: Endodermis of roots facilitating rapid transport of water from cortex to pericycle

question: For a critical study of secondary growth in plants, which one of the following pairs is suitable? [NEET 2007]
explanation: Secondary growth is observed in dicots and gymnosperm. It is not observed in pteridophytes and rarely observed in monocots. Secondary growth results in increase in girth or diameter of the stem by formation of secondary tissue by the activity of lateral meristem. So for study of secondary growth, teak (angiosperm) and pine (gymnosperm) are best suited.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: A common structural feature of vessel elements and sieve tube elements is [NEET 2006]
explanation: Xylem is the principal water conducting tissue of the plant. It consists of four types of cellstracheids, vessels, xylem fibres and xylem parenchyma. Xylem vessels are hollow, elongated cells with open ends and pitted walls. Cells walls are lignified. At maturity nucleus is absent in vessels. The constituent cells of the phloem are sieve elements (sieve cells, sieve tubes), companion cells, phloem fibres and phloem parenchyma cells. Sieve tube members are long, slender, tubelike cells joined end to end, to form long tubular channels – the sieve tubes. Sieve tube members possess specialized sieve areas on the end walls called sieve plate. Young sieve tube members have abundant cytoplasm but their is no nucleus. The nucleus disintegrates during their development.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: In a woody dicotyledonous tree, which of the following parts will mainly consist of primary tissues? [NEET 2005]
explanation: The tissues which develop from apical meristem and procambium are known as primary tissues and these constitute the primary structures of the plant body. The development of the primary tissues causes the stem to grow in length and to some extent in thickness. Stem and root in dicotyledons show secondary growth as they have development of secondary vascular tissues (i.e., secondary xylem and secondary phloem) in them. Flowers, fruits and leaves are primary tissues.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: In a longitudinal section of a root, starting from the tip upward, the four zones occur in the following order: [NEET 2004]
answer: Root cap, cell division, cell enlargement, cell maturation
explanation: The root system of a plant develops from the hypocotyl of the embryo of a seed. The root shows following four regions these usually merge into one another, without distinct boundaries between them. The zones, successively from the apex to the base are– (i) Root cap zone: The apex of each root is covered by a cushion of thin walled cells known as root cap. (ii) Region of cell division: It lies just behind the root cap. It is the main growing region of the root where active cell divisions take place. (iii) Region of elongation: The region of elongation is responsible for growth in length of the root. (iv)Region of maturation: Epidermal cells of this region give out small, thin, cylindrical unicellular outgrowths, known as root hairs. These are the main absorbing organs of the root. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:85, )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Root cap, cell division, cell enlargement, cell maturation
option_b: Root cap, cell division, cell maturation, cell enlargement
option_c: Cell division, cell enlargement, cell maturation, root cap
option_d: Cell division, cell maturation, cell enlargement, root cap

question: The apical meristem of the root is present [NEET 2003]
explanation: Parts of typical root : root cap, meristematic growing region, zone of elongation, root hair zone, zone of meristematic cells. Apical meristem is terminal in position and responsible for terminal growth of the plant. Apical meristem is present at all root tips and shoot tips. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:85, figure 6.1))
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: In which one of the following is nitrogen not a constituent ? [NEET 2003]
explanation: The major storage component of Avocado fruit is oil. It is stored in specialized mesocarp cells called idioblast.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The aleurone layer in maize grain is specially rich in [NEET 2003]
explanation: In monocotyledons the seeds are generally endospermous. The internal structure of grain can be studied in a longitudinal section. It shows two distinct regions upper large region, the endosperm and lower smaller region, the embryo. The endosperm is surrounded by a special one cell thick layer, called aleurone layer. It is filled with aleurone grains which are proteinaceous in nature. Other components of this layer are phytin, carbohydrates and small amounts of phospholipids are also present.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Chlorenchyma is known to develop in the [NEET 2003]
explanation: Chlorenchyma or assimilatory parenchyma are parenchymatous cells that possess abundant chloroplasts in them. They are capable of photosynthesis. A spore capsule of moss can perform photosynthesis because of the presence of chlorenchyma cells in them.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_b: Mycelium of a green mould such as aspergillus

question: Diffuse porous woods are characteristic of plants growing in [NEET 2003]
explanation: In most of the gymnosperms, like conifers and cycads, vessels are absent and the wood is made entirely of tracheids. Such wood is known as nonporous. In angiosperms, on the other hand, the wood consists of both tracheids and vessels. The wide vessels appear as pores between otherwise small sized tracheary elements. Such a wood is known as porous. In porous wood, if vessels have essentially equal diameters and are uniformly distributed throughout the ring, the wood is known as diffuse porous. It is characterstic of plants growing in tropics.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The cells of the quiescent centre are characterised by [NEET 2003]
answer: Having light cytoplasm and small nuclei
explanation: In the apices of some roots, (e.g., Zea mays or maize), there is a central region of cells which normally does not divide. This central inactive region was called quiescent centre by F.A.L. Clowes. The cells of this region have lesser amounts of RNA and DNA so they have small nuclei. These cells also have a lower rate of protein synthesis. Mitochondria and endoplasmic reticulum are less developed. The cells of the quiescent centre are usually inactive. However, if already existing meristematic cells are injured or become inactive due to any other reason, the cells of quiescent centre become active.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Having dense cytoplasm and prominent nuclei
option_b: Having light cytoplasm and small nuclei
option_c: Dividing regularly to add to the corpus
option_d: Dividing regularly to add to tunica

question: Which of the following statements is true? [NEET 2002]
answer: Tracheids are unicellular with wide lumen
explanation: Xylem is the principal water conducting tissue of the plant. It consists of four types of cellstracheids, vessels, xylem fibres and xylem parenchyma. The tracheids and vessels together are known as tracheary elements. Tracheids are characteristic of all vascular plant. Tracheids originate from single cells. These are single elongated cells with tapering ends. The end walls are without perforations. Their length varies from one to three mm. Tracheids are devoid of protoplast, hence dead; fairly large cavity of these cells is without any contents. The wall of tracheids is moderately thick and usually lignified.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Vessels are multicellular with wide lumen.
option_b: Tracheids are multicellular with narrow lumen.
option_c: Vessels are unicellular with narrow lumen.

question: Axillary bud and terminal bud derived from the activity of [NEET 2002]
explanation: Apical meristems are situated at the tips of the root and shoot. They take part in initial growth. Plants elongate and increase in height as a result of divisions in this meristem. Promeristem and primary meristem (root and shoot apices) are included in this type of meristem. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:85, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Four radial vascular bundle are found in [NEET 2002]
explanation: The vascular tissue of the root is characterised by radial arrangement of vascular bundles i.e., xylem and phloem occur in separate patches on alternate radii. The number of xylem and phloem groups vary from two to six. But tetrarch condition (four vascular bundles) is more common. Monocot root generally has more than six vascular bundles (polyarch). Vascular bundles in dicot stems are conjoint, collateral or bicollateral, endarch and open. They are arranged in a ring. In monocot stems the vascular bundles are conjoint, collateral, endarch and closed. They are scattered in the ground tissue(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:91, paragraph no:1).
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Vessels are found in [NEET 2002]
answer: Most of angiosperms and few gymnosperms
explanation: Vessels are long tubelike structures ideally suited for the conduction of water and solutes. These are made up of a row of cylindrical cells arranged in longitudinal series. The partition walls of these cells are perforated and as such the entire structure becomes tubelike. The region of the wall where perforations occur is known as perforation plate. Vessels are found in the wood of almost all the angiosperms except certain primitive members of the order ranales (vesseless dicots), e.g., Trochodendron, Tetracentron, Drimys, Pseudowintera, etc. Vessels also occur in some pteridophytes, such as Selaginella and in the members of order Gnetales of gymnosperms (e.g., Genetum, Ephedra and Welwitschia). (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:87, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2
option_b: Most of angiosperms and few gymnosperms
option_c: All angiosperms, all gymnosperms and some pteridophyta

question: In plants inulin and pectin are [NEET 2001]
explanation: Inulin is a water soluble fructosan. It is a common reserve food in members of family compositae. Pectin in a mucopolysaccharides and occur in plant cell walls. At the time of fruit ripening wall pectins hydrolyse to give constituent sugars.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

answer: Differentiation of procambium followed by the formation of primary phloem and xylem simultaneously
explanation: In plants during vascularisation, differentiation of procambium occurs followed by the formation of primary phloem and xylem simultaneously.

question: Casparian strips are found in [NEET 1999]
explanation: Endodermis is single layered structure which separates cortex from stele. The cells of endodermis are barrelshaped without intercellular spaces, living and containing starch. The radial and tangential walls of endodermal cells possess thickenings of lignin, suberin and cutin in the form of strips or bands, which are known as casparian bands or casparian strips. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:91, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Which of the following meristems is responsible for extrastelar secondary growth in dicotyledonous stem? [NEET 1998]
explanation: Extrastelar secondary growth means growth in the cortical region, external to stele. For extrastelar secondary growth the cork cambium or phellogen develops in the region outside the vascular tissue. This gives rise to cork or phellem and secondary cortex or phelloderm. All the three layers (i.e, cork, cork cambium and secondary cortex) together constitute periderm. Fascicular and interfascicular cambuim occurs in the stelar regions.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:96, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: The periderm includes [NEET 1998]
explanation: Phellogen, phellem, and phelloderm are collectively known as periderm.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:96, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: At maturity, which of the following is nonnucleated? [NEET 1997]
explanation: In pteridophytes and gymnosperms, sieve tubes are not arranged in linear rows and hence called sieve cells. Sieve tube elements are the conducting element of phloem. These are arranged end to end in linear rows with septa (sieve plate) between two sieve tube elements. In the sieve plate, there are present sieve pores. Sieve tube elements are living and have thin cellulosic walls in young cells but they become thick walled and are without nuclei at maturity. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:88, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Which of the following is not true about ‘sclereids’? [NEET 1996]
answer: These are groups of living cells.
explanation: Sclereids are a type of sclerenchyma cells. They are short or irregular, their walls are very thick, irergular and the lumen is very narrow. These are dead cells and do not perform any metabolic functions. They show different types of lignin depositions and also have pits. They are present in hard parts like endocarp of coconut, hard seed coats fruit pulps. They are also called stone cells and are different types as brachysclereids, osteoclereids, macrosclereids, asterosclercids and fileform cells.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:86, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

option_b: These are found in nut shells, guava pulp, pear.
option_c: These are also called stone cells.

question: As a tree grows older, which of the following increases more rapidly in thickness? [NEET 1994]
explanation: Heartwood or duramen is the dark coloured wood near the centre of the axis formed after many years of secondary growth of stem. A small outer region, however, remains light coloured. It is known as sap wood or alburnum. The heartwood is formed due to changes in the elements of the secondary xylem. As secondary growth proceeds most of the older elements of secondary xylem lose water and become filled with organic compounds such as oils, gums, resins, tannins, and aromatic and colouring materials. The wood becomes dark coloured due to accumulating of these substances and is also termed as duramen. The sap wood is the light coloured region of the secondary xylem. Cells of this region are functionally active. The elements of the secondary xylem added by cambial activity are those of sap wood. But gradually most of these elements get transformed into heart wood. Thus the amount of heart wood increases as the tree grows older. The amount of sap wood, however, remains almost constant(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:96, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Where do the casparian bands occur? [NEET 1994, 1990]
explanation: The innermost layer of soft cortex is called as endodermis. This uniseriate layer is characterised by the presence of casparian strips. This thickenings was first observed by Caspary, (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:91, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Which of the following plant cells will show totipotency? [NEET 1993]
explanation: Meristems shows the totipotency because xylem vessels and cork cells are dead while sieve tube cells do not possess nuclei.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:84, paragraph no:3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Periderm is produced by [NEET 1993]
explanation: Periderm is produced by phellogen. The phellogen forms phellem on the outer face and phelloderm on the inner. The three layers i.e., phellem, phellogen and phelloderm jointly constitute the periderm. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:96, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: A narrow layer of thin walled cells found between phloem/bark and wood of a dicot is [NEET 1993]
explanation: A narrow layer of thin walled cells found between phloem/bark and wood of dicot is vascular cambium. Vascular cambium present inside a vascular bundle is called as intrafascicular cambium or fascicular cambium. The vascular cambium is a meristematic tissue. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:94, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Which exposed wood will decay faster? [NEET 1993]
explanation: Sap wood will decay faster. Sap wood is less durable because it is susceptible to attack by pathogen and insects(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:96, paragraph no:3).
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Abnormal/anomalous secondary growth occurs in [NEET 1993]
explanation: Monocot trees such as palms grow in thickness by primary thickening meristem situated at the base of the leaf. Plants like Dracaena show secondary growth by a special cambium. It develops in the form of strips just outside the vascular region. This cambial strips produce secondary vascular bundles which is amphivasal in Dracaena.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Bordered pits are found in [NEET 1993]
explanation: Bordered pits are found in vessel wall. In bordered pits, the thickening material over arches the pit cavity in such a way that a pit chamber opens to the interior by a pit aperture.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: A bicollateral vascular bundle is characterized by [NEET 1992]
explanation: A bicollateral vascular bundles is characterised by xylem being sandwiched between phloem. Here there are two cambuim rings e.g., Cucurbita.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Vascular cambium produces [NEET 1992, 1990]
explanation: Vascular cambium produces secondary xylem and secondary phloem. It is develop from the procambium which is an embryonic tissue, hence it is primary in origin. It is secondary in function for it forms the secondary tissues like secondary xylem, secondary phloem and secondary medullary rays. The cambium is a radially one cell thick zone of meristematic cells. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:94, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: What is true about a monocot leaf? [NEET 1992, 1990]

Also in the upper epidermis, there are some large cells found in groups which are called bulliform cells. The venation pattern in monocot is parallel. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:94, paragraph no1-:2)

question: Which is correct about transport of conduction of substances? [NEET 1991]
answer: Organic food moves upwardly and downwardly through phloem
explanation: Phloem is the food conducting tissue of plants. The sieve tubes are food conducting elements of the plants. It is proposed that food is translocated by mass flow or by streaming currents of protoplasm. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:88, paragraph no:1)

question: An organised and differentiated cellular structure having cytoplasm but no nucleus is [NEET 1991]
explanation: An organised and differentiated cellular structure having cytoplasm but no nucleus are sieve tubes. The sieve tubes are living cells. Their walls are thicker than surrounding parenchyma cells. Sometimes they have a special, shining nacreous thickening. Cytoplasm occurs in the form of thin lining enclosing a big central vacuole.(Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:88, paragraph no:1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Angular collenchyma occurs in [NEET 1991]
explanation: Angular collenchyma occurs in, Cucurbita. It has thickening at the angles and there are no intercellular spaces. It is generally found in leaf petioles.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: For union between stock and scion in grafting which one is the first to occur [NEET 1990]
explanation: Grafting is a techinque in which cambium bearing shoot (scion = graft) of one plant is joined to cambium bearing stump (root system = stock) of a related plant through different unions like tongue grafting, wedge grafting etc. In grafting union between stock and scion produces undifferentiated mass of cells called callus. Therefore, for union between stock and scion in grafting, first to occur is the formation of callus. Callus is more or less corky secondary tissue developed lay woody plants over a wound. It is derived from cambium.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Pericycle of roots produces [NEET 1990]
explanation: Pericycle of root produces lateral roots. Endodermis is followed by pericycle. Usually it is a continuous layer but in some monocots it is interrupted by xylem and phloem. It is the site of origin of lateral roots and cork cambium. The root branches are, therefore described as endogenous in origin. (Reference  : NCERT, page 91, paragraph 1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Collenchyma occurs is [NEET 1990]
explanation: Collenchyma occurs in climbing stems. Collenchyma occurs in the stem and petioles of dicot herbs. Due to deposition of pectin, it has high water retaining capacity. Since pectin appears at the angles, it becomes a spongy tissues. The collenchyma is a mechanical tissue which gives tensile strength to the plant.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Collenchyma occurs in the stem and petioles of [NEET 1990]
explanation: Collenchyma occurs in climbing stems. Collenchyma occurs in the stem and petioles of dicot herbs. Due to deposition of pectin, it has high water retaining capacity. Since pectin appears at the angles, it becomes a spongy tissues. The collenchyma is a mechanical tissue which gives tensile strength to the plant.

question: Monocot leaves possess [NEET 1990]

question: Cork cambium and vascular cambium are [NEET 1990]

question: Cork is formed from [NEET 1988]
explanation: In hypodermis or outer cortical cells, a layer becomes meristematic which is known as cork cambium or phellogen. This phellogen also cuts off cells both on its outer side and inner side. The cells cut off on outer side are phellem or cork cells and cells cut off on inner side are phelloderm or secondary cortex. The phellem or cork cells are dead and have deposition of a fatty substance called suberin (i.e., cork cells are suberized). Suberin is impervious to water and thus cork cells are buoyant (i.e., float on water). Phellem, phellogen and phelloderm collectively constitute periderm. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:96, paragraph no:4)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: Which meristem helps in increasing girth? [NEET 1988]
explanation: The meristem that helps in increasing girth is lateral meristem. The lateral meristem is responsible for lateral growth of the plant i.e., growth in thickness e.g., cambium and cork cambium. It divides only periclinally or radially and is responsible for increase in girth or diameter. (Reference  :NCERT Biology Class 11: page no:85, paragraph no:2)

question:
In old trees the greater part of the secondary xylem is dark brown and resistant to insect attack due to:
 
 (a) secretion of secondary metabolites and their deposition in the lumen of vessels
 
 (b) deposition of organic compounds like tannins and resins in the central layers of stems
 
 (c) deposition of suberin and aromatic substances in the outer layer of stem
 
 (d) deposition of tannins, gum, resin and aromatic substances in the peripheral layers of stem
 
 (e) presence of parenchyma cells, functionally active xylem elements and essential oils
 
 Choose the correct answer from the following options given below:
 [NEET 2022]
explanation:
In old trees, the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown due to deposition of organic compounds like tannins, resins, oils, gums, aromatic
substances and essential oils in the central or innermost layers of the stem. These substances make it hard, durable and resistant to the attacks of micro-
organisms and insects. (Reference  : NCERT, page: 96, paragraph 3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question:
Read the following statements about the vascular bundle:

a. In roots, xylem and phloem in a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner along the different radii.

b. Conjoint closed vascular bundles do not possess cambium.

c. In open vascular bundles, cambium is present in between xylem and phloem.

d. The vascular bundles of dicotyledonous stem possess endarch protoxylem. 

e. In monocotyledonous root, usually there are more than six xylem bundles present.
 
 Choose the correct answer from the following options given below:
 [NEET 2022]
answer: a, c, d  and  e only
explanation:
Each vascular bundle is conjoint, open, and with endarch protoxylem. In dicotyledonous stems, cambium is present between phloem and xylem. Such vascular bundles because of the presence of
cambium possess the ability to form secondary xylem and phloem tissues, and hence are called open vascular bundles. As compared to the dicot root which have fewer xylem bundles, there are usually more than six (polyarch) xylem bundles in the monocot root. When xylem and phloem within a vascular bundle are arranged in an alternate manner along the different radii, the arrangement is called radial
such as in roots. (refernece: NCERT, page 90, paragraph 1).
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2
option_b: b, c, d  and  e only
option_d: a, c, d  and  e only

question:
The anatomy of springwood shows some peculiar features. Identify the correct set of statements about springwood: [NEET 2022]

(a) It is also called as the earlywood


(b) In spring season cambium produces xylem elements with narrow vessels 

(c) It is lighter in colour

(d) The springwood along  with autumnwood shows alternate concentric rings forming annual rings

(e) It is lower density


Choose the correct answer from the following options given below:
answer: a, c, d  and  e only
explanation:
In the spring season, cambium is very active and produces a large number of xylary elements having vessels with wider cavities. The wood formed during this season is called spring
wood or early wood. The spring wood is lighter in colour and has a lower density whereas the autumn wood is darker and has a higher density. The two kinds of woods that appear as alternate concentric rings, constitute an annual ring.(Reference  : NCERT, page 96, paragraph 1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2
option_a: a, b, d  and  e only
option_b: a, c, d  and  e only

question:
Initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium
 during secondary growth takes place in cells of :  [ RE NEET 2022]
explanation:
Secondary growth is an increase in the thickness of the shoots and roots of a vascular plant as a result of the activity of the two lateral meristems, the cork cambium and vascular cambium.
The pericycle is a cylinder of cells that lies just inside the endodermis and phloem in plant roots while in stems, it is situated around the ring of vascular bundles. It has the capacity to regulate the formation of lateral roots by rapidly dividing near the xylem elements of the root. It strengthens the roots and provides protection for the vascular bundles.
In plants undergoing secondary growth, the pericycle contributes to the vascular cambium often diverging into a cork cambium.
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Previous Year Questions 2

question: The type of tissue commonly found in the fruit wall of nuts is :
explanation:
The spherical, oval or cylindrical cells with very narrow lumen; in sclerenchyma are called sclereids. Sclereids are usually found in the fruit walls of nuts, pulp of fruits like guava, pear and sapota; seed coats of legumes and leaves of tea. The gritty texture of pear or guava is because of sclereids.
So, the correct answer is 'Sclereids.'

question:
Consider the following statements regarding stomata and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Stomata regulates the transpiration and gaseous exchange.
 
 2. Each stomata has spherical shaped guard cells.
 
 3. Grass has dumb-bell shaped guard cells.
 
 4. In stomata the inner walls are thin and outer walls are highly thickened.
explanation: Stomata regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange. Stomata have bean shaped guard cells. In grass the guard cells are dumb-bell shaped. The outer walls of the guard cells are thin and the inner walls are highly thickened. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 88; Paragraph 1)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding stomata and choose the correct option.
 
 1. The guard cells regulate the opening and closing of stomata. 
 
 2. Epidermal cells posses chloroplasts.
 
 3. Subsidiary cells are specialized guard cells.
 
 4. Stomatal apparatus consists only of guard cells and stomata.
explanation: The guard cells have chloroplasts and they regulate the opening and the closing of the stomata. Epidermal cells have no chloroplasts. Subsidiary cells are the specialized epidermal cells. The stomatal apparatus consists with not only the stomatal apperature and guard cells, but also with the subsidiary cells. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 89; Paragraph 1)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding epidermal cells and choose the correct option.
 
 1. The root hairs are multicellular elongations of the epidermal cells 
 
 2. They help absorb water and minerals from the soil.
 
 3. Trichomes are unicellular epidermal hairs in the stem.
 
 4. Trichomes enhance the water loss through transpiration.
explanation: The root hairs are the unicellular elongations of the epidermal cells and they help absorb water and minerals from the soil. In the shoot system, trichomes are multicellular epidermal hairs. They prevent the water loss through transpiration.(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 89; Paragraph 2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding ground tissue system and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Ground tissue includes epidermis and vascular bundle.
 
 2. Ground tissue has simple tissues like parenchyma and collenchyma.
 
 3. Ground tissue in leaves have mesophylls containing chloroplasts.
 
 4. Parenchyma is not present in pith and medulla in primary stem.
explanation: The ground tissue is composed of all tissues except epidermis and vascular bundle. It consists of simple tissues such as parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. The ground tissue in leaves is called mesophyll and contains chloroplasts. Parenchymatous cells are usually present in cortex, pericycle, pith and medullary rays, in the primary stems. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 89; Paragraph 3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding vascular tissue system and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Vascular tissue system is devoid of complex tissues.
 
 2. Vascular bundle constitutes only the xylem and the phloem in dicotyledons.
 
 3. In monocotyledons the cambium lies in between the xylem and the phloem.
 
 4. Cambium helps to form secondary xylem and phloem tissues.
explanation: Vascular tissue system consists of complex tissues. In the vascular tissue of dicot stems cambium is also present in addition to the xylem and phloem. Monocot plants don't have a cambium. Cambium helps to form secondary xylem and phloem tissues.(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 90; Paragraph 1)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding vascular bundles and choose the correct option.
 
 1. In conjoint vascular bundles, the xylem and phloem are jointly situated along the same radius.
 
 2. Radial vascular bundles have xylems and phloems arranged in an alternate manner.
 
 3. Radial vascular bundles are common in stems and leaves.
 
 4. The conjoint vascular bundles usually have the phloem located in the inner side of xylem.
explanation:
In conjoint of vascular bundles, the xylem and phloem are jointly situated along the same radius of vascular bundles. Radial vascular bundles have xylems and phloems arranged in an alternate manner. Conjoint vascular bundles are common in stems and leaves not the radial vascular bundles.
The conjoint vascular bundles have the phloem located only on the outer side of xylem. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 90; Paragraph 1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding 'Dicot Root' and choose the correct option.
 
 1. The cortex of the dicot roots consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchyma cells without intercellular spaces.
 
 2. Outermost layer of the transverse section is epliblema.
 
 3. Many cells of epiblema protrude as unicellular root hairs.
 
 4. The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis.
explanation:
The cortex of the dicot roots consists of several layers of thin-walled parenchymal cells with intercellular spaces. The outermost layer of the transverse section of the dicot root is epiblema. Many cells of epiblema protrude as unicellular root hairs. The innermost layer of the cortex is called endodermis.
(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 90; Paragraph 2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the dicotyledonous root and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Endodermis has a double layer of barrel shaped cells with intracellular spaces.
 
 2. The tangential walls of the endodermal cells are water permeable.
 
 3. Suberin is deposited in endodermal cells in the form of casparian strips.
 
 4. Pericycle contains a single layer of parenchyma cells.
explanation: Endodermis has a a single layer of barrel-shaped cells without any intercellular spaces. Both the tangential as well as radial walls of the endodermal cells have a deposition of water-impermeable, waxy material suberin in the form of casparian strips. Pericycle contains a few layers of parenchymal cells.(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 91; Paragraph 1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the dicotyledonous root and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Lateral root initiation during secondary growth occurs in endodermis.
 
 2. The collenchymatous cells in between the xylem and the phloem are called conjuctive tissue.
 
 3. All tissues on the innerside of the endodermis constitute the stele.
 
 4. There are numerous xylem and phloem patches.
explanation: Initiation of lateral roots and vascular cambium during the secondary growth takes place in the pericycle, but not in the endodermis. The parenchymatous cells which lie between the xylem and the phloem are called conjuctive tissue.  All tissues on the innerside of the endodermis such as pericycle, vascular bundles and pith constitute the stele.(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 91; Paragraph 1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding monocotyledonous root and choose the correct option.
 
 1. The anatomy of the monocot root is similar to the dicot root in many respects.
 
 2. There are 2-4 xylem bundles in monocot roots.
 
 3. Monocot roots have a small but well developed pith.
 
 4. Both monocot and dicot roots undergo a secondary growth.
explanation: The anatomy of the monocot root is similar to the dicot root in many respects. There are usually more than 6 xylem bundles in monocot root. The pith of the monocot root is large and well developed. Monocotyledonous roots do not undergo any secondary growth. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 91; Paragraph 3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements regarding dicot stem and choose the correct option.

 2. Epidermis is covered with a thin layer of cuticle.
 
 3. Epidermis has trichomes and stomata in abundance.
 
 4. The cells arranged in multiple layers between epidermis and pericycle make the hypodermis.
explanation: The epidermis is the outermost protective layer of the dicot stem. Epidermis is covered with a thin layer of cuticle. Epidermis has trichomes and a few stomata. The cells arranged in multiple layers between epidermis and pericycle make the cortex. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 92; Paragraph 1)

explanation: The cortex has 3 subzones. Hypodermis has few layers of collenchymatous cells. The innermost layer of the cortex is called the endodermis.(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 92; Paragraph 1)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding monocot stem and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Monocot stem has a small number of vascular bundles.
 
 2. Central vascular bundles are smaller than peripheral ones.
 
 3. Vascular bundles are conjoint and open.
 
 4. Phloem parenchyma is present in vascular bundles.
explanation: Monocot stem has a large number of scattered vascular bundles. Peripheral vascular bundles are generally smaller than the centrally located ones. Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed. The phloem parenchyma is absent, and water-containing cavities are present within the vascular bundles.(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 93; Paragraph 2)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding dorsiventral leaf and choose the correct option.

 2. epidermis has a conspicious cuticle.
 
 3. The abaxial epidermis generally bears less stomata than the adaxial epidermis
 
 4. The adaxial epidermis may sometimes lack stomata.
explanation: The vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf through the lamina shows three main parts, namely, epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system.  The epidermis which covers both the upper surface and lower surface of the leaf has a conspicuous cuticle. The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis. the adaxial epidermis may even lack stomata. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 93; Paragraph 2)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding Dicot leaf and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Mesophyll is the tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis
 
 2. Mesophyll made up of collenchyma has chloroplasts and does photosynthesis.
 
 3. Vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib
 
 4. The size of the vascular bundles are independent on the size of the veins.
explanation: The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll. Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. Vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib. The size of the vascular bundles are dependent on the size of the veins.(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 93; Paragraph 2)

Consider the following statements regarding Dicot leaf and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Pallisade parenchyma and spongy parenchyma are the two types of parenchymal cells in mesophyll.
 
 2. Spongy parenchyma are are arranged vertically and parallel to each other.
 
 3. Pallisade parenchyma are oval or round and loosely arranged.
 
 4. There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between parenchymal cells.
explanation: Mesophyll has two types of cells – the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma. Spongy parenchyma oval or round and loosely arranged. Palisade parenchyma is made up of elongated cells and are adaxially placed. There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between parenchymal cells. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 93; Paragraph 2)

 3. In the reticulate venation of the dicot leaves, the veins have the same thickness.
 
 4. The vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thin walled bundle sheath cells.
explanation: Vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib. The size of the vascular bundles are dependent on the size of the veins. question:
Consider the following statements regarding secondary growth and choose the correct option.
 
 1. The lengthening of roots and stems mediated by lateral meristem is called primary growth.
 
 2. The increase in girth in dicot plants is called the secondary growth.
 
 3. Apical meristem and cork cambium involve in secondary growth.
 
 4. Vascular cambium is made with apical meristem.
explanation: The growth of the roots and stems in length with the help of apical meristem is called the primary growth. The increase in girth in dicot plants is called the secondary growth. Seconday growth is not mediated by the apical meristem. The tissues involved in secondary growth are the two lateral meristems: vascular cambium and cork cambium. Vascular cambium is a lateral meristem. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 94; Paragraph 3)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding vascular cambium and choose the correct option.
 
 1. In the young stem it is present in patches as a single layer between the xylem and phloem.
 
 2. Intrafascicular cambium is present between primary xylem and the primary phloem.
 
 3. Cambium ring cuts off the new cells only towards inside.
 
 4. The cells cut off towards the pith mature to secondary phloem.
explanation: In the young stem the vascular cambium is present in patches as a single layer between the xylem and phloem. the cells of cambium that are present between primary xylem and primary phloem is called intrafascicular cambium. Active cambial ring cuts off cells not only towards inside, but also towards outside. The cells which are cut off towards pith, mature into secondary xylem. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 94; Paragraph 3)

 3. In some places the cambium forms secondary medullary rays.
 
 4. In spring seasons in temperate climates cambium is less active and forms fewer xylary elements
explanation: The primary and secondary phloems get gradually crushed due to the continued formation and accumulation of secondary xylem. But the primary xylem remains intact, in or around the centre. At some places, the cambium forms a narrow band ofparenchyma, which passes through the secondary xylem and the secondary phloem in the radial directions, hence called are secondary medullary rays. In the spring season, cambium is very active and produces a large number of xylary elements. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 96; Paragraph 1)

question:

 1. The cork cambium develops later in cortex to provide protective cell layers.
 
 2. It is made up of broad, thick walled cells.
 
 3. Outer cells cut off by the cork cambium differentiate into secondary cortex.
 
 4. The parenchymal cells in the cork is permeable to water.
explanation: Cork cambium or phellogen develops, usually in the cortex region. It provides a new protective cell layer. . It is made of narrow, thin-walled and nearly rectangular cells. The outer cells cut by the phallogen differentiate into cork or phellem while the inner cells differentiate into secondary cortex or phelloderm. The cork is impermiable to water due to suberin deposition in the cell wall. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 97; Paragraph 1)

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Bark refers to all tissues interior to the vascular cambium.
 
 2. Bark includes periderm and secondary xylem.
 
 3. Lenticles are formed with parenchymal cells.
 
 4. Lenticels permit the exchange of gasses between the outer atmosphere and the internal tissue of the stem.
explanation: Bark refers to all tissues exterior to the vascular cambium. Bark includes periderm and secondary phloem. Lenticles are formed with parenchymal cells rupturing the epidermis. Lenticels permit the exchange of gases between the outer atmosphere and the internal tissue of the stem. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 97; Paragraph 2)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the anatomy of flowering plants and choose the incorrect option. 
 
 1. Anatomy is the external structure of plants.
 
 2. Tissue is the basic unit of the plant.
 
 3. There are similarities in the internal structure of several plants.
 
 4. Internal structures are adapted to diverse environments.
explanation: Anatomy is the study of internal structure of the plants, but not the external structure. The cell is the basic unit of the plant, and a tissue is made up of a group of cells. Different organs in a plant show similarities as well as differences in their internal structure. Internal structures show adaptations to diverse environments.(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 84; Paragraph 1 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Cell is the basic unit of the plant.
 
 2. Monocot plants and Dicot plants are anatomically similar.
 
 3. Different organs in a plant show differences in their internal structure.
 
 4. Several cells get together and form organs.
explanation: The cell is the basic unit of the plant. The monocots and dicots are also seen to be anatomically different. Different organs in a plant show differences in their internal structure. Several tissues get together to form organs. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 84; Paragraph 1 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Tissue is a group of cells performing a common function.
 
 2. Tissues are made up of cells with different origins.
 
 3. Permanent tissues can divide further.
 
 4. Meristematic tissues show active cell division.
explanation: A tissue is a group of cells with a common origin and performing a common function. Meristematic tissues actively divide further but permanent tissues do not. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 84; Paragraph 2 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Meristems are the specialized regions of active cell division.
 
 2. Growth in plants is restricted to meristems.
 
 3. Almost all the plants have the same region as meristems.
 
 4. In apical meristems, meristem occurs at the tip of the roots or shoots.
explanation: Meristems are specialised regions of active cell division. Growth in plants is largely restricted to meristems. Plants have different parts as meristems. The meristems which occur at the tips of roots and shoots and produce primary tissues are called apical meristems. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 84; Paragraph 3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Shoot apical meristem occupies the distant most region of the stem axis.
 
 2. Axillary bud is formed from the left behinds from root apical meristems.
 
 3. Axillary buds are capable of forming a branch or a flower.
 
 4. Root apical meristems occupy the tips of the root.
explanation: Root apical meristem occupies the tip of a root while the shoot apical meristem occupies the distant most region of the stem axis. Axillary bud is formed from the left behinds from shoot apical meristems. They are capable of forming a branch or a flower. Root apical meristem occupies the tip of a root. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 84; Paragraph 1 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
 
 1. The meristem which occurs in between the mature tissues is known as intercalary meristem.
 
 2. Apical meristem is a secondary meristem.
 
 3. Intercalary meristem occurs in grass.
 
 4. Lateral and intercalary meristems are primary meristems.
explanation: Intercalary meristem occurs between the mature tissues. They occur in grasses and regenerate parts removed by the grazing herbivores. Both apical and intercalary meristem are primary meristems while the lateral meristems are secondary meristems. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 85; Paragraph 1 )

explanation: Both apical and intercalary meristems are primary meristems but not the secondary meristems. They are known so because they appear early in life of a plant and contribute to the formation of the primary plant body. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 85; Paragraph 1)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding meristems and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Intercalary meristem regenerates parts of the grasses removed by grazing herbivores.
 
 2. Secondary meristems appear later than primary meristems.
 
 3. Secondary meristems produce woody axis.
 
 4. Interfascicular cambium is an example of an intercalary meristem.
explanation: Intercalary meristem is seen in grasses and regenerates parts removed by the grazing herbivores. Primary meristems occur early in life and secondary meristems occur later. Secondary meristem occurs in mature regions of roots and shoots and produces woody axis. Fascicular vascular cambium, interfascicular cambium and cork-cambium are examples of lateral meristems which are responsible to produce secondary tissues. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 85; Paragraph 2 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding secondary meristems and choose the correct option.
 
 1. They occur in the mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants.
 
 2. Fascicular vascular cambium is an example for a secondary meristem.
 
 3. They are responsible for producing secondary tissues.
 
 4. They are spherical in shape.
explanation: Secondary meristems occur in mature regions of roots and shoots of many plants. Fascicular vascular cambium, interfascicular cambium and cork-cambium are examples of lateral meristems. They are cylindrical in shape, not spherical. They are responsible for producing secondary tissues.  (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 85; Paragraph 2 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding cell division in plants and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Following division, structurally and functionally specialized cells are made.
 
 2. Immature cells constitute the permanent tissues.
 
 3. Newly formed structurally and functionally specialised cells have the ability to divide further.
 
 4. Dermal tissues and vascular tissues are formed during the formation of primary plant body.
explanation: After the primary and the secondary division, the formed cells are structurally and functionally specialized and don't have the ability to divide further. Dermal tissues, ground tissues and vascular tissues are produced by specific regions of apical meristem. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 85; Paragraph 3 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding permanent tissues and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Cells in the permanent tissues can divide further.
 
 2. Complex tissues have different types of cells.
 
 3. In simple tissues, cells are similar in structure but different in function.
 
 4. Permanent tissues are made up of mature cells.
explanation: Cells in the permanent tissues do not usually divide further. Permanent tissues with different types of cells are called complex tissues Permanent tissues are composed of mature cells. In simple tissues all cells are similar in structure and function. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 86; Paragraph 1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding simple tissues and choose the correct option.
 
 1. A simple tissue comprises two or three types of cells.
 
 2. Parenchyma and Collenchyma are complex tissues while sclerenchyma is a simple tissue.
 
 3. Parenchymal cells are isodiametric.

explanation: A simple tissue is made of only one type of cells. The various simple tissues in plants are parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. Parenchymal cells are isodiametric.  They may be spherical, oval, round, polygonal or elongated in shape.(Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 86; Paragraph 1)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding sclerenchyma and choose the correct option.
 
 1. They have non-lignified cell walls with pits.
 
 2. They are living cells with protoplasts.
 
 3. Fibres and sclereids are the two types of sclerenchyma.
 
 4. Fibres are commonly found in fruit walls and nuts.
explanation: Sclerenchyma have thick and lignified cell walls with pits. They are non living cells without protoplasts. Fibres and sclereids are the two types of sclerenchyma. The fibres are thick-walled, elongated and pointed cells, occuring in groups, in various parts of the plant. Scleirids are the ones commonly found in the fruit, walls of nuts not the fibres. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 86; Paragraph 4 )

question:
Consider the following statements regarding complex tissues and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Complex tissues are made of one type of cells.
 
 2. Xylem and phloem are complex tissues.
 
 3. Phloem conducts water and minerals from root to stem.
 
 4. Xylem provides mechanical strength to plant parts.
explanation: The complex tissues are made of more than one type of cells which work together as a unit. t. Xylem and phloem are the complex tissues in plants. Xylem conducts water and minerals from root to stem and provides mechanical support to plant parts. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 87; Paragraph 1 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding xylem and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Xylem is composed of tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres and xylem parenchyma. 
 
 2. Gymnosperms have vessels in their xylem.
 
 3. Tracheids have thick lignified walls.
 
 4. Tracheids have a protoplasm.
explanation: Xylem is composed of four different kinds of elements, namely, tracheids, vessels, xylem fibres and xylem parenchyma. Gymnosperms do not have vessels in their xylem. Tracheids are elongated or cells with thick and lignified walls and tapering ends. Trachieds are dead and without protoplasm. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 87; Paragraph 2 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:

 1. Inner layers of cell walls are with uniform thickness.
 
 2. In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water transporting elements.
 
 3. Vessels are cylindrical and have a protoplasm.
 
 4. Vessels have a large central cavity.
explanation: The inner layers of the cells in the xylem are not with uniform, they vary in thickness. In flowering plants, tracheids and vessels are the main water transporting elements. Vessels are cylindrical, but devoid of protoplasm. They are with a lignified wall and a large central cavity. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 87; Paragraph 2 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding vessels and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Vessels are characteristic to gymnosperms.
 
 2. Vessel members are interconnected through perforations in their common walls.
 
 3. Vessel is a long cylindrical structure.
 
 4. Vessels have obliterated central lumens
explanation: Vessels are characteristic to angiosperms. Gymnosperms lack vessels. Vessel members are interconnected through perforations in their common walls. Vessel is a long cylindrical tube-like structure with no obliterations in central lumen. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 87; Paragraph 2 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding xylem and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Xylem fibre lumens are always aseptate.
 
 2. Xylem parenchyma have thick walls made of cellulose.
 
 3. They store food in the form of starch and fat.
 
 4. The radial conduction of water occurs through xylem fibre.
explanation: Xylem fibre lumens can either be septate or aseptate. Xylem parenchyma cells are living cells and thin walls made up of cellulose. They store food materials in the form of starch or fat, and other substances like tannins. The radial conduction of water takes place by the ray parenchymatous cells. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 87; Paragraph 2 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:

 2. Metaxylem lies towards the periphery of the organ in roots.
 
 3. Primary xylem in the stem is called endarch.
 
 4. In roots metaxylem lies towards the center while the first formed primary xylem lies towards the periphery of the organs.
explanation: Protoxylem is the first formed primary xylem and in the stem it lies towards the centre of the organs. Protoxylem in the stem is known as endarch. In roots metaxylem lies towards the centre and the protoxylem lies towards the periphery. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 87; Paragraph 2)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding phloem and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Phloem transports food materials from leaves to other parts of the plant.
 
 2. Angiosperm phloem have albuminous cells and sieve cells.
 
 3. Gymnosperms have sieve tubes and companion cells.
 
 4. Sieve tubes are associated with companion cells.
explanation: Phloem transports food materials, from leaves to other parts of the plant. Phloem in angiosperms has sieve tube elements, companion cells, phloem parenchyma and phloem fibres but not albuminous cells. Gymnosperms have albuminous cells and sieve cells. Sieve tube elements are associated with companion cells. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 87; Paragraph 3)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
 
 1. The end walls of sieve tube elements are perforated in a sieve-like manner to form the sieve plates.
 
 2. The companion cells are specialized collenchymatous cells.
 
 3. The sieve tube elements and companion cells are connected by pit fields.
 
 4. The companion cells help in maintaining the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes.
explanation: End walls of the sieve tube elements are perforated in a sieve-like manner to form the sieve plates. The companion cells are specialised parenchymatous cells not collenchymatous. . The sieve tube elements and companion cells are connected by pit fields which are present between their common longitudinal walls. The companion cells help in maintaining the pressure gradient in the sieve tubes. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 88; Paragraph 1 )
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Phloem parenchyma has dense cytoplasm and nucleus
 
 2. Cell wall is made up of cellulose and has pits
 
 3. All monocotyledons have phloem parenchyma.
 
 4. Phloem fibre are made of collenchyma.
explanation: Phloem parenchyma is made up of elongated, tapering cylindrical cells which have dense cytoplasm and nucleus. The cell wall is composed of cellulose and has pits. In most of the monocotyledons phloem parenchyma is absent. Phloem fibres are made up of sclerenchyma cells. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 88; Paragraph 1 )

question:
Consider the following statements regarding phloem and choose the correct option.

 2. Phloem fibres are elongated, unbranched and have pointed, needle like apices.
 
 3. Phloem fibres has thin cell walls.

explanation: Phloem fibres are usually absent in the primary phloem but present in the secondary phloem. Phloem fibres are are much elongated, unbranched and have pointed, needle like apices. Phloem fibres are thick walled. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 88; Paragraph 1)
topic_name: Structural Organisation In Plants And Animals >> Anatomy of Flowering Plants >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the tissue system and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Tissues vary depending on their location in the plant body.
 
 2. Tissue systems are of two types depending on their structure and location.
 
 3. The epidermal tissue system forms the outer-most layer of the plant body.
 
 4. Epidermal appendages are the trichomes and hair.
explanation: Tissues vary depending on their location in the plant body. Tissue systems are of three types depending on their structure and location. The epidermal tissue system forms the outer-most layer of the primary plant body. Tricomes and hair are epidermal appendages. (Reference  s: NCERT Chapter 6; Page 88; Paragraph 2)

question:
Consider the following statements and choose the correct option.
 
 1. Epidermis has a continuous layer of loosely arranged cells.
 
 2. Epidermal cells are multilayered parenchymal cells.
 
 3. Epidermis is covered from the outside with stomata.
 
 4. Cuticles regulate the process of transpiration and gaseous exchange.
explanation: The epidermis has a compactly arranged continuous layer of cells. Epidermal cells are single layered parenchymal cells. Outside the epidermis is covered with cuticle.
