question: Match the following group of organisms with the level of organisation with the tabular diagram? (0452)
explanation: Though all members of Animalia are multicellular, all of them do not exhibit the same pattern of organisation of cells. For example, in sponges, the cells are arranged as loose cell aggregates, i.e., they exhibit cellular level of organisation. Some division of labour (activities) occur among the cells. In coelenterates, the arrangement of cells is more complex. Here the cells performing the same function are arranged into tissues, hence is called tissue level of organisation. A still higher level of organisation, i.e., organ level is exhibited by members of Platyhelminthes and other higher phyla where tissues are grouped together to form organs, each specialised for a particular function. In animals like Annelids, Arthropods, Molluscs, Echinoderms and Chordates, organs have associated to form functional systems,each system concerned with a specific physiological function. This pattern is called organ system level of organisation. (Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page 46,47)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Basis of Classification

question:
Consider the following statements: 

i. All members of Animalia are multicellular. 

ii. The digestive system in Platyhelminthes has only a single opening to the outside of the body that serves as both mouth and anus. 

iii. In aschelminthes the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. 

iv. Notochord is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the ventral side during embryonic development. 

Which of the above statements are true?
explanation:
The digestive system in Platyhelminthes has only a single opening to the outside of the body that serves as both mouth and anus, and is hence called incomplete(type of digestive sysytem). In some animals, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. Such a body cavity is called pseudocoelom and the animals possessing them are called pseudocoelomates, e.g., aschelminthes. Notochord is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on the dorsal side during embryonic development. (Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page 46,47,48)
Aschelminthes are triploblastic but the mesoderm layer, doesn't neccesarily have to line the body cavity like Eucoelomates, it can be present as scattered pouches, which indicates that they(aschelminthes) are one of the most primitive triploblastic animals to evolve.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Basis of Classification

question:

i. The circulatory system is of three types- open, closed and mixed. 

ii. Open type in which the blood is pumped out of the heart and the cells and tissues are directly bathed in it. 

iii. Closed type in which the blood is circulated through a series of vessels of varying diameters (arteries, veins and capillaries). 

iv. Mixed type in which blood is circulated through a series of vessels in the upper part of the body while the cells and tissues in the lower part of the body are directly bathed in it. 

Which of the above statements are True?
explanation: The circulatory system may be of two types: (i) open type in which the blood is pumped out of the heart and the cells and tissues are directly bathed in it and (ii) closed type in which the blood is circulated through a series of vessels of varying diameters (arteries, veins and capillaries). (Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page 47; paragraph 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Basis of Classification

Animals like annelids, arthropods, etc., where the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane, exhibit bilateral symmetry.(Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page 47; paragraph 4)

question:

answer: Both assertion and reason are true but reason is not a correct explanation of the assertion.
explanation: All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates because chordata includes other subphylums also besides Vertibrata- Urochordata or Tunicata and Cephalochordata. Thus phylum Chordata is divided into three subphyla: Urochordata or Tunicata, Cephalochordata and Vertebrata. Subphyla Urochordata and Cephalochordata are often referred to as protochordates and are exclusively marine. In Urochordata, notochord is present only in larval tail, while in Cephalochordata, it extends from head to tail region and is persistent throughout their life. The members of subphylum Vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period. The notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in the adult. (Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page 55)

explanation: The molluscs have a soft body surrounded by an external calcareous shell. The echinoderms possess a spiny skin. Their most distinctive feature is the presence of water vascular system. question:
Which of the following statements are true for the Phylum Chordata?[NEET 2020]

(A) In Urochordata, notochord extends from head to tail and it is present throughout their life.

(B) In Vertebrata, notochord is present during the embryonic period only.

(C) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow.

(D) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla : Hemichordata, Tunicata and Cephalochordata.
explanation: In Urochordata, notochord is present only in larval tail. Phylum Chordata is divided into three subphyla : Urochordata or Tunicata, Cephalochordata and Vertebrata.(Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page-55)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question:
Consider following features. 
Select the correct option of animal groups which possess all the above characteristics.
[NEET 2019]

(A) Organ system level of organisation 

(B) Bilateral symmetry 

(C) True coelomates with segmentation of body
explanation: Mollusca shows organ system level of organisation with unsegmented body (except Neopilina which is a segmented mollusc) having distinct head, muscular foot and visceral hump. They usually show bilateral symmetry but some molluscs (example Pila) become asymmetrical due to torsion.(Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page-55,53)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following animals are true coelomates with bilateral symmetry?[Odisha NEET 2019]
explanation: Among the followings Annelids is best answer.(Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page-52, Paragraph-2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following animals does not undergo metamorphosis?[NEET 2018]
explanation: Metamorphosis is the process of transformation of an immature larva into an adult form in two or more distinct stages. Animals that undergo metamorphosis are said to have indirect development, e.g., tunicates, moth,starfish, etc. In case of earthworm, development is direct which means no larval stage is present and hence, there is no metamorphosis.(Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page-52,Paragraph-2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Identify the vertebrate groupof animals characterised by crop and gizzard in its digestive system.[NEET 2018]
explanation: The alimentary canal of birds have additional chambers, the crop and gizzard. Crop stores and softens the food, however the gizzard helps in crushing and churning the food.(Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page-58,Paragraph-2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of these animals is not a homeotherm?[NEET 2018]
explanation: Homeotherms are the animals that maintain constant body temperature, irrespective of surrounding temperature by metabolic activity, e.g., birds and mammals. Turtle (Chelone) belongs to Class Reptilia and is poikilotherm or cold blooded.(Reference  : NCERT Biology, Class 11; Page-58,Paragraph-1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Important characteristic that hemichordates share with chordates is [NEET 2017]
explanation: An important characteristics that hemichordates and chordates share is presence of pharyngeal gill slits. Gill slits are dorsal in position in hemichordates whereas they are lateral in chordates. A true unotochord does not occur in hemichordates. Nervous system is distinctly of vertebrate type being intraepidermal in position and having a ventral nerve cord.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which among these is the correct combination of aquatic mammals? [NEET 2017]
explanation: Whales, dolphin and seals are examples of aquatic mammals. Trygon and sharks are cartilaginous fishes. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 60; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following represents order of ‘horse’? [NEET 2017]
explanation: Perissodactyla represents the order of horse. Equidae is the family, caballus is the subspecies whereas E. ferus is the species of horse.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: In case of poriferans, the spongocoel is lined with flagellated cells called [NEET 2017]
explanation: Spongocoel is the central body cavity of the sponges. It is lined by highly specialised flagellated cells called choanocytes. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 49; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Choose the correct statement. [NEET 2016]
answer: All cyclostomes do not possess jaws and paired fins.
explanation: Ornithorhynchus and Tachyglossus are oviparous mammals. Crocodile is a reptile which possesses four chambered heart. In cartilaginous fish (except Chimaera) gills are not covered by an operculum. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 54, 56, 58 and 60)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_b: All cyclostomes do not possess jaws and paired fins.
option_c: All reptiles have a three chambered heart.
option_d: All pisces have gills covered by an operculum

question: Which one of the following characteristics is not shared by birds and mammals? [NEET 2016]
explanation: All birds are oviparous while all mammals except Ornithorhyncus (duck billed platypus) and Echidna or Tachyglossus (spiny anteater) are viviparous.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following features is not present in the phylum arthropoda? [NEET 2016]
explanation: Parapodia are flattened, fleshy, vertical flaplike outgrowths of body wall found in annelids on lateral sides of trunk segments. These are hollow structures enclosing coelom which is continuous with that of trunk segments. These serve the dual purpose of locomotion and respiration. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 52; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Body having meshwork of cells, internal cavities lined with food filtering flagellated cells and indirect development are the characteristics ofphylum [NEET 2015]
explanation: Phylum Porifera (the sponges) has cellular level of body organisation, with inner cellular layer consisting of highly specialised flagellated cells called choanocytes (or collar cells). The development in this phylum is indirect as it includes a free swimming larva called amphiblastula or parenchymula for dispersal of the species.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Metagenesis refers to [NEET 2015]
answer: Alternation of generation between asexual and sexual phases of an organism
explanation: An alternation of generation between asexual and sexual phases of an organism is referred to as metagenesis. E.g. in Obelia (a coelenterate), polyps reproduce asexually and medusae reproduce sexually. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 50; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Occurrence of a drastic change in form during postembryonic development
option_b: Presence of a segmented body and parthenogenetic mode of reproduction
option_d: Alternation of generation between asexual and sexual phases of an organism

question: A jawless fish, which lays eggs in fresh water and whose ammocoetes larvae after metamorphosis return to the ocean is [NEET 2015]
explanation: Petromyzon (Lamprey) belongs to the Class Cyclostomata of Phylum Chordata. It is a jawless fish which lays eggs in fresh water. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 56; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following endoparasites of humans does show viviparity? [NEET 2015 cancelled]
explanation: Trichinella spiralis is a minute nematode parasite that shows viviparity i.e., produces live youngs (larvae) not eggs. The adults of T. spiralis live in the human small intestine, where the females release large numbers of larvae. These larvae bore through the intestine and can cause trichinosis or trichiniasis which has symptoms like diarrohea, nausea, vertigo, pain in limbs and fever etc. Humans get infected after eating imperfectly cooked meat infected with the parasite’s larval cysts.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following animals is not viviparous? [2015 cancelled]
explanation: Duckbilled platypus is an egg laying mammal. It is found in the rivers in eastern Australia and Tasmania. It is a beaver like monotreme about (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 60; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following characteristics is mainly responsible for diversification of insects on land? [2015 cancelled]
explanation: Exoskeleton made of cuticle has enabled insects to live on land and to diversify to almost all the possible habitats. It gives them protection, support and also helps to prevent desiccation.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Select the taxon mentioned that represents both marine and fresh water species. [2014]
explanation: Cnidarians are the saclike animals which are aquatic, mostly marine except a few like Hydra, are fresh water. They are the simplest organisms that have attained a tissue level of organization. Members of Ctenophora, Cephalochordata and Echinodermata are exclusively marine. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 50; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following living organisms completely lacks a cell wall? [2014]
explanation: Gorgonia (sea fan) is an animal belonging to phylum Coelenterata. All animals lack cell wall.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Planaria possesses high capacity of [2014]
explanation: Planaria possesses high degree of regeneration. Both epimorphosis, in which the missing parts are formed and morphallaxis, in which the whole body can be regenerated from a fragment of the body, occurs. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 51; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: A marine cartilaginous fish that can produce electric current is [2014]
explanation: Torpedo is a bottomliving marine fish, discharging electricity which is sufficient to stun preys such as small fishes, etc. A pair of electric organs are situated on the dorsal side of the trunk region. Infact the electric organs are the modified lateral muscleplates innervated by the cranial nerves. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 57; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which of the following are correctly matched with respect to their taxonomic classification? [NEET 2013]
answer: House fly, butterfly, tsetse fly, silver fish - insecta
explanation: Spiny anteater (Echidna) is a prototherian mammal whereas, sea urchins and sea cucumber are echinoderms. Silver fish (Lepisma) is an insect, Cuttle fish (Sepia) is a mollusc and flying fish (Exocoetus) is a bony fish. Centipede is class chilopoda, Millipede is class diplopoda and Scorpion and Spider are class arachnida of Phylum Arthropoda. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 57 and 60)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: House fly, butterfly, tsetse fly, silver fish - insecta
option_b: Spiny anteater, sea urchin, sea cucumber - Echinodermata
option_c: Flying fish, cuttle fish, silver fish-Pisces

question: Which group of animals belong to the same phylum? [NEET 2013]
explanation: Prawn, Scorpion and Locusta belong to the phylum Arthropoda. All other animals categories are given below: Sponge ® Porifera Sea anemone ® Coelenterata Starfish ® Echinodermata Malarial parasite, Amoeba ® Protozoa Mosquito ® Arthropoda Earthworm ® Annelida Pinworm ® Aschelminthes Tapeworm ® Platyhelminthes. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 53; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: One of the representatives of phylum arthropoda is [NEET 2013]
explanation: Phylum Arthropoda is the largest phylum of Animalia which includes insects. Examples include Apis, silkworm, Laccifer, silver fish (Lepisma), locust, etc. Puffer fish and flying fish (Exocoetus) are examples of superclass Pisces, while cuttle fish (Sepia) belongs to Mollusca.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: The characteristics of class reptilia are [Karnataka NEET 2013]
answer: Body covered with dry and cornified skin, scales over the body are epidermal, they do not have external ears
explanation: Reptiles represent the first class of vertebrates fully adapted for life in dry places on land. The characters of reptiles are in fact a combination of characters that are found in fish and amphibians on one hand and birds and mammals on the other. Their exoskeleton is of horny epidermal scales, shields, plates and scutes. The skin is dry, cornified and devoid of glands. Reptiles lack external ears and have immovable eyelids.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 58; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Body covered with moist skin which is devoid of scales, the ear is represented by a tympanum, alimentary canal, urinary and reproductive tracts open into a common cloaca
option_b: Fresh water animals with bony endoskeleton, airbladder to regulate buoyancy
option_c: Marine animals with cartilaginous endoskeleton, body covered with placoid scales
option_d: Body covered with dry and cornified skin, scales over the body are epidermal, they do not have external ears

question: Which one of the following groups of animals reproduces only by sexual means? [Karnataka NEET 2013]
explanation: In ctenophores, asexual reproduction is absent. They are monoecious and fertilization is generally external. In cnidaria, asexual reproduction (budding) is found in the polyps and sexual reproduction is found in the medusa form. Both asexual and sexual reproduction occur in porifera (sponges). Asexual reproduction occurs by budding and gemmules. In protozoa, asexual reproduction takes place by binary fission, budding etc. and sexual reproduction takes place by syngamy and conjugation.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 51; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Sharks and dog fishes differ from skates and rays because [Karnataka NEET 2013]
answer: Their pectoral fins are distinctly marked off from cylindrical bodies
explanation: Sharks and dogfishes have cylindrical body while skates and rays have both of their pectoral fins fused. It gives a winglike appearance and are not distinct from body.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_b: Head and trunk are widened considerably
option_c: Distinct demarcation between body and tail
option_d: Their pectoral fins are distinctly marked off from cylindrical bodies

question: Pheretima and its close relatives derive nourishment from [2012]
answer: Decaying fallen leaves and soil organic matter
explanation: Pheretima (earthworm) and related organisms feed upon the decaying organic matter found in the soil. They also feed on the bits of plants and animal matter. Thus, they are saprophytes.

answer: All bony fishes have four pairs of gills and an operculum on each side
explanation: All bony fishes have four pairs of gills and an operculum on each side, it has no exception rest all options has one or more exception.Crocodile in reptiles has 4 chambered heart.Some sponges may live in fresh water.Ornithorhynchus is an oviparous mammal.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 57; Paragraph No. 3)

question: What will you look for to identify the sex of the following? [2011]
answer: Male shark - claspers borne on pelvic fins
explanation: Tail end is straight in female Ascaris, while tail end is curved ventral words in male Ascaris. Anal cerci is present in both male and female cockroach, while anal style is present only in the male cockroach. The forelimbs in both frogs (male and female) bear small articular pads dorsally at the joints of digit, but the males possess a special nuptial, copulatory pad on ventral side of the first finger of each forelimb. Copulatory pad appears merely as rough patches, but during breeding season, these become thick and sticky. In copulation, the male strongly grips a female under her armpits by means of these pads. Claspers are modified inner edges of pelvic fins in male sharks. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 57; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Female ascari - sharply curved posterior end
option_b: Male frog - copulatory pad on the first digit of the hind limb
option_d: Male shark - claspers borne on pelvic fins

question: Which one of the following groups of animals is correctly matched with its characteristic feature without any exception? [2011]
explanation: Crocodile in reptiles has 4 chambered heart.Some chordates maybe jawless like agnatha.Ornithorhynchus is oviparous mammal.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 56; Paragraph No. 3)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

option_b: Chordata : possess a mouth with an upper and a lower jaw

question: Which one of the following statements is totally wrong about the occurrence of notochord, while the other three are correct? [Mains 2011]
answer: It is absent throughout life in humans from the very beginning.
explanation: Humans are mammals which are chordates. Phylum chordata includes animals which possess a notochord either throughout or during early embryonic life. In Ascidia (urochordata), notochord is present only in larval tail while in Amphioxus (cephalochordata), it extends from head to tail region and is persistent throughout their life. It is replaced by a vertebral column in adult frog.  (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 55; Paragraph No. 4)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: It is present only in larval tail in ascidian.
option_b: It is replaced by a vertebral column in adult frog.
option_c: It is absent throughout life in humans from the very beginning.
option_d: It is present throughout life in amphioxus

question: Ureters act as urinogenital ducts in [Mains 2011]
explanation: In male frogs, two ureters act as urinogenital duct which open into the cloaca. They run backwards from the kidneys and open into the cloaca. In female ureters carry urine alone, while in male both sperms and urine are carried. Hence, are called urinogenital ducts.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: One example of animals having a single opening to the outside that serves both as mouth as well as anus is [2010]
explanation: In Fasciola (flatworms) the body has a single cavity with one opening to the outside. The single opening functions as both mouth for ingestion (intake of food) and anus for egestion (undigested food is passed out). It is called blind sac plan. Other examples are coelenterates.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following statements about all the four of spongilla, leech, dolphin and penguin is correct? [2010]
answer: Spongilla has special collared cells called choanocytes, not found in the remaining three.
explanation: Spongilla is a common, widely distributed fresh water sponge belonging to phylum porifera. Canal system in Spongilla is essentially of rhagon type with choanocytes restricted to small rounded chambers. It is not found in leech, dolphin and penguin. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 49; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Penguin is homoiothermic while the remaining three are poikilothermic.
option_b: Leech is a fresh water form while all others are marine.
option_c: Spongilla has special collared cells called choanocytes, not found in the remaining three.

question: Which one of the following kinds of animals are triploblastic? [2010]
explanation: Triploblastic is a condition which describes an animal having a body composed of three embryonic germ layers : the ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm. Most multicellular animals belonging to phylum platyhelminthes to phylum chordata are triploblastic. Ctenophores, sponges and corals are diploblastic.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 51; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following statements about certain given animals is correct? [Mains 2010]
explanation: Acoelomates are animals having no body cavity or coelom. Examples are poriferans coelenterates, ctenophora, platyhelminthes and nemertinea. In pseudocoelomates, body space is pseudocoelom or false coelom. Examples are ectoprocta, aschelminthes. In coelomates, body space is a true coelom enclosed by mesoderm on both sides. Remaining phyla of bilateria, from annelida to arthropoda are coelomates. Molluses and insects are coelomates while flatworms are acoelomates.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 52; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: In which one of the following organisms its excretory organs are correctly stated? [Mains 2010]
answer: Earthworm – pharyngeal, integumentary and septal nephridia
explanation: Nephridia is the excretory organ of the earthworm. Earthworms have three types of nephridial structures called as septal, integumentary and pharyngeal nephridia. These three nephridial structures are present on different positions in the body and also vary in structures. Septal and pharyngeal nephridia are both enteronephric i.e., nitrogen products are expelled in gut. Integumentary nephridia is exonephric i.e., nitrogen waste products are directly discharged outside. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 52; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Humans – kidneys, sebaceous glands and tear glands
option_b: Earthworm – pharyngeal, integumentary and septal nephridia
option_c: Cockroach – malpighian tubules and enteric caeca
option_d: Frog – kidneys, skin and buccal epithelium

question: Crocodile and penguin are similar to whale and dogfish in which one of the following features? [Mains 2010]
answer: Have gill slits at some stage
explanation: Animals belonging to Phylum Chordata are fundamentally characterised by the presence of a notochord, a dorsal hollow nerve cord and paired pharyngeal gill slits. Crocodile, penguin, whale and dogfish are all chordates. All of them have gill slits or have had it during embryonic development. Thus, paired gill slits are present in these animal at some stage of life. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 55; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Possess a solid single stranded central nervous system
option_b: Lay eggs and guard them till they hatch
option_d: Have gill slits at some stage

question: Which one of the following groups of animals is bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic? [2009]
explanation: Aschelminthes is a superphylum consisting of pseudocoelomates. These are mostly aquatic, free living or parasitic. Their body is slender, bilaterally symmetrical and triploblastic. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 52; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: If a live earthworm is pricked with a needle on its outer surface without damaging its gut, the fluid that comes out is [2009]
explanation: Coelom or body cavity of earthworm is filled with coelomic fluid. It lies between body wall and alimentary canal. So if a live earthworm is pricked with a needle on its outer surface without damaging the gut then only coelomic fluid will come out.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following pairs of animals comprises ‘jawless fishes’? [2009]
explanation: Agnatha is subphylum or superclass of marine and fresh water vertebrates that lack jaws. They are fishlike animals with cartilaginous skeletons and welldeveloped sucking mouthparts with horny teeth. The only living agnathans are lampreys and hagfishes (Class Cyclostomata), which are parasites or scavengers.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 56; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following in birds, indicates their reptilian ancestry? [2008]
explanation: Birds have originated from some ancestral reptilian stalk. These two classes have so many features in common that link the two groups. The evidence of reptilian ancestry of birds is furnished by their comparative anatomy, embryology and palaeontology. One of the features is that all birds have horny epidermal scales confined to the lower parts of their legs and feet, which are exactly like the epidermal scales of the reptiles. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 58; Paragraph No. 3)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1
option_a: Two special chambers crop and gizzard in their digestive tract

question: Ascaris is characterized by [2008]
answer: Presence of neither true coelom nor metamerism
explanation: Ascaris belong to the Phylum Nematoda of Superphylum Aschelminthes. They have a cylindrical body without showing any metamerism, a pseudocoel (false coelom) and a complete digestive tract lined by endodermal epithelium. The cuticle covering the body surface bears minute transverse striations giving a pseudosegmented appearance to the worm.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 52; Paragraph No. 1)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

option_b: Presence of true coelom and metamerism (metamerisation)

question: Which one of the following pairs of items correctly belongs to the category of organs mentioned against it? [2008]
answer: Nephridia of earthworm and malpighian tubules of cockroach excretory organs
explanation: Nephridia are excretory organs of earthworm which consist of a simple or branched tube formed by the ingrowth of ectoderm with cilia at the inner end. Excretory products diffuse into the nephridium and are wafted to the exterior by ciliary action. Malpighian tubules are the organs that are involved in the excretion of nitrogenous wastes in cockroach. It open into the intestine; selectively extract from the blood uric acid, whichtogether with water and salts – is deposited into the hindgut and excreted in the faeces.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 52; Paragraph No. 2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following phyla is correctly matched with its two general characteristics? [2008]
answer: Arthropoda body divided into head, thorax and abdomen and respiration by tracheae
explanation: Arthropods are the largest phylum of Kingdom Animalia that characteristically possesses an outer body layer – the cuticle. The body is composed of segments usually forming distinct specialized body regions, i.e., head, thorax and abdomen. In them the trachea or windpipe or book lungs are the respiratory organs found in terrestrial forms, which help in respiration. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 53; Paragraph No. 1)

question: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of phylum annelida? [2008]
explanation: Phylum Annelida comprises invertebrates, which are segmented worms having cylindrical soft bodies showing metameric segmentation. These are triploblastic animals showing bilateral symmetry. A true coelom is present which is filled with coelomic fluid containing cells. Annelids are perhaps the first animals to have a true schizocoelic coelom.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 53; Paragraph No. 1)

question: Biradial symmetry and lack of cnidoblasts are the characteristics of [2006]
explanation: Ctenophora is a small phylum of exclusively marine, invertebrate animals. Ctenoplana and Beroe are examples of ctenophora. They have biradial symmetry (a combination of radial and bilateral symmetries). They lack the specialized stinging cells (nematocysts) found in coelenterates, but one species (Haeckelia rubra) incorporates those of its jellyfish prey for its own defense.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 51; Paragraph No. 1)

question: Which one of the following is not a living fossil? [2006]
explanation: Living fossil is a term for any living species (or clade) of organism which closely resembles species otherwise only known from fossils and has no close living relatives. These species have all survived major extinction events, and generally retain low taxonomic diversities. Some examples of living fossils in animals are – coelocanth, coral (polyp), crocodylia (crocodiles, gavials and alligators), horseshoe crab (Limulus polyphemus), monotremes (Platypus and Echidna), snoutnosed frog (Nasikabatrachus sahyadrensis). Archaeopteryx is the earliest and most primitive known bird to date. It lived in the Jurassic Period around.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 12; Page 130; Paragraph No. 1 and fig. 7.2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Metameric segmentation is the characteristic of [2006]
explanation: The term metamerism refers to a linear repetition of parts in an animal body. It occurs in three highly organized phyla : Annelida, Arthropoda and Chordata. Each segment is called a metamere, or somite. Segmentation often affects both external and internal structures. Such a condition is called metameric segmentation. In chordates, the segmentation is apparent only in the embryonic stage. In the adult chordates, segmentation is visible in the internal structures, such as vertebrae, ribs, nerves and blood vessels. Other animals have unsegmented bodies.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 52 and 53)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question: Which one of the following is a matching set of a phylum and its three examples? [2006]

The body is often divided into a head, with eyes or tentacles, a muscular foot and a visceral mass housing the organs. Loligo (squid or sea arrow), Teredo (shipworm), Octopus are some of their examples. In option (a) Spongilla and Euplectella belong to porifera but Pennatula (the sea pen or sea feather) belongs to coelenterata. In option (b) Physalia and Aurelia belong to cnidaria but Bonellia belongs to Phylum Annelida. In option (c) Planaria and Schistosoma belong to platyhelminthes but Enterobius (Pinworm) belongs to aschelminthes.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 54; Paragraph No. 1)

question: Which of the following is not found in birds? [1999]
explanation: Forelimbs are absent in birds as they are modified into wings for flight. They are attached high on the back, to the anterior or thoracic region of the trunk, and are very powerful when compared with the size and strength of the bird. Each wing is elongated, flattened and distally pointed with its longitudinal axis at right angles to that of the trunk. Hindlimb is made of three parts thigh, shank and foot. Pectoral girdle on each side consists of three bones a large coracoid, scapula and clavicle. Pelvic girdle consists of ilium, ischium and pubis.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 58; Paragraph No. 3)

question: Most appropriate term to describe the life cycle of obelia is [1998]
explanation: Obelia belongs to the Phylum Coelenterata. In Obelia, lifecycle includes two clearly defined phases : a fixed polypoid phase (hydroid colony) and a pelagic medusoid phase. Hydroid colony has no gonads and reproduces by asexual budding to give rise to medusae. On the other hand, medusae reproduce exclusively by sexual method (ova and sperms) to give rise to new hydroid colonies. This fact apparently seems to have given rise to the idea of alternation of generations, also called metagenesis. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 50; Paragraph No. 2)

question: The nephridia in earthworm are analogous to [1996]

question:
Select the correct statements : 
 (A) Platyhelminthes are triploblastic 
pseudocoelomate and bilaterally symmetrical 
organisms. 
 (B) Ctenophores reproduce only sexually and 
fertilization is external. 
 (C) In tapeworm, fertilization is internal but sexes 
are not separate. 
 (D) Ctenophores are exclusively marine, diploblastic and bioluminescent organisms. 
(E) In sponges, fertilization is external and 
development is direct. 
 Choose the correct answer from the options given 
below :[ NEET 2023(Phase 2)]
explanation:
Explanation: (A) Platyhelminthes are triploblastic pseudocoelomate and bilaterally symmetrical organisms. This statement is incorrect. Platyhelminthes are triploblastic, but they are acoelomate (lacking a body cavity) and exhibit bilateral symmetry.

(B) Ctenophores reproduce only sexually, and fertilization is external. This statement is correct. Ctenophores reproduce through external fertilization, where the male and female gametes are released into the water and fertilization occurs outside the body.
(C) In tapeworm, fertilization is internal, but sexes are not separate. This statement is correct. Tapeworms are hermaphroditic, meaning they have both male and female reproductive organs within the same individual. Fertilization occurs internally.

(D) Ctenophores are exclusively marine, diploblastic, and bioluminescent organisms. This statement is correct. Ctenophores are exclusively marine organisms, and they are diploblastic, having two germ layers (ectoderm and endoderm). Many species of ctenophores are bioluminescent
(E) In sponges, fertilization is external, and development is direct. This statement is not included in the given options.

Therefore, the correct option is 2. (B), (C), and (D) only.
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question:
Consider following statement regarding classification of animals and choose the correct option

explanation: Animals are classified into five different groups in a system given by Whittaker. This classification is based on features common to various individuals in relation to the arrangement of cells, body symmetry, nature of coelom, and patterns of digestive, circulatory or reproductive systems. This classification helps in assigning a systematic position to newly described species (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 46; Paragraph No.2)

question:
Consider following statement regarding organ systems in animals and choose the correct option
 
1. Organ level starts from Cnidaria such as Sea anemone

2. Digestive organs join to form incomplete digestive system in snail

3. Similar organs associated functionally to perform specific tasks

4. Highly complex organ systems are found in Platyhelminthes
explanation: Organ level has started in members of Platyhelminthes and extends to other higher phyla such as phylum annelida where tissues are grouped together to form organs, each specialised for a particular function. In animals like Annelids, Arthropods, Molluscs, Echinoderms and Chordates, organs have  associated to form functional systems, each system concerned with a specific physiological function. This pattern is called organ system level of organisation. Organ systems in different groups of animals exhibit various patterns of complexities. For example, the digestive system  in Platyhelminthes has only a single opening to the outside of the body that serves as bothmouth and anus, and is hence called incomplete. A complete digestive system has two openings, mouth and anus which are present in molluscs (phylum of snails), annelids, arthropods, echinoderms and all chordates. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 46, 47)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statement regarding the circulatory system and choose the correct option
 
1. Hemolymph is present in animals with a close circulatory system

2. Invertebrates with a close circulatory system are earthworms

3. Capillaries are one to reach tissues in the circulatory system

4. Major function of the circulatory system is to remove solutes
explanation: Circulatory system has two types i.e. open and close circulatory system. In open circulatory system, blood is not confined to vessels but in close circulatory system, blood is present in vessels. Hemolymph is present in animals with open circulatory system such as insects Close circulatory system is present in annelids and earthworm is one of them. Three types of veins are present in close circulatory system that are arteries, veins and capillaries and only the capillaries are those to reach tissues. The major function of circulatory system is to transport nutrients from one part of bosy to other (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 47; Paragraph No.2)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider following statement regarding symmetry and choose the correct option

1. Asymmetrical organisms are least modified such as starfish                                                                                                                                                                                                                        

2. Radial symmetry is usually the characteristic of invertebrates

3. Ctenophores are the only animals exhibiting bilateral symmetry

4. Any plane passing from center of bilateral animal divides it into equal halves
explanation: Animals can be categorised on the basis of their symmetry. Sponges are mostly asymmetrical, i.e., any plane that passes through the centre does not divide them into equal halves. Starfish belongs to Echinodermata so they are not asymmetrical They have modified form of radial symmetry called as pentaradial symmetry. When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry. Coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms have this kind of body plane. Animals like annelids, arthropods, etc., where the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane, exhibit bilateral symmetry (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 47; Paragraph No.3)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider following statement regarding diploblastic and triploblastic organisation and choose the correct option

1. Formation of three germs layers is definite feature of triploblastic organisation

2. Third and distinctive germinal layer in triploblastic organisms is endoderm 

3. Mesoglea is highly differentiated layer in diploblastic animals 

4. Chordates represent triploblastic levels of organisation
explanation: Animals in which the cells are arranged in two embryonic layers, an external ectoderm and an internal endoderm, are called diploblastic animals, e.g., coelenterates. An undifferentiated layer, mesoglea, is present in between the ectoderm and the endoderm. Those animals in which the developing embryo has a third germinal layer, mesoderm, in between the ectoderm and endoderm, are called triploblastic animals (platyhelminthes to chordates) Chordates usually include fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds and mammals. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 47, 48)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Animal Kingdom >> Assertion Reason and Multiple Statement Questions

question:
Consider following statement regarding coelom and choose the correct option 

1. Coelom is the cavity present between gut and body wall 

2. Endoderm directly lines the coelom in pseudocoelomates

3. On the bases of coelom, animals are classified into five categories

4. In chordates,coelom occupies a major space in abdomen
explanation: Presence or absence of a cavity between the bodywall and the gut wall is very important and one of the major feature in classification. Their are three types of animals on the bases of coelom. The body cavity, which is lined by mesoderm is called coelom. Animals possessing coelom are called coelomates, e.g., annelids, molluscs, arthropods, echinoderms, hemichordates and chordates. In chordates, coelom reduced to small cavities. In some animals, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. Such a body cavity is called pseudocoelom and the animals possessing them are called pseudocoelomates, e.g., aschelminthes. The animals in which the body cavity is absent are called acoelomates, e.g., platyhelminthes (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 48; Paragraph No.6)

3. Body cavity is not lined by mesoderm in false coelom

4. Coelom provides space for gametes in invertebrates
explanation: The presence or absence of a cavity between the bodywall and the gut wall is very important in classification. The body cavity, which is lined by mesoderm is called coelom. Animals possessing coelom are called coelomates, e.g., annelids, molluscs, arthropods, echinoderms, hemichordates and chordates. In some animals, the body cavity is not lined by mesoderm, instead, the mesoderm is present as scattered pouches in between the ectoderm and endoderm. Such a body cavity is called pseudocoelom and the animals possessing them are called pseudocoelomates, e.g., aschelminthes. The animals in which the body cavity is absent are called acoelomates, e.g., platyhelminthes. Coelom does not provide space for gametes but it acts as protective cushion for organs (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 48; Paragraph No.6)

Reason: In radial symmetry, any plane passing from the center of body divides the animal into equal right and left halves.
answer: If both Assertion and Reason are false.
explanation: When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry. Animals having dorsal tubular nerve cord are termed as chordates and they exhibit bilateral symmetry in which only one plane passing from the center of body divides the animal into equal right and left halves. Coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms have radial symmetry while hemichordates exhibit bilateral symmetry (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 47, Paragraph No. 3)

explanation: In some animals, the body is externally and internally divided into segments with a serial repetition of at least some organs. This phenomenon is called metamerism or segmentation. 3. Locusta, Limulus and Sea lilies have notochord which function in protection, support and movment

4. Notochord is one of distinctive feature of embryo of chordates.
explanation: Notochord is a mesodermally derived rod-like structure formed on only the dorsal side during embryonic development in some animals and persists in adults. Animals with notochord are called chordates (fishes- mammals) and those animals which do not form this structure are called non-chordates, e.g., porifera to echinoderms. Locusta and Limulus belongs to phylum arthropoda and Sea lilies belongs to phylum echinodermata. They come under the category of non chordates due to the absence of notochord (Reference  : NCERT Biology class 11; Page 48; Paragraph No. 4)

Consider following statement regarding phylum porifera and choose the correct option

1. Sponges are exclusively marine in nature with no representative in freshwater bodies

2. Members of phylum porifera are single celled, biradial and dioecious

3. Sponges are considered as hermaphrodite as sexes are separate and fertilization is external

4. In sponges, sexual reproduction is by gametes and asexual reproduction is with the help of fragmentation.
explanation: Members of phylum porifera are commonly known as sponges. They are generally marine but some species also present in freshwater such as fresh water sponge (Spongilla) and mostly asymmetrical animals (having no symmetry). These are primitive multicellular animals and have cellular level of organisation. Sexes are not separate (hermaphrodite, Monoecious), i.e., eggs and sperms are produced by the same individual while dioecious are those animals which have separate sexes. Sponges reproduce asexually by fragmentation and sexually by formation of gametes. Fertilisation is internal and takes place within the body of animal (Reference  : NCERT Biology class 11; Page 49; Paragraph No. 1)

explanation: Cnidarians exhibit only two basic body forms called polyp and medusa. The former is a sessile and cylindrical form like Hydra, Adamsia, etc. whereas, the latter is umbrella-shaped and free-swimming like Aurelia or jelly fish. Those cnidarians which exist in both forms exhibit alternation of generation (Metagenesis), i.e., polyps produce medusae asexually and medusae form the polyps sexually (e.g., Obelia). Jelly fish does not exhibit polymorphism. It only exists in medusa form (Reference  : NCERT Biology class 11; Page 50; Paragraph No. 1)

explanation: This is the largest phylum of Animalia which includes insects. Over two-thirds of all named species on earth are arthropods. They have organ-system level of organisation. They are bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic (three germ layers are present such as ectoderm, endoderm and mesoderm), segmented and coelomate (having a true coelom) animals. They have open circulatory system in which blood is not confined to blood vessels and malpighian tubules are major excretory organs to remove nitrogenous wastes outside the body (Reference  : NCERT Biology class 11; Page 53; Paragraph No. 1)

explanation: In arthropods, Respiratory organs are gills, book gills, book lungs or tracheal system which are used by different class of phylum arthropoda. Sensory organs like antennae, eyes (compound and simple), statocysts or balancing organs are present in all arthropods. Excretion takes place through malpighian tubules. answer: If both Assertion and Reason are false.
explanation:
Hemichordates have three body regions i.e. proboscis region, neck and trunk and excretion is done by proboscis glands that are present in probosics region While metanephridia are excretory organs which have a ciliated funnel nephrostome that collects wastes from cells and pulls into metanephridia (Reference  : NCERT Biology class 11; Page 54; Paragraph No. 4)
A survey of animal kingdom presents a variety of excretory structures. In most of the invertebrates, these structures are simple tubular forms whereas vertebrates have complex tubular organs called kidneys. Some of these structures are mentioned here. Protonephridia or flame cells are the excretory structures in Platyhelminthes (Flatworms, e.g., Planaria), rotifers, some annelids and the cephalochordate – Amphioxus. Protonephridia are primarily concerned with ionic and fluid volume regulation, i.e., osmoregulation.

explanation:

question:
Consider these statements and choose the correct option.

1. Sponges are mostly symmetrical.

2. When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called bilateral symmetry.

3. Symmetry in which the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane, exhibit radial symmetry.

4. Annelids possess radial symmetry.
explanation:
Animals can be categorised on the basis of their symmetry. Sponges are mostly asymmetrical, i.e., any plane that passes through the centre does not divide them into equal halves. When any plane passing through the central axis of the body divides the organism into two identical halves, it is called radial symmetry.
Coelenterates, ctenophores and echinoderms have this kind of body plan. Animals like annelids, arthropods, etc., where the body can be divided into identical left and right halves in only one plane, exhibit bilateral symmetry.

question: Match The Following
explanation:
Sexual reproduction takes place through the fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be
flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile)
but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called
isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of
Eudorina is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, nonmotile
(static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed
oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 30; Paragraph No. 5)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Algae

question: Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the______.

topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Algae

question: At least a half of the total carbon dioxide fixation on earth is carried out by ______ through photosynthesis.

question: Types of chloroplasts found in different species of green Algae are
explanation:
Different shapes of chloroplasts are seen in different species of green algae
Chloroplasts come in different shapes- discoid, cup-shaped, girdle shaped, reticulate, plate-like, ribbon-shaped, or even spiral. Cup-shaped chloroplasts are found in organisms such as Chlamydomonas, a green alga. Girdle shaped chloroplasts are found in organisms such as the filamentous green algae Ulothrix. Reticulate chloroplasts are found in the free-living, filamentous green algae Oedogonium. Higher plants have oval, discoid shaped chloroplasts.

explanation:

question: All are archegoniate except -
explanation:
Archegonia is a multicellular, flask-shaped, egg-producing organ occurring in mosses, liverworts, ferns, and most gymnosperms. The plant history of archegoniate plants is zygote-dominant between the formation of zygote and the onset of meiosis. As the archegonium matures the neck-canal cells, located above the egg, disappear thus producing a passage for the entry of the sperm. The archegoniate lineage, therefore, includes the bryophytes, pteridophytes, and gymnosperms. In gymnosperms, megasporangium develops into a multicellular female
gametophyte that bears two or more archegonia or
female sex organs. The multicellular female gametophyte
is also retained within megasporangium. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 39; Paragraph No. 1)

question:
Which one is CORRECT about male and female gametophytes? 

(i)In bryophytes and pteridophytes they have independent free-living existence 

(ii)In gymnosperms and angiosperms they have no independent free-living existence 

(iii)In bryophytes, pteridophytes and angiosperms they have free-living life
explanation: Different plant groups exhibit different life cycle. There are two alternating phases in life cycle of every plant. The gametophyte (haploid) and the sporophyte (diploid). When the haploid gametophyte is dominant, photosynthetic and free living/independant  the  it is the haplontic life cycle which is found in algae Volvox, Spirogyra  and some species of Chlaydomonas exhibit this pattern. When the diploid sporophyte is dominant, photosynthetic and independant  it is called diplontic life cycle which is exhibited an alga, Fucus sp., and all seed bearing plants i.e., gymnosperms and angiosperms. Bryophytes and pteridophytes, interestingly, exhibit an intermediate condition (Haplo-diplontic) where both phases are multicellular but they differ in dominant phases. In Bryophytes the haploid gametophyte is dominant, photosynthetic and free living/independant  and the diploid sporophyte is short lived and multicellular. In pteridophytes, the diploid sporophyte dominant, photosynthetic and independant  which alternates with photosynthetic and independant but short lived gametophyte. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 42)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Gymnosperms

question: Monocotyledons and dicotyledons are
explanation:
Angiosperms are divided into two classes which are monocotyledons and dicotyledons. The dicotyledons are
characterised by seeds having two cotyledons, reticulate venations in
leaves, and tetramerous or pentamerous flowers, i.e., having four or five
members in each floral whorls. The monocotyledons on the other hand
are characterised by single cotyledonous seeds, parallel venation in
leaves, and trimerous flowers having three members in each floral whorls. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 40; Paragraph No. 1)

question: Which of the following is responsible for peat formation? [AIPMT 2014]
explanation:
Among the bryophytes, Sphagnum accounts by far the most important place economically. It is popularly called bog moss or peat moss. It is perennial and its growth continues year after year. Older portions undergo death but do not decompose due to the secretion of acid that accounts for the antibacterial and antifungal actions. The increasing mass of dead remains accumulates year after year and forms a compact dark-colored mass rich in carbon which is called peat. Peat is used as fuel. Paraffin, acetic acid, peat tar, and ammonia are formed as byproducts of peat obtained for industrial uses. Species of Sphagnum, a moss, provide peat that have long been used as
fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because
of their capacity to hold water.(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 35; Paragraph No. 3)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Previous Year Questions 1

question:

Lactobacillus, nostoc, chara, Nitrosomonas,Nitrobacter, streptomyces, saccharomyces,Trypanosoma, Porphyra, Wolffia 

[AIPMT Mains 2012]
explanation: Autotrophic nutrition involves the manufacture of organic materials from inorganic raw materials with the help of energy obtained from outside sources. It is of two types – chemosynthesis and photosynthesis. The organisms which can manufacture their organic food from inorganic raw materials with the help of energy derived from exergonic chemical reactions are called chemoautotrophs. Nitrosomonas and Nitrobacter are chemoautotrophic nitrifying bacteria. Those organisms that can manufacture organic compounds from inorganic raw materials with the help of solar energy in the presence of photosynthetic pigments are called photoautotrophs. E.g., Nostoc, Chara, Porphyra and Wolffia.

question: Spore dissemination in some liverworts is aided by [AIPMT 2007]
explanation: An elater is a cell (or structure attached to a cell) that is hygroscopic and therefore will change shape in response to changes in moisture in the environment. Elaters come in a variety of forms but are always associated with plant spores. In plants that do not have seeds, they function in dispersing the spores to a new location. In the liverworts, elaters are cells that develop in the sporophyte alongside the spores. They are complete cells, usually with helcial thickenings at maturity that respond to moisture content. In most liverworts, the elaters are unattached, but in some leafy species (such as Frullania) a few elaters will remain attached to the inside of the sporangium (spore capsule). The elaters by hygroscopic movement help in spore dispersal.

question:
Diversification in plant life appeared 
[AIPMT 2005]
answer: Due to long periods of evolutionary changes
explanation: Diversification in plant life appeared due to long periods of evolutionary changes. Algae and bryophytes have a thalloid plant body with no differentiation into roots, stems, and leaves. They had no vascular tissues but later in pteridophytes, vascular tissues (xylem and phloem) developed, and the plant body became differentiated into root, stem, and leaves. But the vascular tissues lack vessels and companion cells and they reproduce by spores. In gymnosperms, seed habits developed but the seeds are not enclosed inside the fruit. In angiosperms vessels and companions, cells are present, flowers are present and seeds are enclosed inside fruits. Thus the path of evolution is from algae to bryophytes to pteridophytes to gymnosperms and finally to angiosperm.

question:

 [AIPMT 1999]

question: Sexual reproduction is absent in [AIPMT 1995]
explanation:
Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. question: In ulothrix/spirogyra, reduction division (meiosis) occurs at the time of [AIPMT 1993]
explanation: In Ulothrix/Spirogyra reduction division (meiosis) occurs at the time of zygospore formation. The plant body of Ulothrix and Spirogyra is gametophytic (haploid), they produce zoogametes (n) which fuses to form zygospores. Sporophytic generation is represented only by the one-celled zygote. There are no free-living sporophytes. Meiosis in the zygote results in the formation of haploid spores. The haploid spores divide mitotically and form the gametophyte. The dominant, photosynthetic phase in such plants is the free-living gametophyte. This kind of life cycle is termed as haplontic. Many algae such as Volvox, Spirogyra and some species of Chlamydomonas represent this pattern. (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 42; Paragraph No. 2)

In angiosperms the correct sequence of events in formation of female gametophyte in the ovule is : 
 (A) 3 successive free nuclear divisions functional megaspore. 
 (B) Degeneration of 3 megaspores. 
 (C) Meiotic division in megaspore mother cell.

 (E) Formation of wall resulting in seven celled embryosac. 
 Choose the correct answer from the options given below : [ NEET 2023]

The correct sequence of events for the formation of the female gametophyte in the ovule in angiosperms is:

Meiotic division in the megaspore mother cell (C)

question: Meiosis in Dryopteris takes place during [1997]
explanation:
Bryophytes and pteridophytes, interestingly, exhibit an intermediate condition (Haplo-diplontic); both phases are multicellular. However, they differ in their dominant phases.A dominant, independent, photosynthetic, thalloid or erect phase is represented by a haploid gametophyte and it alternates with the short- lived multicelluler sporophyte totally or partially dependent on the gametophyte for its anchorage and nutrition. All bryophytes represent this pattern. The diploid sporophyte is represented by a dominant, independent, photosynthetic, vascular plant body. It alternates with multicellular, saprophytic/autotrophic, independent but short-lived haploid gametophyte. Such a pattern is known as haplo-diplontic life cycle. All pteridophytes exhibit this pattern and Dryopteris is a fern(pteridophyte)
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 43; Paragraph No. 2) (Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 42; figure 3,7(c))

question:
Consider the following statements?
i. In plants, both haploid and diploid cells can divide by mitosis.

ii. The haploid plant body produces gametes by mitosis.

iii. Following fertilisation the zygote divides by mitosis to produce a diploid sporophytic plant body.

iv. Haploid spores are produced by sporophyte by meiosis.

How many of the above statements are false?
explanation:
Statements ii and iv are false. 
In plants, both haploid and diploid cells can divide by mitosis. This ability leads to the formation of different plant bodies - haploid and diploid. The haploid plant body produces gametes by mitosis. This plant body represents a gametophyte. Following fertilisation the zygote also divides by mitosis to produce a diploid sporophytic plant body. Haploid spores are produced by this plant body by meiosis. These in turn, divide by mitosis to form a haploid plant body once again. Thus, during the life cycle of any sexually reproducing plant, there is an alternation of generations between gamete producing haploid gametophyte and spore producing diploid sporophyte.
(Reference  : NCERT Biology Class 11; Page 42)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Assertion Reason and Multiple statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements about artificial classification systems:
i. They were based mainly on vegetative characters or on the androecium structure.

ii. They separated the closely related species.

iii. Gave more weightage to vegetative characteristics than sexual characteristics.

iv. This system is not acceptable since we know that often the vegetative characters are more easily affected by the environment.

Which of the above statements are true?
explanation:
The earliest systems of classification used only gross superficial morphological characters
such as habit, colour, number and shape of leaves, etc. They were based mainly on
vegetative characters or on the androecium structure (system given by Linnaeus). Such
systems were artificial; they separated the closely related species since they were based on
a few characteristics. Also, the artificial systems gave equal weightage to vegetative and
sexual characteristics; this is not acceptable since we know that often the vegetative
characters are more easily affected by environment.
(ref. NCERT biology class 11, page 29)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Assertion Reason and Multiple statement Questions

question: Match the following
answer: Ulothrix - Flagellated and similar in size, Spirogyra -  Non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size, Eudorina - Two gametes dissimilar in size, Volvox- One large non motile (static) female gamete and a smaller motile male gamete
explanation:
Sexual reproduction in algae takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can
be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in
size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes
dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one
large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed
oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.
(ref. NCERT biology class 11, page 30)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Assertion Reason and Multiple statement Questions
option_a: Ulothrix, Flagellated and similar in size
option_b: Spirogyra, Non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size
option_c: Eudorina, Two gametes dissimilar in size
option_d: Volvox, One large non motile (static) female gamete and a smaller motile male gamete

question:
Consider the following statements about Phaeophyceae:
i. Primarily in marine habitats.

ii. Branched forms as represented by kelps may reach a height of 100 metres.

iii. They possess chlorophyll a and c.

iv. They vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of chlorophyll a and c.

v. Asexual reproduction in most brown algae is by biflagellate zoospores.

All of them statements are true except?
explanation:
The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats. They
show great variation in size and form. They range from simple branched, filamentous forms
(Ectocarpus) to profusely branched forms as represented by kelps, which may reach a
height of 100 metres. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls.
They vary in colour from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount
of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them.
Asexual reproduction in most brown algae is by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped
and have two unequal laterally attached flagella.
(ref. NCERT biology class 11; page 32,33)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Assertion Reason and Multiple statement Questions

question:
Consider the following statements about reproduction in Angiosperms:
i. Each ovule has a megaspore mother cell that undergoes meiosis to form four haploid megaspores. One of them degenerates and three fuse to produce the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).

ii. Each embryo-sac has a three-celled egg apparatus consisting of one egg cell and two polar nuclei.

iii. The pollen tubes enter the embryo-sac where one male gamete is discharged.

iv. The synergids and antipodals provide nourishment to the developing embryo.

Which of the above statements are true?
explanation:
Each ovule has a megaspore mother cell that undergoes meiosis to form four haploid
megaspores. Three of them degenerate and one divide to form the embryo sac. Each
embryo-sac has a three-celled egg apparatus – one egg cell and two synergids, three
antipodal cells and two polar nuclei. The polar nuclei eventually fuse to produce a diploid
secondary nucleus.
The pollen grains germinate on the stigma and the resulting pollen tubes grow through the
tissues of stigma and style and reach the ovule. The pollen tubes enter the embryo-sac
where two male gametes are discharged. One of the male gametes fuses with the egg cell
(syngamy) to form a zygote. The other male gamete fuses with the diploid secondary
nucleus to produce the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN). Because of the
occurrence of two fusions i.e., syngamy and triple fusion, this event is termed as double
fertilisation, an event unique to angiosperms. The zygote develops into an embryo (with one
or two cotyledons) and the PEN develops into endosperm which provides nourishment
to the developing embryo. The synergids and antipodals degenerate after fertilisation.
(ref. NCERT biology class 11; page 40,41)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:

Y: The diploid sporophyte is represented by a dominant, independent, photosynthetic, vascular plant body. It alternates with multicellular, saprophytic/autotrophic,independent but short-lived haploid gametophyte.

Z: The diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant. The gametophytic phase is represented by the single to few-celled haploid gametophyte.

answer: Plant Z maybe a gymnosperm or angiosperm.
explanation:
A dominant, independent, photosynthetic, thalloid or erect phase is represented by a haploid gametophyte and it alternates with the short- lived multicellular sporophyte totally or partially dependent on the gametophyte for its anchorage and nutrition. All bryophytes represent this pattern. The diploid sporophyte is represented by a dominant, independent, photosynthetic, vascular plant body. It alternates with multicellular, saprophytic/autotrophic, independent but short-lived haploid gametophyte. All pteridophytes exhibit this pattern. The diploid sporophyte is the dominant, photosynthetic, independent phase of the plant. The gametophytic phase is represented by the single to few-celled haploid gametophyte. All seed bearing plants i.eGymnosperms and angiosperms, follow this pattern.
(ref. NCERT biology class 11; page 42,43)

question:
Consider the following life cycle of a plant X:

The sporangia produce spores by meiosis in spore mother cells. The spores germinate to give rise to inconspicuous photosynthetic thalloid gametophytes called prothallus. The gametophytes bear male and female sex organs called antheridia and
archegonia, respectively. Fusion of male gamete with the egg present in the archegonium results in the formation of zygote. The female gametophytes in these plants are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods. The development
of the zygotes into young embryos takes place within the female gametophytes.

Plant X most probably belongs to:
explanation:
The sporophytes bear sporangia that are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls. In some cases sporophylls may form distinct compact structures called strobili or cones (Selaginella, Equisetum). The sporangia produce spores by meiosis in spore mother cells. The spores germinate to give rise to inconspicuous, small but multicellular,free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophytes called prothallus. The gametophytes bear male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia, respectively. Water is required for transfer of antherozoids – the male gametes released from the antheridia, to the mouth of archegonium. Fusion of male gamete with the egg present in the archegonium results in the formation of zygote. The development of the zygotes into young embryos takes place within the female gametophytes. This event is a precursor to the seed habit considered an important step in evolution.
(ref. NCERT biology class 11; page 37,38)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

question:
Consider the following life cycle of a plant X:

It produces haploid microspores and megaspores. The megaspore mother cell is differentiated from one of the cells of the nucellus. The nucellus is protected by envelopes and the composite structure is called an ovule. The pollen grain is released
from the microsporangium. They come in contact with the opening of the ovules borne on megasporophylls. Following fertilisation, zygote develops into an embryo and the ovules into seeds.

Plant X most probably belongs to:
explanation:
The gymnosperms are heterosporous; they produce haploid microspores and megaspores.The two kinds of spores are produced within sporangia that are borne on sporophylls which are arranged spirally along an axis to form lax or compact strobili or cones. The strobili bearing microsporophylls and microsporangia are called microsporangiate or male strobili. The development of pollen grains take place within the microsporangia. The cones bearing megasporophylls with ovules or megasporangia are called macrosporangiate or female strobili.The megaspore mother cell is differentiated from one of the cells of the nucellus. The nucellus is protected by envelopes and the composite structure is called an ovule. The ovules are borne on megasporophylls which may be clustered to form the female cones. The megaspore mother cell divides meiotically to form four megaspores. One of the megaspores enclosed within the megasporangium develops into a multicellular female gametophyte that bears two or more archegonia or female sex organs. The pollen grain is released from the microsporangium. They are carried in air currents and come in contact with the opening of the ovules borne on megasporophylls. The pollen tube carrying the male gametes grows towards archegonia in the ovules and discharge their contents near the mouth of the archegonia. Following fertilisation, zygote develops into an embryo and the ovules into seeds. These seeds are not covered.
(ref. NCERT biology class 11; page 38,39)
topic_name: Diversity In Living World >> Plant Kingdom >> Indepth questions (Syllabus reduction)

This phenomenon of two fusions is called double fertilisation and is unique to angiosperms.

question:
Which of the following techniques serve the purpose of early diagnosis?
 1)Recombinant DNA technology

2) PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction

3) Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA)

4) Blood and Urine analysis
explanation: R-DNA technology: Recombinant DNA technology, joining together of DNA molecules from two different species that are inserted into a host organism to produce new genetic combinations. It can provide precise diagnostic information about genetic diseases. PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) involves amplification of the nucleic acid in the pathogen allowing us to detect the pathogen at very low concentration. PCR used to detect HIV in suspected AIDS patients and to detect gene mutations in suspected cancer patients. Using the conventional method of diagnosis(serum, urine analysis, etc.) early detection of disease is not possible as the markers for most diseases appear late. Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay (ELISA): The basic principle of ELISA is antigen-antibody reactions. ELISA can diagnose infections by detecting the presence of antigens (proteins of the pathogen) in the patient serum or by detecting the antibodies produced against the pathogen. So, the correct option is '(i), (ii) and (iii)'. Blood and Urine analysis are useful in diagnosis of a disease after the disease has progressed and presents with visible symptoms.
topic_name: Biotechnology and Its Applications >> Biotechnology And Its Applications >> Molecular Diagnosis

question: In Bt cotton, the Bt toxin present in plant tissue as protoxin is converted into active toxin due to [AIPMT 2015 Cancelled]
answer: Alkaline pH of the insect gut.
explanation: Soil bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis produces proteins that kill certain insects like lepidopterans (tobacco budworm, armyworm), coleopterans (beetles) and dipterans (flies, mosquitoes). B. thuringiensis forms some protein crystals. These crystals contain a toxic insecticidal protein. This toxin does not kill the Bacillus(bacterium) because it exists as inactive protoxins in them. The activated toxin binds to the surface of midgut epithelial cells and create pores that cause swelling and lysis and finally cause death of the insect.

This new variety of Basmati had actually been derived from Indian farmers’ varieties. Indian Basmati was crossed with semi-dwarf varieties and claimed as an invention or a novelty. It caused a brief diplomatic crisis between India and United States with India threatening to take the matter to WTO (World Trade Organisation) as a violation of TRIPS (Trade Related Aspects of Intellectual Property Rights). Both voluntarily and due to review decisions by United States patent office, Rice Tec lost most of the claims of the patent.
