question: Select incorrect statement, regarding chemical structure of insulin. [ NEET 2023(Phase 2)]
answer:
(1) Mature insulin molecule consists of three 
polypeptide chains-A, B and C.
explanation:
The chemical structure of insulin consists of two polypeptide chains, not three. The two chains are referred to as the A chain and the B chain. The A chain contains 21 amino acids, while the B chain contains 30 amino acids. These two chains are held together by disulfide bridges.

The correct structure of mature insulin is a dimer, composed of an A chain and a B chain connected by disulfide bridges. The C-peptide, which is derived from the precursor molecule proinsulin, is removed during the processing of proinsulin to form mature insulin. Therefore, statement 3 is also correct.

So, the incorrect statement is 1: "Mature insulin molecule consists of three polypeptide chains - A, B and C."
topic_name: Biotechnology and Its Applications >> Biotechnology And Its Applications >> Previous Year Questions 2

question:
Consider the following statements regarding genetically modified organisms (GMOs): 

(i) E. coli expressing human insulin is an example of a GMO

(ii) Wheat varieties developed by interbreeding to have high crop yield can be considered a GMO

(iii) Bacteria with manipulated genes for overexpression of a bacterial metabolite

(iv) The variety of rice enriched with Vitamin A is an example of a GMO

Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?
explanation: Genetically modified organisms (GMOs) are those organisms that have their genes manipulated by recombinant DNA technology to be used for human use. E. coli has been used as a microbial factory for the production of insulin, a human hormone, using the techniques of RDT. Hence, it is classified as a GMO. Similarly, RDT techniques have been applied to genetically modify bacterial and other microbial species such that they produce a specific metabolite at a significantly higher level than in wild type bacteria. Such bacteria (and other such organisms), hence, are also referred to as GMOs. Crop varieties obtained by interbreeding are not termed as GMOs because the genetic changes involved are natural that can also introduce undesired features to the resultant crop variety. Only those crop varieties are called GMOs that have been genetically manipulated/modified by human interference using the principles of RDT for the manifestation of a specific set of phenotypes or features, e.g. increased nutritional value, higher yields, etc. All wild type rice varieties do not contain Vitamin A. Some varieties have been genetically modified to produce Vitamin A. These rice varities are characterized by their golden color and hence are called golden rice.

Bt cotton is a genetically modified crop that expresses the Bt protein from a bacteria. This protein is toxic to certain pests and imparts pest resistance to cotton crop. This is also an example of how prokaryotic genes can be expressed in eukaryotic cells.  Since plants are eukaryotes, their cellular machinery is more complex than that of bacteria. Hence, simple bacterial plasmids cannot be used as cloning vectors in plants. Ti plasmid from Agrobacterium tumefaciens is the preferred cloning vector for plants and it can be used to express human genes in plants too.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding RNAi in plants: 

(i) RNAi is a natural phenomenon that occurs in all plant cells.

(ii) RNAi occurs only in specific plants that have been genetically modified to perform RNAi.

(iii) Tobacco plants were genetically modified by dsRNA to work against nematode infections.

(iv) Tobacco plants were genetically modified by nematode genes to induce RNAi against them.

Which of the above statements is/are CORRECT?
explanation: RNA interference (RNAi) is used by eukaryotic cells as a technique for genetic regulation and cellular defense. SInce plants are eukaryotic, they also naturally use RNAi for gene expression regulation. In order to increase resistance of tobacco plants against a specific nematode, Meloidegyne incognitia, nematode-specific genes were introduced in the plant genome using Ti plasmid as cloning vector. The introduction of DNA was such that it produced both sense and anti-sense RNA in the host cells. These two RNAs being complementary to each other formed a double stranded (dsRNA) that initiated RNAi and thus, silenced the specific mRNA.of the nematode. This eventually enabled the plant to stave off nematode infection.

This eventually leads to blocking of expression of pest RNA leading to its death.

(iii) Insulin from cattle and pigs can be utilized to manage diabetes in human individuals

(iv) Some strains of E. coli naturally synthesize insulin, hence they are used as primary source of insulin for therapeutics

Which of the above statements is/are CORRECT?
explanation: Insulin is an endocrine hormone produced in the pancreas to regulate the levels of blood sugar in the body. Diabetic patients do not have enough insulin to regulate their blood sugar levels, hence they often require insulin from external sources. Earlier, insulin extracted from slaughtered pigs and cattle was utilized to manage diabetes. However, after the inception of rDNA technology, E. coli was genetically modified to produce the different peptide chains of human insulin, which was then used for diabetic patients. E. coli is a prokaryote and lacks the ability to naturally synthesize human proteins and peptides such as insulin.
topic_name: Biotechnology and Its Applications >> Biotechnology And Its Applications >> Assertion Reason and Mutliple statement questions

question:
Assertion: Recombinant E. coli is capable of synthesizing insulin in its mature form

Reason: Genes coding for the insulin peptide chains were inserted in E. coli plasmids
explanation: E. coli is not capable of producing insulin in its mature form. Insulin is synthesized as prohormone consisting of an extra peptide chain known as the C peptide. To form mature, functional insulin, C peptide is cleaved from the prohormone and the A and B peptide chains are linked via disulphide linkages. In order to synthesize insulin in E. coli, the genes coding for the A and B peptide are separately inserted into the E. coli plasmid vectors. The A and B peptide chains are extracted after expression and linked via sulphide bonds to form human insulin.

Which of the above statements is/are INCORRECT?
explanation: Insulin is synthesized as an inactive prohormone in all mammals consisting of an extra 'C peptide' in between the A and B polypeptide chains. In order to produce mature and functional insulin, the C peptide is cleaved and the A and B chains are linked via disulphide linkages. Eli Lilly was the first company to obtain human recombinant insulin. It was achieved by expressing the DNA sequences of A and B chains separately in E. coli plasmids and extracting them. After extraction, the poypeptide chains were linked via sulphide bonds to form human recombinant insulin.

Eli Lilly was the first company to produce and commercialize recombinant human insulin. However, it is impossible to obtain mature insulin from E. coli since the bacteria does not have the cellular machinery to cleave and then link two polypeptide chains together. Instead, Eli Lilly were able to obtain recombinant A and B polypeptide chains of insulin expressed separately in E. coli and then combined them via chemical means by sulphide bonds.

Which of the above statements is/are CORRECT?
explanation: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) and enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) both are examples of molecular diagnostic techniques since they detect diseases using molecular interaction. PCR and ELISA both can be used for detection of infections. PCR enables the replication of a gene of interest into a million copies in in vitro conditions. Whereas ELISA is based on antibody-antigen interactions and detects pathogenic antigens (proteins, etc.) or other antibodies produced in response to the pathogen.

question:
Assertion: PCR can be utilized to detect genetic disorders

Reason: PCR utilizes DNA polymerase and a pair of specific primers to create copies of a gene of interest
answer: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
explanation: PCR is a molecular technique to create multiple copies of a gene/DNA of interest. It achieves it by using a set of specific primers that bind to the region of interest via complementary base pairing. The primer is then extended along the length of the region of interest by DNA polymerase and dNTPs. Thus, one molecule is copied to two molecules at the end of one PCR cycle. In this way, millions of copies of the gene of interest can be created over a few cycles. PCR is used to detect the presence of pathogenic DNA in samples.Genetic disorders are those wherein genes are mutated/deleted leading to a loss/reduction of function. Such genes can be detected by PCR because of its amplification potential.

Both autoradiograhy and PCR can be used to detect mutations in genes. PCR is a DNA-based technique and hence cannot be used to detect pathogenic proteins. ELISA can only detect pathogenic proteins since it is based on the interaction of antibodies with antigens.

question:
Consider the following statements:

(i) Tissue culture enables the growth of healthy plant from diseased plant

(ii) Protoplasts are single plant cells with all cell structures that can be grown to give rise to whole plant

(iii) It is not possible to fuse the characteristics of two different species using plant tissue culture

(iv) Somatic hybrids are plants obtained after fusion of two different protoplasts and subsequent growth in test tube

Which of the above statements is/are CORRECT?
explanation: Tissue culture can be used to recover healthy plants from diseased plants. This is achieved by culturing and growing the apical or axillary meristem of the plant that does not infected by a pathogen e.g. virus. Protoplasts are single plant cells whose cell wall has been digested, in other words, they are plant cells with only one layer of plasma membrane. It is possible to fuse the characteristics of two different plant species using tissue culture. This is achieved by a technique called as somatic hybridization, wherein protoplasts from two different varieties or species of crops can be fused and grown in lab conditions to form a hybrid plant. These hybrid plants are referred to as somatic hybrids. Pomato is one of the most prominent example of somatic hybridization wherein protoplasts from tomato and potato were fused to generate pomato.
topic_name: Biotechnology and Its Applications >> Biotechnology And Its Applications >> Assertion Reason and Mutliple statement questions

Somatic hybridization involves the fusion of protoplasts, single plant cells without a cell wall, to yield a hybrid protoplast which is grown into a hybrid plant.
